eyebrow: The Human Body · 人體探索
lead_en: Big ideas about how your body works, read in English and explored with 3D models you can turn, and with measurements you take on yourself.
lead_zh: 用英文讀懂身體運作的大道理，用可以親手旋轉的 3D 模型看懂，再用自己的身體量一量。

intro.en: Every lesson starts with a question about your own body. A 3D model lets you turn, take apart, and look inside the answer, and an English reading explains it, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 每一課都從一個關於自己身體的問題開始：先用 3D 模型轉一轉、拆一拆、看進裡面，找出答案；再讀一篇英文短文把道理講清楚，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: Each lesson also has you measure something on yourself, plus vocabulary, comprehension questions, a short quiz, and a classroom activity. These lessons are for learning, not medical advice.
intro.zh: 每一課也會請你在自己身上量一量、數一數，並附生字、閱讀理解、小測驗和課堂活動。本系列是教育用途，不是醫療建議。

lessons.title: Why Do We Need a Skeleton?
lessons.blurb_en: 206 bones hold you up, protect your organs, and even make your blood. Take a 3D skeleton apart bone by bone.
lessons.blurb_zh: 206 塊骨頭撐起身體、保護內臟，還會製造血液；3D 骨架可以一塊塊拆開看。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your skeleton is a living frame. It holds you up, protects your organs, gives your muscles something to pull on, and makes new blood cells every day.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 骨骼是活的支架：撐起身體、保護內臟、讓肌肉有地方施力，每天還製造新的血球。

lab.how_en: Every bone in this model has its real shape, built from scans of a real adult. Drag to turn it and scroll or pinch to zoom. Tap any bone to learn its name, tap a body part to look at it on its own, or tap one of the five jobs to see which bones do it. The slider takes the whole skeleton apart.
lab.how_zh: 模型裡每一塊骨頭都是真實的形狀，來自真人的掃描資料。拖曳可以旋轉、滾輪或雙指可以縮放。點任何一塊骨頭，看它叫什麼名字；點身體部位，單獨看那一區；點五大功能，看哪些骨頭在做這件事。拖動滑桿，可以把整副骨架拆開。

legend.en: Gold glow: the bone you tapped
legend.zh: 金色發光：你點選的骨頭

legend.en: Red (Make blood): bones with red marrow in adults
legend.zh: 紅色（造血）：成人有紅骨髓的骨頭

legend.en: Soft shapes (Protect): brain, heart, lungs, and spinal cord, drawn simply to show where they sit
legend.zh: 半透明形狀（保護）：腦、心臟、肺、脊髓，只是示意位置的簡化形狀

lab.scale_en: The bones are real: 199 of the 206, in their true shapes and sizes. The data set leaves out the coccyx (tailbone) and the six tiny bones inside the ears. The organs are simple shapes, not real anatomy.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是真實的：206 塊中的 199 塊，形狀與大小都是真的；資料裡少了尾骨和耳朵裡的六塊聽小骨。器官只是簡單的示意形狀，不是真實解剖。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向。

paras: Imagine for a moment that every bone in your body disappeared. You could not stand, sit up, or even hold up your head. You would slump to the floor like a pile of laundry. Some animals, such as jellyfish and octopuses, get along fine without bones, but they live in water, which helps hold them up. On land, a large animal needs a strong frame inside it. Your frame is your skeleton: about 206 bones, from the tiny ones deep inside your ears to the long thighbone in each leg.

The first job of the skeleton is support. Your spine, a stack of 24 small bones called vertebrae resting on a larger bone called the sacrum, holds up your head and body like the pole of a tent. Your pelvis passes that weight to your legs, and your legs carry it down to your feet. The second job is protection. Your skull is a hard helmet around your brain. Your ribs form a cage around your heart and lungs, and your vertebrae make a bony tunnel that shields your spinal cord, the bundle of nerves that carries messages between your brain and the rest of your body.

The third job is movement. Bones cannot move by themselves, but muscles are attached to them, and when a muscle gets shorter, it pulls on a bone. The places where two bones meet are called joints. Some joints, like your elbow and knee, bend in one direction, like a door on its hinges. Others, like your shoulder and hip, are ball-and-socket joints that let you swing an arm or a leg in a circle. Your hands are especially clever. Each one has 27 bones, which is why you can write, button a shirt, and pick up a peanut with chopsticks.

The fourth and fifth jobs are hidden inside. Many bones are filled with a soft tissue called marrow. Red marrow, which in adults is found mostly in flat bones such as the ribs, hips, and vertebrae, makes new blood cells, hundreds of billions of them every day. They include red blood cells that carry oxygen, white blood cells that fight germs, and platelets that help a cut stop bleeding. Bones also store minerals, especially calcium. When your heart and nerves need more calcium than your food provides, your bones release some into your blood.

It is easy to think of bones as dead, dry sticks, like the skeleton that hangs in a science classroom. But the bones inside you are alive. They have blood vessels and nerves, which is one reason a broken bone hurts so much, and they are always rebuilding themselves. Some cells break down old bone while others build new bone, so over about ten years, most of an adult's skeleton is replaced. A newborn baby has around 300 bones and bony parts. As a child grows, many of them join together, which is why an adult has only about 206.

Because bone is alive, it responds to how you treat it. When you run, jump, and play, the extra force tells your bones to grow thicker and stronger. Astronauts who spend months in space, where their bones carry almost no weight, lose bone and must exercise every day to slow the loss. Your bones reach their greatest strength by your late twenties, and much of it is built while you are still in school. So move every day, and eat foods with calcium, such as milk, tofu, small dried fish, and dark green vegetables. Then try this: count the bones in one of your hands.
paras_zh: 想像一下，你身上的每一塊骨頭突然都消失了。你沒辦法站、沒辦法坐起來，連頭都抬不起來，整個人會像一堆換下來的衣服一樣癱在地上。有些動物，像水母和章魚，沒有骨頭也活得好好的，但牠們住在水裡，水會幫忙撐住身體。在陸地上，體型大的動物身體裡需要一副堅固的支架。你的支架就是骨骼：大約 206 塊骨頭，從耳朵深處的小骨頭，到每條腿裡長長的股骨。
骨骼的第一個工作是支撐。你的脊柱由 24 塊叫做椎骨的小骨頭疊成，底下坐在一塊比較大的薦骨上，像帳篷的營柱一樣撐起頭和身體。骨盆把這些重量傳到雙腿，雙腿再一路傳到腳底。第二個工作是保護。頭顱骨是包住大腦的硬安全帽；肋骨圍成一個籠子，保護心臟和肺；椎骨則連成一條骨頭隧道，守護脊髓——那一束在大腦和全身之間傳遞訊息的神經。
第三個工作是運動。骨頭自己不會動，但肌肉附著在骨頭上，肌肉一縮短，就會拉動骨頭。兩塊骨頭相接的地方叫做關節。有些關節，像手肘和膝蓋，只往一個方向彎，就像門繞著鉸鏈開關；有些關節，像肩膀和髖部，是球窩關節，讓你可以把手臂或腿甩成一個圓。你的手特別靈巧：每隻手有 27 塊骨頭，所以你才能寫字、扣扣子，還能用筷子夾起一顆花生。
第四和第五個工作藏在骨頭裡面。許多骨頭裡充滿一種柔軟的組織，叫做骨髓。紅骨髓在成人身上主要位於扁平的骨頭裡，例如肋骨、髖骨和椎骨，它負責製造新的血球，每天多達幾千億個：有運送氧氣的紅血球、對抗病菌的白血球，還有幫助傷口止血的血小板。骨頭也儲存礦物質，特別是鈣。當心臟和神經需要的鈣比食物提供的還多時，骨頭就會釋放一些鈣到血液裡。
我們很容易把骨頭想成死掉的乾柴，就像掛在自然教室裡的那副骨架。但你身體裡的骨頭是活的：它們有血管和神經，這也是骨折會那麼痛的原因之一；而且骨頭一直在重建自己。有些細胞負責拆掉舊骨頭，另一些細胞負責蓋新骨頭，所以大約十年之間，成人的骨骼大部分都會換新。剛出生的嬰兒大約有 300 塊骨頭和骨質部分；孩子長大的過程中，其中許多會癒合在一起，所以成人只剩大約 206 塊。
因為骨頭是活的，它會回應你怎麼對待它。當你跑、跳、玩耍，多出來的力量會告訴骨頭：要長得更粗、更強壯。在太空待上好幾個月的太空人，骨頭幾乎不用承受重量，骨量就會流失，所以他們每天都得運動來減緩流失。骨骼在二十多歲後段達到最強壯的時候，而其中很大一部分是在求學階段打下的基礎。所以每天都要動一動，也要吃含鈣的食物，例如牛奶、豆腐、小魚乾和深綠色蔬菜。然後試試看：數一數你一隻手有幾塊骨頭。
questions: Why can a jellyfish live without bones, when a large land animal cannot?
Name the three parts of the skeleton that protect organs, and say what each one protects.
Why does an adult have fewer bones than a newborn baby?
answers: The jellyfish lives in water, which helps hold its body up. On land, nothing holds a large body up, so it needs a strong frame inside it.
The skull protects the brain, the ribs protect the heart and lungs, and the vertebrae protect the spinal cord.
A newborn has around 300 bones and bony parts, and many of them join together as a child grows, leaving about 206 in an adult.

vocab.ex: The museum has the skeleton of a whale hanging from the ceiling.
vocab.exzh: 博物館的天花板上掛著一副鯨魚的骨骼。

vocab.ex: Four strong legs support the heavy table.
vocab.exzh: 四隻結實的桌腳撐起這張沉重的桌子。

vocab.ex: A helmet protects your head when you ride a bike.
vocab.exzh: 騎腳踏車時，安全帽保護你的頭。

vocab.ex: Each vertebra in your spine has a hole for the spinal cord to pass through.
vocab.exzh: 脊柱裡的每一塊椎骨都有一個洞，讓脊髓穿過。

vocab.ex: Your knee is the largest joint in your body.
vocab.exzh: 膝蓋是你身上最大的關節。

vocab.ex: Doctors can take a little marrow from a healthy person to help a patient with a blood disease.
vocab.exzh: 醫生可以從健康的人身上取一點骨髓，幫助血液疾病的病人。

vocab.ex: Calcium is the mineral that makes bones and teeth hard.
vocab.exzh: 鈣是讓骨頭和牙齒堅硬的礦物質。

vocab.ex: We need to replace the old batteries in the flashlight.
vocab.exzh: 我們需要換掉手電筒裡的舊電池。

quiz.q: About how many bones does an adult have?
Which bones form a cage around the heart and lungs?
What does red marrow do?
options: It pulls on bones to move them
It carries messages from the brain

quiz.q: What is a joint?
options: A place where two bones meet
A muscle that bends the arm
The soft tissue inside a bone
A bone in the middle of the spine

quiz.q: According to the reading, what makes bones grow thicker and stronger?
options: Resting in bed as much as possible
Living in space for a few months

jobs.text_en: The spine, pelvis, and legs carry your weight like the frame of a building.
jobs.text_zh: 脊柱、骨盆和雙腿像建築物的骨架一樣，承受你全身的重量。
jobs.try_en: Stand up straight, then slowly bend forward. Feel your spine curve like a chain.
jobs.try_zh: 站直，再慢慢向前彎腰，感覺脊柱像一條鏈子一節一節彎下來。

jobs.text_en: The skull guards the brain, the ribs guard the heart and lungs, and the spine guards the spinal cord.
jobs.text_zh: 頭顱骨守護大腦，肋骨守護心臟和肺，脊柱守護脊髓。
jobs.try_en: Tap your head gently, then your ribs. Both feel hard because bone is right under the skin.
jobs.try_zh: 輕輕敲一敲頭頂，再敲一敲肋骨：都硬硬的，因為皮膚底下就是骨頭。

jobs.text_en: Muscles pull on bones, and joints let them bend, twist, and turn.
jobs.text_zh: 肌肉拉動骨頭，關節讓骨頭能彎、能扭、能轉。
jobs.try_en: Swing your arm in a circle, then try it with your forearm. Which joint can do it?
jobs.try_zh: 把整隻手臂甩一圈，再只用前臂試試看。哪一個關節做得到？

jobs.text_en: Red marrow inside flat bones makes hundreds of billions of new blood cells every day.
jobs.text_zh: 扁平骨頭裡的紅骨髓，每天製造幾千億個新的血球。
jobs.try_en: Press on your breastbone. Right behind it, marrow is making blood cells as you read this.
jobs.try_zh: 按一按胸骨：就在它裡面，骨髓正在一邊製造血球，一邊讓你讀這句話。

jobs.text_en: Bones are a bank for calcium. When your blood runs low, your bones lend some.
jobs.text_zh: 骨頭是鈣的銀行；血液裡的鈣不夠時，骨頭會借一些出來。
jobs.try_en: List three foods you ate this week that have calcium.
jobs.try_zh: 列出這個星期你吃過的三種含鈣食物。

lessons.jobs_note_en: Tap “See it in 3D” to light up the bones that do each job.
lessons.jobs_note_zh: 點「在模型中看」，3D 骨架就會亮起負責那項工作的骨頭。

counts.note_en: 8 around the brain, 14 in the face
counts.note_zh: 8 塊包住大腦、14 塊組成臉

counts.note_en: 3 in each ear, the smallest in the body (not in the model)
counts.note_zh: 每耳 3 塊，全身最小（模型中沒有）

counts.note_en: In the neck, the only bone that touches no other bone
counts.note_zh: 在脖子，唯一不和其他骨頭相接的骨頭

counts.note_en: 24 vertebrae, the sacrum, and the coccyx
counts.note_zh: 24 塊椎骨，加上薦骨與尾骨

counts.note_en: 12 pairs of ribs and the breastbone
Humerus, radius, and ulna on each side
counts.note_zh: 每邊各有肱骨、橈骨、尺骨

counts.note_en: Each one grows from three bones that join
counts.note_zh: 每塊都由三塊骨頭長在一起

counts.note_en: Femur, kneecap, tibia, and fibula on each side
counts.note_zh: 每邊各有股骨、髕骨、脛骨、腓骨

lessons.counts_note_en: Counts are for a typical adult; some people have an extra small bone or two. Your hands and feet hold 106 bones, more than half of the 206.
lessons.counts_note_zh: 以一般成人計算，有些人會多一兩塊小骨頭。雙手和雙腳加起來就有 106 塊，超過全身 206 塊的一半。

measure.title_en: Count the bones in your own hand
measure.title_zh: 數一數自己手上的骨頭
measure.lead_en: Press the button, and the 3D hand lights up one bone at a time. Follow along on your own hand, pressing each spot as it lights up.
measure.lead_zh: 按下按鈕，3D 模型的手會一塊一塊亮起來。跟著在自己的手上按一按，亮到哪裡就摸到哪裡。

steps.en: Wrist
steps.zh: 手腕
steps.text_en: Press around the base of your hand. You cannot feel all eight, but you can feel them slide when you bend your wrist.
steps.text_zh: 按一按手掌根部。八塊摸不全，但彎手腕時可以感覺到它們在滑動。

steps.en: Palm
steps.zh: 手掌
steps.text_en: Run a finger across the back of your hand. One long bone leads to each finger.
steps.text_zh: 用一根手指劃過手背：每根手指下面都有一根長長的骨頭。

steps.en: Fingers
steps.zh: 手指
steps.text_en: Bend each finger and count the parts between the creases. The thumb has two; the others have three.
steps.text_zh: 彎一彎每根手指，數一數摺痕之間有幾節：拇指兩節，其他手指三節。

myths.myth_en: Bones are dead and dry, like sticks.
myths.myth_zh: 骨頭是死的、乾的，像木棍一樣。
myths.fact_en: Living bones have blood vessels and nerves, and cells inside them are always tearing down old bone and building new bone.
myths.fact_zh: 活的骨頭有血管和神經，裡面的細胞一直在拆掉舊骨頭、蓋新骨頭。

myths.myth_en: Babies have fewer bones than adults.
myths.myth_zh: 嬰兒的骨頭比大人少。
myths.fact_en: It is the other way around. A newborn has around 300 bones and bony parts, and many join together as the child grows.
myths.fact_zh: 剛好相反。新生兒大約有 300 塊骨頭和骨質部分，長大的過程中許多會癒合在一起。

myths.myth_en: Bones are solid all the way through.
myths.myth_zh: 骨頭從外到內都是實心的。
myths.fact_en: Most bones have a hard outer shell and a light, honeycomb-like inside, often with marrow in the spaces. That makes them strong but not too heavy.
myths.fact_zh: 大多數骨頭外層是堅硬的殼，裡面是像蜂巢一樣輕巧的結構，空隙裡常常有骨髓。這樣既堅固又不會太重。

myths.myth_en: Once you are grown, your bones stop changing.
myths.myth_zh: 長大以後，骨頭就不會再改變了。
myths.fact_en: Adult bones keep rebuilding themselves all through life. Exercise makes them stronger, and months without using them, as in space or in a cast, makes them weaker.
myths.fact_zh: 成人的骨頭一輩子都在重建。運動讓它們更強壯；好幾個月不用它們（像在太空，或打石膏的時候）就會變弱。

tricks.title_en: Breakfast at 7, lunch at 12, dinner at 5
tricks.title_zh: 早餐 7 點、午餐 12 點、晚餐 5 點
tricks.body_en: That is how many vertebrae you have in each part of your back: 7 in the neck, 12 in the chest, and 5 in the lower back.
tricks.body_zh: 這就是脊柱各段的椎骨數：頸椎 7 塊、胸椎 12 塊、腰椎 5 塊。

tricks.title_en: More than half in your hands and feet
tricks.body_en: 27 + 27 + 26 + 26 = 106. More than half of your bones are in your hands and feet.
tricks.body_zh: 27 + 27 + 26 + 26 = 106：你全身一半以上的骨頭都在手和腳。

tricks.title_en: The radius is on the thumb side
tricks.body_en: Hold your hand out, thumb up. The radius runs to your thumb and the ulna to your little finger. Turn your palm over, and the radius crosses over the ulna.
tricks.body_zh: 把手伸出去、拇指朝上：橈骨通到拇指、尺骨通到小指。把手掌翻過來，橈骨就會交叉跨到尺骨上面。

tricks.body_en: Femur = thighbone, patella = kneecap, clavicle = collarbone, scapula = shoulder blade, sternum = breastbone. Doctors use the first names; everyone else uses the second.
tricks.body_zh: femur＝thighbone（股骨）、patella＝kneecap（髕骨）、clavicle＝collarbone（鎖骨）、scapula＝shoulder blade（肩胛骨）、sternum＝breastbone（胸骨）。醫生用前面那個名字，一般人用後面那個。

activities.title_en: Why Are Bones Shaped Like Tubes?
activities.title_zh: 骨頭為什麼是管子的形狀？

materials.en: Three sheets of the same printer paper
materials.zh: 三張一樣的影印紙

materials.en: Tape
materials.zh: 膠帶

materials.en: A stack of light books or notebooks
materials.zh: 一疊輕的書或筆記本

steps.en: Fold one sheet into a flat strip, fold one into a square column, and roll one into a round tube. Tape each one so it keeps its shape.
steps.zh: 一張摺成扁平的長條，一張摺成方柱，一張捲成圓管，各用膠帶固定。

steps.en: Stand each one on its end and gently place books on top, one at a time.
steps.zh: 把它們一一立起來，在上面一本一本輕輕放書。

steps.en: Count how many books each shape holds before it bends.
steps.zh: 記錄每種形狀在彎掉之前撐得住幾本書。

steps.en: Ask: the same paper, the same weight. Why does the round tube hold the most? Where in your body are the tube-shaped bones?
steps.zh: 問問自己：同樣的紙、同樣的重量，為什麼圓管撐得最多？你身上哪些骨頭是管子的形狀？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: then turn the 3D model to the legs and arms. The long bones are hollow tubes filled with marrow, strong for their weight like the paper tube.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：做完再把 3D 模型轉到手臂和腿。長骨就是裡面裝著骨髓的空心管，跟紙管一樣，用很少的重量換來很大的強度。

materials.en: A clean chicken drumstick bone (boil it and scrub off the meat)
materials.zh: 一根洗乾淨的雞腿骨（先煮過，把肉刷掉）

materials.en: A jar with a lid, and enough white vinegar to cover the bone
materials.zh: 一個有蓋的罐子，和足夠蓋過骨頭的白醋

materials.en: A second clean bone to compare
materials.zh: 另一根洗乾淨的骨頭，用來對照

steps.en: Try to bend the bones. They are hard and stiff.
steps.zh: 試著把骨頭折彎：它們又硬又直。

steps.en: Put one bone in the jar, cover it with vinegar, and close the lid. Leave the other bone dry.
steps.zh: 把一根骨頭放進罐子，倒醋蓋過，蓋上蓋子；另一根保持乾燥。

steps.en: After three days, pour out the vinegar and add fresh vinegar. Wait about three more days.
steps.zh: 三天後把醋倒掉、換新的醋，再等大約三天。

steps.en: Rinse the bone and try to bend it again. Compare it with the dry bone. What did the vinegar take away?
steps.zh: 把骨頭沖乾淨，再試著折彎，和乾燥的那根比一比。醋帶走了什麼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the vinegar dissolves the calcium, leaving the soft, bendy framework behind. Bones need both: calcium for hardness and the framework for toughness. Wash hands after handling raw chicken.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：醋溶掉了鈣，留下柔軟、可以彎曲的骨架纖維。骨頭兩樣都需要：鈣讓它堅硬，纖維讓它有韌性、不易斷。碰過生雞肉之後要洗手。

culture.body_en: Chinese often talks about bones together with 筋 (jīn), the sinews that tie muscles and bones together. Someone healthy and strong has good 筋骨, and a serious injury is 傷筋動骨, “hurting the sinews and moving the bones.” A common saying, 傷筋動骨一百天, says such an injury takes a hundred days to heal. It is a saying, not a medical rule, but it makes the same point doctors do: bones heal, but slowly.
culture.body_zh: 中文常把骨頭和「筋」（連接肌肉與骨頭的韌帶、肌腱）放在一起講：身體健壯叫「筋骨好」，嚴重的傷叫「傷筋動骨」。俗話說「傷筋動骨一百天」，意思是這種傷要一百天才會好。這是俗語，不是醫學規則，但它和醫生說的是同一件事：骨頭會癒合，只是很慢。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If you think you have hurt a bone, tell an adult and see a doctor.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果覺得骨頭受傷了，請告訴大人並就醫。

lessons.title: How Do Muscles Move Your Bones?
lessons.blurb_en: Muscles can only pull, never push, so they work in pairs. Lift a 3D arm and watch the biceps and triceps take turns.
lessons.blurb_zh: 肌肉只能拉、不能推，所以總是成對工作；抬起 3D 手臂，看二頭肌和三頭肌輪流用力。
lessons.big_idea_en: Muscles can only pull. To bend and straighten a joint, two muscles take turns, one on each side.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 肌肉只能拉。要讓關節彎曲又伸直，兩條肌肉在兩側輪流用力。

lab.title_zh: 二頭肌和三頭肌輪流用力
lab.how_en: The bones are the real ones from Lesson 1; the two muscles are drawn to show how they work. Press Lift, Lower slowly, or Push, or drag the slider to bend the elbow yourself. Put something in the hand to see how hard the biceps has to pull, and turn on Lever to see why.
lab.how_zh: 骨頭是第一課那副真實骨架；兩條肌肉是為了說明原理畫上去的。按「舉起」「慢慢放下」「推出」，或拖動滑桿自己彎手肘。在手上放個東西，看二頭肌要出多少力；打開「槓桿」看看為什麼。

legend.en: Red: a muscle that is pulling (getting shorter)
legend.zh: 紅色：正在用力收縮（變短）的肌肉

legend.en: Orange: a muscle working while it gets longer, like a brake
legend.zh: 橘色：一邊用力一邊變長的肌肉，像煞車

legend.en: White ends: tendons, the tough cords that tie muscle to bone
legend.zh: 白色兩端：肌腱，把肌肉綁在骨頭上的強韌繩索

legend.en: Gold arrows: the direction each muscle pulls. There are no pushing arrows.
legend.zh: 金色箭頭：肌肉拉的方向——沒有「推」的箭頭

lab.scale_en: The bones are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1. The two muscles are simplified shapes: in a real arm, the biceps starts at two points on the shoulder blade, and the triceps has three heads. The pulling force is a rough estimate for an adult arm.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架。兩條肌肉是簡化的形狀：真實的二頭肌從肩胛骨的兩個地方出發，三頭肌則有三個頭。拉力是以成人手臂粗估的數字。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the muscles are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，肌肉為本站自繪示意。

paras: Make a fist and slowly bend your arm, bringing your hand up toward your shoulder. A bump rises on the front of your upper arm. That bump is your biceps, one of more than 600 muscles in your body. Together, your muscles make up about a third or more of your body weight. Every move you make, from blinking to kicking a ball, happens because a muscle pulls on something.

A muscle is a bundle of long, thin cells called muscle fibers. When your brain sends a signal down a nerve, the fibers contract, which means they get shorter and fatter. At each end, the muscle turns into a tendon, a tough cord that is tied to a bone. As the muscle shortens, the tendon pulls the bone along with it. But here is the surprising part: a muscle can only pull. It cannot push. When the signal stops, the muscle relaxes, but it does not stretch itself back out.

So how does your arm straighten again? Muscles work in pairs, one on each side of a joint. When the biceps on the front of your upper arm contracts, it pulls your forearm up and bends the elbow. To straighten the elbow with force, as when you push a door open or do a push-up, the triceps on the back of your upper arm contracts and pulls the other way. While one muscle pulls, its partner relaxes and gets stretched. Your knee works the same way: the big muscles on the front of your thigh straighten it, and the ones on the back bend it.

Your bones and muscles work like levers, with each joint as the pivot. The biceps is attached to the forearm only about four centimeters from the elbow, but your hand is more than thirty centimeters away. That means the biceps has to pull about eight times harder than the weight in your hand. Holding a three-kilogram dumbbell with your elbow bent at a right angle, your biceps pulls roughly as hard as lifting almost thirty kilograms. Why would the body be built this way? Because a short pull close to the joint moves the hand a long way, and quickly, which is just what you need to throw a ball or wave hello.

Not all of your muscles move bones. The muscles you control on purpose, like your biceps, are called skeletal muscles. Your heart is made of cardiac muscle, which beats about 100,000 times a day without ever taking a break or waiting for you to think about it. The walls of your stomach, intestines, and blood vessels contain smooth muscle, which squeezes slowly to move food along and to control the flow of blood. You cannot tell these muscles what to do, and they keep working even while you sleep.

Muscles also do a job you might not expect: they keep you warm. Working muscles produce heat, which is why you get hot when you run, and why you shiver on a cold day. Shivering is thousands of tiny, fast contractions whose only purpose is to make heat. Like bones, muscles respond to how you use them. Regular exercise makes muscle fibers thicker and stronger, while weeks of rest in bed make them smaller. Now try it yourself: rest one hand on your upper arm, then lift a bag and press down on a desk, and feel your two muscles take turns.
paras_zh: 握緊拳頭，慢慢彎起手臂，把手往肩膀的方向抬。上臂前面會鼓起一塊——那就是二頭肌，你全身六百多塊肌肉中的一塊。肌肉加起來大約占體重的三分之一以上。你做的每一個動作，從眨眼到踢球，都是因為有一塊肌肉在拉著某個東西。
肌肉是一束又長又細的細胞，叫做肌纖維。大腦沿著神經送出訊號時，肌纖維會收縮，也就是變短、變粗。肌肉的兩端各變成一條肌腱——一條綁在骨頭上的強韌繩索。肌肉一縮短，肌腱就把骨頭跟著拉過去。但令人意外的是：肌肉只能拉，不能推。訊號停止時，肌肉會放鬆，但它不會自己伸展回原來的長度。
那手臂要怎麼再伸直呢？肌肉是成對工作的，關節兩側各一條。上臂前面的二頭肌收縮時，把前臂往上拉，手肘就彎起來。要用力把手肘伸直，例如推開一扇門或做伏地挺身，就換上臂後面的三頭肌收縮，往另一個方向拉。一條肌肉在拉的時候，它的搭檔就放鬆、被拉長。膝蓋也是一樣：大腿前面的大肌肉把膝蓋伸直，後面的肌肉把它彎起來。
骨頭和肌肉就像槓桿，每個關節就是支點。二頭肌接在前臂上離手肘只有大約四公分的地方，手卻在三十多公分外。這表示二頭肌要出的力，大約是手上重量的八倍。手肘彎成直角拿著一個三公斤的啞鈴時，二頭肌出的力大概等於舉起將近三十公斤。身體為什麼要這樣設計？因為在靠近關節的地方拉一小段，手就能移動很遠、而且很快——丟球、揮手打招呼需要的正是這個。
不是所有肌肉都拉骨頭。像二頭肌這種你可以自己控制的肌肉，叫做骨骼肌。心臟由心肌構成，一天大約跳十萬下，從不休息，也不用等你想到它。胃、腸和血管的管壁裡有平滑肌，它們慢慢地收縮，把食物往前推送、控制血液的流動。這些肌肉你無法指揮，連睡覺時它們也照樣工作。
肌肉還有一個你可能想不到的工作：幫你保暖。工作中的肌肉會產生熱，所以你跑步時會變熱，冷天時會發抖——發抖就是成千上萬次又小又快的收縮，唯一的目的就是產生熱。跟骨頭一樣，肌肉會回應你怎麼使用它：規律運動讓肌纖維變粗、變強壯；在床上躺好幾個星期，肌肉就會變小。現在自己試試看：把一隻手放在上臂上，提起書包、再用力按桌面，感覺兩條肌肉輪流用力。
questions: Why do muscles have to work in pairs?
What does a tendon do?
Why does the biceps have to pull much harder than the weight in your hand?
answers: Because a muscle can only pull, never push. One muscle bends the joint, and its partner on the other side pulls it straight again.
A tendon is a tough cord at the end of a muscle that ties the muscle to a bone, so when the muscle shortens, the tendon pulls the bone.
The biceps is attached only about four centimeters from the elbow, while the hand is more than thirty centimeters away, so, like a lever, it must pull about eight times harder than the weight.

vocab.ex: You use more than forty muscles in your face to smile and frown.
vocab.exzh: 微笑和皺眉時，你用到臉上四十多塊肌肉。

vocab.ex: Your heart contracts to push blood out into your body.
vocab.exzh: 心臟收縮，把血液送到全身。

vocab.ex: Take a deep breath and let your shoulders relax.
vocab.exzh: 深呼吸，讓肩膀放鬆。

vocab.ex: The Achilles tendon connects your calf muscle to your heel.
vocab.exzh: 阿基里斯腱把小腿的肌肉連到腳跟。

vocab.ex: A single fiber of this rope is thin, but thousands together are very strong.
vocab.exzh: 這條繩子的一根纖維很細，但成千上萬根合在一起就非常結實。

vocab.ex: I need a new pair of running shoes.
vocab.exzh: 我需要一雙新的跑鞋。

vocab.ex: A seesaw is a lever, and the middle is its pivot.
vocab.exzh: 蹺蹺板是一種槓桿，中間就是它的支點。

vocab.ex: We shivered at the bus stop in the cold wind.
vocab.exzh: 我們在冷風中的公車站發抖。

quiz.q: What can a muscle do?
Which muscle bends your elbow?
What connects a muscle to a bone?
What kind of muscle is your heart made of?
According to the reading, why do we shiver when we are cold?
options: Muscles contract quickly to make heat
Our muscles are too tired to hold still
The cold air pushes our muscles

pairs.text_en: The biceps on the front bends the elbow; the triceps on the back straightens it.
pairs.text_zh: 前面的二頭肌讓手肘彎曲，後面的三頭肌讓手肘伸直。
pairs.try_en: Do a slow push-up against a wall and feel the back of your arm work.
pairs.try_zh: 對著牆慢慢做伏地挺身，摸摸上臂後面在用力。

pairs.text_en: The quadriceps on the front of the thigh straightens the knee; the hamstrings on the back bend it.
pairs.text_zh: 大腿前面的股四頭肌把膝蓋伸直，後面的大腿後肌群把它彎起來。
pairs.try_en: Sit on a chair and straighten one leg. Feel the top of your thigh go hard.
pairs.try_zh: 坐在椅子上把一條腿伸直，摸摸大腿上面變硬了。

pairs.text_en: The shin muscle lifts your toes; the calf muscle, pulling on the Achilles tendon, points them down.
pairs.text_zh: 脛前肌把腳尖抬起；小腿肌拉著阿基里斯腱，讓腳尖往下踩。
pairs.try_en: Stand on your tiptoes, then rock back onto your heels.
pairs.try_zh: 踮起腳尖，再往後站到腳跟上。

pairs.text_en: Belly muscles curl you forward; back muscles straighten you up again.
pairs.text_zh: 腹肌讓你向前捲起身體，背肌再把你拉直。
pairs.try_en: Do one slow sit-up, then lie on your stomach and lift your chest a little.
pairs.try_zh: 慢慢做一下仰臥起坐，再趴著把胸口微微抬起。

lessons.pairs_note_en: In every pair, the two muscles sit on opposite sides of a joint. Doctors call them antagonists: partners that pull in opposite directions.
lessons.pairs_note_zh: 每一對肌肉都位在關節的兩側，醫學上叫做拮抗肌：方向相反、互相搭配的搭檔。

kinds.where_en: Attached to bones
kinds.text_en: Moves your body, keeps you standing, and makes heat. It gets tired and needs rest.
kinds.text_zh: 讓身體動、讓你站得住，也會產生熱。它會累，需要休息。

kinds.where_en: Only in the heart
kinds.text_en: Beats about 100,000 times a day for your whole life and never takes a break. Lesson 3 follows the blood it pumps.
kinds.text_zh: 一輩子每天跳大約十萬下，從不休息。第三課會跟著它打出的血液走一趟。

kinds.where_en: Stomach, intestines, blood vessels
kinds.text_en: Squeezes slowly in waves to move food along and to widen or narrow your blood vessels.
kinds.text_zh: 像波浪一樣慢慢收縮，把食物往前推，也讓血管變寬或變窄。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Only skeletal muscle pulls on bones, and it is the only kind you can move just by deciding to.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 只有骨骼肌會拉骨頭，也只有它是你「想動就能動」的。

measure.lead_en: Rest your left hand on your right upper arm, with your thumb on the front and your fingers on the back. Then try these three moves.
measure.lead_zh: 把左手放在右上臂上，拇指在前面、其他手指在後面，然後做下面三個動作。

steps.en: Lift
steps.zh: 舉起
steps.text_en: Lift a school bag by bending your elbow. The front (biceps) goes hard; the back stays soft.
steps.text_zh: 彎起手肘提起書包：前面（二頭肌）變硬，後面還是軟的。

steps.en: Push
steps.zh: 推
steps.text_en: Put your palm on a desk and press straight down. Now the back (triceps) goes hard, and the front goes soft.
steps.text_zh: 手掌放在桌上用力往下壓：這次換後面（三頭肌）變硬，前面變軟。

steps.en: Relax
steps.zh: 放鬆
steps.text_en: Let your arm hang loosely. Both muscles are soft, and you can wiggle them from side to side.
steps.text_zh: 讓手臂自然垂下：兩條肌肉都軟軟的，可以左右晃動它們。

measure.button_zh: 在 3D 模型裡舉起再推出

myths.myth_en: Muscles can push as well as pull.
myths.myth_zh: 肌肉可以拉，也可以推。
myths.fact_en: A muscle can only pull. Every push you make, like pushing a door, is really a muscle pulling on the other side of a joint. In the model, the arrows only ever point toward the middle of a muscle.
myths.fact_zh: 肌肉只能拉。你做的每一個「推」（像推門），其實都是關節另一側的肌肉在拉。模型裡的箭頭，永遠指向肌肉的中間。

myths.myth_en: When you lower a heavy bag, your triceps does the work.
myths.myth_zh: 慢慢放下重物時，是三頭肌在出力。
myths.fact_en: Gravity pulls the bag down. Your biceps keeps working and lets itself get longer bit by bit, like a brake. Press Lower slowly in the model and watch it turn orange.
myths.fact_zh: 把重物往下拉的是重力；二頭肌一直在用力，讓自己一點一點變長，就像煞車。在模型裡按「慢慢放下」，看它變成橘色。

myths.myth_en: If you stop exercising, your muscles turn into fat.
myths.myth_zh: 不運動，肌肉就會變成脂肪。
myths.fact_en: Muscle and fat are different tissues, and one cannot turn into the other. Unused muscles shrink, and if you eat more than you use, fat can build up, so it can look that way.
myths.fact_zh: 肌肉和脂肪是兩種不同的組織，不會互相變來變去。不用的肌肉會變小；吃得比用掉的多，脂肪會增加——所以看起來像是變了。

myths.myth_en: The biceps is the biggest muscle in your body.
myths.myth_zh: 二頭肌是全身最大的肌肉。
myths.fact_en: The biggest is the gluteus maximus, the muscle you sit on. It straightens your hip every time you climb stairs or stand up from a chair.
myths.fact_zh: 最大的是臀大肌，就是你坐著的那塊肌肉。每次爬樓梯或從椅子上站起來，都是它把髖部伸直。

tricks.title_en: Muscles pull, bones move, joints bend
tricks.body_en: Three parts, three jobs. If you remember the order, you can explain any move your body makes.
tricks.body_zh: 三個部分、三個工作。記住這個順序，就能解釋身體的任何一個動作。

tricks.body_en: A bicycle has two wheels and a tricycle has three. The biceps starts with two heads and the triceps with three.
tricks.body_zh: bicycle 兩個輪子、tricycle 三個輪子；biceps 起點有兩個頭，triceps 有三個頭。

tricks.body_en: In every pair, one muscle contracts while its partner relaxes. If both pulled hard at once, the joint would lock in place.
tricks.body_zh: 每一對肌肉裡，一條收縮，它的搭檔就放鬆。如果兩條同時用力，關節就會卡住不動。

tricks.body_en: The biceps shortens only a few centimeters, but the hand swings through a big arc. That trade of force for speed is why you can throw a ball so fast.
tricks.body_zh: 二頭肌只縮短幾公分，手卻劃過一大段弧線。用力氣換速度，所以你才能把球丟得那麼快。

activities.title_en: Build a Cardboard Arm with String Muscles
activities.title_zh: 用紙板和棉線做一隻手臂

materials.en: Two strips of stiff cardboard, about 3 × 20 centimeters (upper arm and forearm)
materials.zh: 兩條硬紙板，約 3 × 20 公分（上臂與前臂）

materials.en: A brass paper fastener (the elbow)
materials.zh: 一個雙腳釘（手肘）

materials.en: Two pieces of string, about 40 centimeters each (the muscles)
materials.zh: 兩條棉線，各約 40 公分（肌肉）

materials.en: A hole punch and tape
materials.zh: 打洞機和膠帶

steps.en: Join the two strips at one end with the fastener so they can bend like an elbow.
steps.zh: 用雙腳釘把兩條紙板的一端接起來，讓它們可以像手肘一樣彎。

steps.en: Punch a hole in the forearm strip about 3 centimeters from the elbow. Tie one string there and run it along the front of the upper arm. This is the biceps.
steps.zh: 在前臂紙板離手肘約 3 公分處打一個洞，綁上一條棉線，沿著上臂的前面拉上去——這是二頭肌。

steps.en: Tape the second string to the short tab of the forearm behind the elbow and run it along the back of the upper arm. This is the triceps.
steps.zh: 把第二條棉線貼在前臂超出手肘後面的那一小段，沿著上臂的後面拉上去——這是三頭肌。

steps.en: Hold the upper arm still and pull each string. Then try to push with a string. What happens?
steps.zh: 固定上臂，分別拉兩條線；再試試看用線「推」。會發生什麼事？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: a string, like a muscle, goes slack when you try to push with it, so the arm needs one string on each side. Then move the biceps hole farther from the elbow: the pull gets easier, but the hand moves less.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：棉線和肌肉一樣，一推就軟掉，所以手臂兩側各需要一條。接著把二頭肌的洞打在離手肘更遠的地方：拉起來比較省力，但手移動的距離變短了。

activities.title_en: The Clothespin Squeeze: Do Muscles Get Tired?

materials.en: A spring clothespin for each student
materials.zh: 每人一個有彈簧的曬衣夾

materials.en: A timer
materials.zh: 一個計時器

materials.en: Paper to record the counts
materials.zh: 記錄次數的紙

steps.en: Hold the clothespin between your thumb and index finger. Count how many times you can squeeze it open in 30 seconds.
steps.zh: 用拇指和食指捏住曬衣夾，數一數 30 秒內能捏開幾次。

steps.en: Without resting, do it again two more times, and write down each count.
steps.zh: 不要休息，再連續做兩次，記下每次的次數。

steps.en: Rest for one minute, then try once more.
steps.zh: 休息一分鐘，再做一次。

steps.en: Compare the counts. What happened, and what did the rest do?
steps.zh: 比較這幾次的次數：發生了什麼事？休息帶來什麼改變？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the counts usually drop as the small muscles in the hand tire, and they come back after a rest. That is why skeletal muscles need breaks, while the heart, made of a different kind of muscle, never gets tired this way.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：次數通常會越來越少，因為手上的小肌肉累了；休息之後又會恢復。這就是骨骼肌需要休息的原因——而由另一種肌肉構成的心臟，不會這樣累。

culture.body_en: In Chinese, a muscle cramp is 抽筋 (chōujīn), literally “a sinew being pulled.” That is a good description: in a cramp, a muscle contracts on its own and will not relax. Its partner on the other side can help. For a calf cramp, gently pulling your toes toward you uses the shin side to stretch the calf. Another saying, 活動活動筋骨, “move your sinews and bones a little,” means to loosen up and warm up before exercise.
culture.body_zh: 中文把肌肉痙攣叫「抽筋」，字面上是「一條筋被抽住」。這個說法很傳神：抽筋時，肌肉自己收縮、放不開。這時關節另一側的搭檔可以幫忙——小腿抽筋時，把腳尖輕輕往身體方向拉，就是用前側把小腿肌拉開。另一句「活動活動筋骨」，則是運動前暖身、鬆一鬆的意思。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If a muscle hurts badly, swells, or a cramp will not go away, tell an adult and see a doctor.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果肌肉非常痛、腫起來，或抽筋一直不好，請告訴大人並就醫。

lessons.title: Where Does Your Blood Go?
lessons.title_zh: 血液在身體裡怎麼流動？
lessons.blurb_en: Your heart sends blood around two loops, one to the lungs and one to the whole body. Tap along with your pulse, and the 3D heart beats with you.
lessons.blurb_zh: 心臟把血液送進兩個循環：一個到肺、一個到全身。跟著自己的脈搏點一點，3D 心臟就用你的心跳跳動。
lessons.big_idea_en: The heart is two pumps side by side. The right side sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen; the left side sends it to the rest of the body.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 心臟是並排的兩個幫浦：右邊把血送到肺裡拿氧氣，左邊把血送到全身。

lab.how_en: Watch the blood cells flow: dark red on the way to the lungs, bright red after they pick up oxygen. Switch to slow motion to see the valves open and close, follow the glowing drop around both loops, or press Measure my pulse and tap along with your own heartbeat for 15 seconds. The heart in the model will then beat at your speed.
lab.how_zh: 看血球流動：往肺去的時候是暗紅色，拿到氧氣之後變成鮮紅色。切到慢動作，看瓣膜一開一關；跟著發光的那一滴血繞完兩個循環；或按「量我的脈搏」，跟著自己的心跳按 15 秒，模型裡的心臟就會用你的速度跳。

legend.en: Bright red: blood rich in oxygen
legend.zh: 鮮紅色：含氧多的血

legend.en: Dark red: blood low in oxygen. Real blood is never blue.
legend.zh: 暗紅色：含氧少的血——真正的血從來不是藍色

legend.en: Cream disks: valves, shown closed. They open to let blood through one way.
legend.zh: 米色圓片：瓣膜關上時的樣子；打開時只讓血往一個方向流

legend.en: Glowing drop: one blood cell you can follow
legend.zh: 發光的點：可以跟著走的一顆血球

lab.scale_en: A simplified model, not real anatomy. The real heart is tilted, with its tip toward the lower left, and the chambers are hidden inside thick muscle walls. The loops are drawn short: in your body, one trip around both loops takes about a minute at rest, not a few heartbeats.
lab.scale_zh: 這是簡化的示意模型，不是真實解剖。真正的心臟是斜的，心尖朝左下，腔室藏在厚厚的心肌裡。循環也畫得很短：在身體裡，安靜時血液繞完兩個循環大約要一分鐘，不是幾下心跳。

stops.en: Right atrium: blood from the body arrives
stops.zh: 右心房：從全身回來的血進來

stops.en: Right ventricle: squeezes it toward the lungs
Pulmonary artery: on the way to the lungs
Lungs: drops carbon dioxide, picks up oxygen
stops.zh: 肺：放下二氧化碳、帶走氧氣

stops.en: Pulmonary vein and left atrium: back to the heart
stops.zh: 肺靜脈、左心房：回到心臟

stops.en: Aorta: out to the whole body
Capillaries: delivers oxygen and food, picks up waste
stops.zh: 微血管：送出氧氣與養分、收走廢物

paras: Press two fingers gently on the thumb side of your wrist. Each little bump you feel is your pulse, and every bump is one squeeze of your heart. Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist, sitting behind your breastbone between your two lungs. It beats about 100,000 times a day, and in a long life, close to three billion times, without ever stopping to rest.

Why does it work so hard? Every cell in your body needs a steady supply of oxygen and food, and every cell makes waste, such as carbon dioxide, that has to be carried away. Blood is the delivery service. An adult has about five liters of it, and the heart pumps all of it around the body roughly once every minute when you are resting.

The surprising part is that your heart is really two pumps, side by side, divided by a wall of muscle. The right side collects blood coming back from the body, which has given away much of its oxygen, and pumps it to the lungs. There the blood drops off carbon dioxide and picks up fresh oxygen. The left side collects that oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and pumps it out to the rest of the body. Both sides squeeze at the same moment, so every heartbeat sends blood around both loops at once. The left side has the thickest wall, because it has to push blood all the way to your toes and back.

Each pump has two rooms, called chambers. The upper chamber, the atrium, collects blood. The lower chamber, the ventricle, is the strong one that squeezes it out. Between the chambers, and at the exits, are valves, flaps that work like one-way doors. When they snap shut, they make the sound a doctor hears through a stethoscope: lub-dub, lub-dub. The first sound is the doors between the atria and the ventricles closing, and the second is the doors at the exits closing.

Blood travels through three kinds of tubes. Arteries carry it away from the heart. Their walls are thick and stretchy, and the pulse you feel is an artery swelling with each squeeze. Arteries branch into capillaries, tubes so thin that blood cells must line up in single file to pass through. Their walls are only one cell thick, so oxygen and food can slip out and waste can slip in. Capillaries join into veins, which carry the blood back to the heart. For a long time, people in Europe believed that the body used up blood and kept making new blood. In 1628, the English doctor William Harvey showed that it must flow around and around in a circle.

Your heart rate changes all day. It is slowest when you are asleep, and it speeds up when you run, get excited, or feel scared, so that more oxygen reaches your working muscles. For most adults, a resting pulse is between 60 and 100 beats a minute, and children's hearts usually beat a little faster. Regular exercise makes the heart muscle stronger, so it can pump more blood with each beat. Now find your own pulse, count it for 15 seconds, and let the heart in the model beat with yours.
paras_zh: 把兩根手指輕輕放在手腕靠拇指的那一側。你摸到的每一下小小的跳動，就是脈搏，而每一下都是心臟擠壓了一次。心臟是一塊大約拳頭大小的肌肉，位在胸骨後面、兩片肺的中間。它一天大約跳十萬下，長壽的人一輩子會跳將近三十億下，從來不停下來休息。
它為什麼要這麼努力？身體的每一個細胞都需要源源不絕的氧氣和養分，而每個細胞也會製造廢物，例如二氧化碳，必須被運走。血液就是這套快遞系統。成人全身大約有五公升的血，安靜時，心臟大約每一分鐘就把全部的血送完一圈。
令人意外的是，心臟其實是兩個並排的幫浦，中間隔著一道肌肉牆。右邊收集從全身回來、已經交出大部分氧氣的血，把它送到肺；血在肺裡放下二氧化碳、帶走新鮮的氧氣。左邊收集從肺回來、充滿氧氣的血，把它送到全身。左右兩邊在同一瞬間收縮，所以每一次心跳都同時把血送進兩個循環。左邊的心壁最厚，因為它得把血一路推到腳趾、再繞回來。
每個幫浦都有兩個房間，叫做腔室。上面的心房負責收集血液，下面的心室是強壯的那一個，負責把血擠出去。腔室之間和出口都有瓣膜，也就是像單向門一樣的薄片。它們啪一聲關上時，就發出醫生用聽診器聽到的聲音：噗通、噗通。第一聲是心房和心室之間的門關上，第二聲是出口的門關上。
血液在三種管子裡流動。動脈把血帶離心臟，管壁厚又有彈性，你摸到的脈搏，就是動脈隨著每一次擠壓鼓起來。動脈分支成微血管，細到血球必須排成一列才能通過；微血管壁只有一個細胞厚，氧氣和養分可以滲出去，廢物可以滲進來。微血管再匯集成靜脈，把血帶回心臟。很長一段時間，歐洲人以為身體會把血用掉、再不斷製造新的血；直到 1628 年，英國醫生威廉・哈維證明，血液一定是一圈又一圈地循環。
心跳速度一整天都在變：睡覺時最慢；跑步、興奮或害怕時變快，好讓更多氧氣送到正在工作的肌肉。大多數成人安靜時的脈搏是每分鐘 60 到 100 下，孩子的心跳通常稍微快一點。規律運動讓心肌更強壯，每跳一下就能打出更多血。現在找到自己的脈搏，數 15 秒，讓模型裡的心臟跟著你的心跳一起跳。
questions: Why do we say the heart is two pumps?
What happens to blood in the lungs, and what happens to it in the capillaries of the body?
What makes the lub-dub sound of the heart?
answers: Because the right side and the left side each pump blood on their own path: the right side sends blood to the lungs, and the left side sends it to the rest of the body.
In the lungs, blood drops off carbon dioxide and picks up oxygen. In the capillaries of the body, it gives oxygen and food to the cells and picks up waste.
The valves snapping shut: first the valves between the atria and the ventricles, then the valves at the exits of the ventricles.

vocab.ex: Your heart beats faster when you run up the stairs.
vocab.exzh: 跑上樓梯時，你的心臟跳得比較快。

vocab.ex: Firefighters pump water from the river to put out the fire.
vocab.exzh: 消防員從河裡抽水來滅火。

vocab.ex: Fish take oxygen from the water with their gills.
vocab.exzh: 魚用鰓從水中取得氧氣。

vocab.ex: The nurse felt the artery in my wrist to count my pulse.
vocab.exzh: 護理師摸我手腕的動脈來數脈搏。

vocab.ex: You can see the blue lines of veins under the skin of your hand.
vocab.exzh: 你可以看到手背皮膚下青藍色的靜脈。

vocab.ex: A capillary is thinner than a single hair.
vocab.exzh: 一條微血管比一根頭髮還細。

vocab.ex: After the race, my pulse was 150 beats a minute.
vocab.exzh: 賽跑完，我的脈搏是每分鐘 150 下。

vocab.ex: Turn the valve to stop the water.
vocab.exzh: 轉動閥門把水關掉。

quiz.q: Where does the right side of the heart send blood?
options: To the left side of the body

quiz.q: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?
What do the valves in the heart do?
About how much blood does an adult have?
According to the reading, what did William Harvey show in 1628?
options: Blood flows around and around in a circle

chambers.text_en: A waiting room for blood that has given away its oxygen.
chambers.text_zh: 已經交出氧氣的血，先在這裡等候。

chambers.text_en: A gentle pump: the lungs are close by, so it does not need to push very hard.
chambers.text_zh: 溫和的幫浦：肺就在旁邊，不需要太用力。

chambers.text_en: Collects bright red, oxygen-rich blood fresh from the lungs.
chambers.text_zh: 收集剛從肺回來、充滿氧氣的鮮紅色血液。

chambers.text_en: The strongest chamber, with the thickest wall. Its squeeze is the pulse you feel.
chambers.text_zh: 最強壯、心壁最厚的腔室；你摸到的脈搏，就是它擠出來的。

lessons.chambers_note_en: Atria on top collect; ventricles below pump. The right side handles oxygen-poor blood, the left side oxygen-rich blood, and the two never mix.
lessons.chambers_note_zh: 上面的心房負責收集，下面的心室負責打出。右邊處理缺氧的血、左邊處理充氧的血，兩邊從不混在一起。

kinds_head.eyebrow: Three Kinds of Tubes · 三種血管

kinds.where_en: Away from the heart
kinds.text_en: They swell with every heartbeat. That swelling is the pulse you feel in your wrist and neck.
kinds.text_zh: 每次心跳都會鼓起來，那就是你在手腕、脖子摸到的脈搏。

kinds.where_en: Between arteries and veins
kinds.text_en: So narrow that blood cells pass in single file. This is where oxygen, food, and waste trade places.
kinds.text_zh: 窄到血球只能排成一列通過；氧氣、養分和廢物就在這裡交換。

kinds.where_en: Back to the heart
kinds.text_en: Blood here moves slowly and gently. Little valves stop it from sliding back down your legs.
kinds.text_zh: 這裡的血流得又慢又輕；小小的瓣膜防止血從腿往下倒流。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Laid end to end, all the blood vessels in an adult would stretch for tens of thousands of kilometers, and almost all of that length is capillaries.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把成人全身的血管接成一條，長度有好幾萬公里，而其中幾乎全是微血管。

measure.title_en: Find your pulse and give the heart your beat
measure.title_zh: 找到脈搏，讓心臟用你的速度跳
measure.lead_en: Use two fingers, not your thumb, because your thumb has a pulse of its own. Then press Measure my pulse and tap once for every beat for 15 seconds.
measure.lead_zh: 用兩根手指，不要用拇指，因為拇指自己也有脈搏。然後按「量我的脈搏」，15 秒內每摸到一下就按一次。

steps.en: Find it
steps.zh: 找到它
steps.text_en: Put two fingers on the thumb side of your wrist, just below the palm, and press gently until you feel a beat.
steps.text_zh: 兩根手指放在手腕靠拇指的一側、手掌下方一點，輕輕按到感覺有跳動。

steps.en: Count
steps.zh: 數一數
steps.text_en: Count the beats for 15 seconds, then multiply by 4 to get beats per minute. The model does the math for you.
steps.text_zh: 數 15 秒內跳幾下，再乘以 4 就是每分鐘的心跳。模型會幫你算。

steps.en: Move and measure again
steps.zh: 動一動再量
steps.text_en: Do 30 jumping jacks, then measure again right away. How much faster is it? How long until it slows down?
steps.text_zh: 做 30 下開合跳，馬上再量一次。快了多少？多久才慢下來？

myths.myth_en: The blood in your veins is blue.
myths.myth_zh: 靜脈裡的血是藍色的。
myths.fact_en: Blood is always red: bright red with lots of oxygen, dark red with less. Veins only look blue through your skin because of the way skin scatters light.
myths.fact_zh: 血永遠是紅色的：含氧多是鮮紅、含氧少是暗紅。靜脈隔著皮膚看起來是藍的，是皮膚散射光線造成的。

myths.myth_en: Your heart is on the left side of your chest.
myths.myth_zh: 心臟在胸口的左邊。
myths.fact_en: It sits almost in the middle, behind the breastbone. Its tip points to the left, and the strong left ventricle is there, so the beat is easiest to feel on the left.
myths.fact_zh: 它幾乎在正中間、胸骨後面，只是心尖朝左，強壯的左心室又在那一側，所以左邊最容易摸到心跳。

myths.myth_en: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood, and veins carry oxygen-poor blood.
myths.myth_zh: 動脈裡是充氧血，靜脈裡是缺氧血。
myths.fact_en: Arteries and veins are named for their direction, not their oxygen. The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood back.
myths.fact_zh: 動脈、靜脈是依方向命名，不是依含氧量。肺動脈把缺氧的血送到肺，肺靜脈再把充氧的血帶回來。

myths.myth_en: The heart pumps blood to the lungs first, and then to the body.
myths.myth_zh: 心臟先把血送到肺，再送到全身。
myths.fact_en: Both sides squeeze at the same moment. With every beat, the right side pushes blood toward the lungs while the left side pushes blood toward the body.
myths.fact_zh: 左右兩邊在同一瞬間收縮。每跳一下，右邊把血推向肺的同時，左邊也把血推向全身。

tricks.title_en: A for Artery, A for Away
tricks.body_en: Arteries carry blood away from the heart. Veins bring it back.
tricks.body_zh: 動脈把血帶離心臟，靜脈把血帶回來。

tricks.title_en: Right to breathe, left to feed
tricks.title_zh: 右邊送去呼吸，左邊送去餵飽全身
tricks.body_en: The right side sends blood to the lungs to breathe in oxygen. The left side sends it out to feed every cell.
tricks.body_zh: 右心把血送到肺裡「呼吸」拿氧氣；左心把血送出去「餵」每一個細胞。

tricks.body_en: Lub: the doors between the upper and lower chambers shut. Dub: the doors at the exits shut. Turn on the sound in the model and watch the valves.
tricks.body_zh: 噗：上下腔室之間的門關上；通：出口的門關上。在模型裡打開心跳聲，對照瓣膜看看。

tricks.body_en: Make a fist: your heart is about that size, and it grows as you grow. Squeeze your fist hard: your heart does that about 100,000 times a day.
tricks.body_zh: 握個拳頭：你的心臟大約就這麼大，而且跟著你一起長大。用力握緊拳頭——你的心臟一天要這樣擠大約十萬次。

activities.title_en: Rest, Exercise, Recover: A Pulse Graph
activities.title_zh: 安靜、運動、恢復：畫出脈搏圖

materials.en: A clock or timer with seconds
materials.zh: 有秒針的時鐘或計時器

materials.en: A worksheet or graph paper
materials.zh: 學習單或方格紙

materials.en: Space to jump safely
materials.zh: 可以安全跳動的空間

steps.en: Sit quietly for two minutes, then count your pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4.
steps.zh: 安靜坐兩分鐘，數 15 秒脈搏，再乘以 4。

steps.en: Do 30 jumping jacks and measure again right away.
steps.zh: 做 30 下開合跳，馬上再量一次。

steps.en: Measure again after 1, 2, and 3 minutes of rest.
steps.zh: 休息 1、2、3 分鐘後各再量一次。

steps.en: Graph your results: time along the bottom, beats per minute up the side. How long does your heart take to recover?
steps.zh: 把結果畫成圖：橫軸是時間、縱軸是每分鐘心跳。你的心臟要多久才恢復？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: compare graphs without ranking students. A heart that slows down quickly after exercise is a sign of fitness, and every student's graph will look a little different. Anyone with a heart condition can do the counting without the jumping.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：比較圖形，但不要替學生排名。運動後心跳很快就慢下來，是體能好的表現，而每個人的圖都會有點不一樣。有心臟疾病的學生可以只負責數，不用跳。

materials.en: An empty paper towel tube, or a sheet of paper rolled into a tube
materials.zh: 一個空的廚房紙巾捲筒，或一張捲成筒狀的紙

materials.en: A quiet room
materials.zh: 一間安靜的教室

materials.en: A partner
materials.zh: 一位同伴

steps.en: Place one end of the tube on your partner's chest, a little left of the middle, and your ear on the other end.
steps.zh: 把紙筒一端放在同伴胸口正中偏左一點，另一端貼著你的耳朵。

steps.en: Listen for lub-dub. Count the beats for 15 seconds.
steps.zh: 聽「噗通」聲，數 15 秒跳幾下。

steps.en: Have your partner do 20 jumping jacks, then listen again. What changed?
steps.zh: 請同伴做 20 下開合跳，再聽一次。有什麼改變？

steps.en: Switch roles.
steps.zh: 交換角色。

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: always ask before touching, and let students listen to their own heart if they prefer. The first sound is longer and lower; the second is shorter and sharper. Match them to the valves in the 3D model in slow motion.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：碰觸別人之前一定要先徵得同意，也可以讓學生聽自己的心跳。第一聲比較長、比較低，第二聲比較短、比較清脆；用 3D 模型的慢動作對照瓣膜看看。

culture.title_en: Taking the Pulse, and a Ring with No End
culture.body_en: In Chinese, taking someone's pulse is 把脈 (bǎmài), and in traditional Chinese medicine a doctor feels the pulse at three spots on the wrist. The ancient medical classic, the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic (黃帝內經), describes the body's flow as moving “like a ring with no end” (如環無端). And Chinese often uses 心 (heart) for the mind as well: 心想 means to think, and 心跳 is simply a heartbeat.
culture.body_zh: 中文把量脈搏叫「把脈」，中醫會在手腕上的三個位置切脈。古老的醫書《黃帝內經》形容身體裡的運行「如環無端」，像一個沒有終點的環。中文也常用「心」來指心思：「心想」是想，「心跳」就是心臟的跳動。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If your heart races for no reason, or you feel chest pain or faint, stop and tell an adult right away. When feeling a pulse in the neck, press gently and on one side only.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果心跳無緣無故變得很快，或覺得胸痛、快要昏倒，請馬上停下來告訴大人。在脖子量脈搏時要輕輕按，而且只按一邊。

lessons.title: How Does Air Get into Your Blood?
lessons.blurb_en: Every breath travels to hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs, where oxygen crosses into your blood. Breathe along with a 3D pair of lungs.
lessons.blurb_zh: 每一口氣都會走到幾億個小肺泡，氧氣在那裡進入血液；跟著 3D 的肺一起呼吸。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your lungs cannot pull in air by themselves. The diaphragm moves down, the chest gets bigger, and air rushes in.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 肺自己不會吸氣；是橫膈膜往下移、胸腔變大，空氣才湧進來。

lab.how_en: Watch the diaphragm under the lungs: when it moves down and the ribs lift, the lungs fill. Press and hold Hold to breathe in while you take a real breath, and let go as you breathe out; the model breathes with you. The small window shows what happens inside one air sac. Press Count my breaths to give the model your own breathing rate.
lab.how_zh: 看肺底下的橫膈膜：它往下移、肋骨往上抬，肺就鼓起來。真的吸一口氣時按住「按住吸氣」，吐氣時放開，模型就跟著你呼吸。旁邊的小窗顯示一個肺泡裡發生的事。按「數我的呼吸」，讓模型改用你自己的呼吸節奏。

legend.en: Red-brown dome: the diaphragm, the main breathing muscle
legend.zh: 紅褐色圓頂：橫膈膜，最主要的呼吸肌

legend.en: Light blue dots: fresh air coming in
legend.zh: 淡藍色的點：吸進來的新鮮空氣

legend.en: Yellow dots: air going out, with more carbon dioxide
legend.zh: 黃色的點：吐出去的空氣，二氧化碳比較多

legend.en: Cream tubes: the airways, branching like an upside-down tree
legend.zh: 米色管子：氣管與支氣管，像一棵倒過來的樹

lab.scale_en: The ribs, breastbone, and spine are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1. The lungs, airways, diaphragm, and heart are simplified drawings: real airways branch more than 20 times, not 6, and real air sacs are far too small to see.
lab.scale_zh: 肋骨、胸骨和脊椎是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架。肺、氣管、橫膈膜和心臟是簡化的示意圖：真實的氣管會分岔 20 多次，不是 6 次；真正的肺泡也小到肉眼看不見。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the lungs, airways, diaphragm, and heart are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，肺、氣管、橫膈膜與心臟為本站自繪示意。

paras: Put one hand on your belly and take a slow, deep breath. You probably felt your belly push out. You breathe more than 20,000 times a day, usually without thinking about it at all. A person can live for weeks without food and for days without water, but only a few minutes without air. Every one of your cells needs a steady supply of oxygen, and your lungs are where your body gets it.

Here is the surprise: your lungs cannot pull in air by themselves. They have no muscles of their own. The work is done by the diaphragm, a dome-shaped sheet of muscle under your lungs. When you breathe in, the diaphragm tightens and flattens, moving down, while small muscles between your ribs lift the ribs up and out. Your chest gets bigger, the air pressure inside your lungs drops, and air rushes in to fill the space. When you breathe out quietly, the diaphragm relaxes and domes back up, and your stretchy lungs spring back, like a balloon letting go of its air. The hand on your belly moved because the diaphragm pushed down on everything below it.

Air takes a long trip to get to your blood. It enters through your nose, where tiny hairs and sticky mucus catch dust, and where the air is warmed and made moist. It passes down your throat into the trachea, or windpipe, a tube held open by rings of cartilage that you can feel at the front of your neck. The trachea splits into two bronchi, one for each lung, and they split again and again, more than 20 times, into thousands of tiny tubes called bronchioles. Doctors call this the bronchial tree, because it looks like a tree turned upside down.

At the very end of the smallest branches are the alveoli, tiny air sacs that grow in bunches like grapes. You have hundreds of millions of them. Spread flat, their surface would cover about the floor of a classroom. Each air sac is wrapped in a net of capillaries, and the walls between the air and the blood are thinner than a soap bubble. Oxygen slips across into the blood, and carbon dioxide slips out into the air sac. Then the heart, which you met in Lesson 3, carries the fresh, oxygen-rich blood to the rest of your body.

The air you breathe in is about 21 percent oxygen. Surprisingly, the air you breathe out still has about 16 percent oxygen, but it carries about 100 times more carbon dioxide than it did coming in. Your cells use oxygen to release the energy stored in food, and carbon dioxide is what is left over. In fact, what makes you feel that you need to breathe is mostly a rise in carbon dioxide in your blood, which your brain keeps track of all the time. That is why you breathe faster and deeper when you run.

Most adults at rest breathe about 12 to 20 times a minute, and children breathe a little faster. Your lungs keep growing until you are about 20 years old, so the choices you make now matter. Smoke, whether from cigarettes, burning incense in a closed room, or polluted air, damages the delicate air sacs, while regular exercise strengthens the muscles that help you breathe. Now count your breaths for 30 seconds, and let the lungs in the model breathe with you.
paras_zh: 一手放在肚子上，慢慢深吸一口氣。你大概會感覺到肚子往外鼓。你一天呼吸兩萬多次，通常完全沒在想它。人可以好幾個星期不吃東西、好幾天不喝水，卻只能撐幾分鐘不呼吸。你的每一個細胞都需要源源不絕的氧氣，而肺就是身體取得氧氣的地方。
令人意外的是：肺自己不會吸氣，它們沒有自己的肌肉。真正在工作的是橫膈膜——肺底下一片圓頂形的肌肉。吸氣時，橫膈膜收縮變平、往下移，同時肋骨之間的小肌肉把肋骨往上、往外抬。胸腔變大，肺裡的氣壓下降，空氣就湧進來填滿空間。安靜吐氣時，橫膈膜放鬆、彈回圓頂，有彈性的肺也縮回去，就像氣球把氣放掉一樣。放在肚子上的手會動，是因為橫膈膜往下壓到它下面所有的器官。
空氣要走一段很長的路才到得了血液。它從鼻子進來，鼻毛和黏黏的鼻涕會攔住灰塵，空氣也在這裡被加溫、變得濕潤。接著它經過喉嚨，進入氣管——一條靠著一圈圈軟骨撐開的管子，你在脖子前面就摸得到。氣管分成兩條支氣管，一邊一條，然後一分再分，分岔二十多次，變成成千上萬條細小的細支氣管。醫生把它叫做支氣管樹，因為它看起來就像一棵倒過來的樹。
在最細的分支末端，是一串串像葡萄一樣的小氣囊，叫做肺泡。你有好幾億個肺泡；把它們的表面攤平，大約可以鋪滿一間教室的地板。每個肺泡外面都包著一層微血管網，空氣和血液之間的壁比肥皂泡還薄。氧氣從這裡滲進血液，二氧化碳則滲出來、進到肺泡裡。接著，第三課認識的心臟，就把新鮮、充滿氧氣的血送到全身。
我們吸進去的空氣大約有 21% 是氧氣。出乎意料的是，吐出來的空氣仍然有大約 16% 的氧氣，但二氧化碳比吸進來時多了約 100 倍。細胞用氧氣把食物裡儲存的能量釋放出來，二氧化碳就是剩下的東西。其實，讓你覺得「需要呼吸」的，主要是血液裡的二氧化碳變多了，而大腦隨時都在監測它。這就是為什麼跑步時，你會呼吸得又快又深。
大多數成人安靜時每分鐘呼吸 12 到 20 次，孩子稍微快一點。你的肺會一直長到大約 20 歲，所以現在的選擇很重要。煙——不論是香菸、在密閉房間裡燒香，或是污染的空氣——都會傷害脆弱的肺泡；規律運動則會讓幫助呼吸的肌肉更強壯。現在數一數你 30 秒呼吸幾次，讓模型裡的肺跟著你一起呼吸。
questions: If the lungs have no muscles, what makes air come in when you breathe in?
What happens in the alveoli?
What makes you feel that you need to breathe faster when you run?
answers: The diaphragm tightens and moves down, and the muscles between the ribs lift the ribs up and out. The chest gets bigger, the pressure inside the lungs drops, and air rushes in.
Oxygen passes from the air sacs into the blood in the capillaries around them, and carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air sacs to be breathed out.
Mostly a rise in carbon dioxide in the blood, which the brain keeps track of. Working muscles make more carbon dioxide, so you breathe faster and deeper.

vocab.ex: Whales have huge lungs and can hold their breath for a long time.
vocab.exzh: 鯨魚有巨大的肺，可以憋氣很久。

vocab.ex: Breathe in slowly through your nose.
vocab.exzh: 用鼻子慢慢吸氣。

vocab.ex: Singers learn to control their diaphragm to hold long notes.
vocab.exzh: 歌手學習控制橫膈膜，來唱出長音。

vocab.ex: The trachea is also called the windpipe.
vocab.exzh: 氣管的英文也叫 windpipe。

vocab.ex: Each tiny air sac is wrapped in blood vessels.
vocab.exzh: 每一個小小的肺泡都包著血管。

vocab.ex: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen.
vocab.exzh: 植物吸收二氧化碳，釋放出氧氣。

vocab.ex: Inhale deeply before you dive into the pool.
vocab.exzh: 跳進泳池之前，先深深吸一口氣。

vocab.ex: Exhale slowly and let your shoulders relax.
vocab.exzh: 慢慢吐氣，讓肩膀放鬆。

quiz.q: Which muscle does most of the work when you breathe in?
Where does oxygen pass into the blood?
What does the nose do to the air you breathe in?
About how much oxygen is in the air you breathe out?
According to the reading, why do people call the airways a tree?
options: They branch again and again like an upside-down tree

kinds_head.eyebrow: The Path of a Breath · 一口氣的旅程
kinds_head.en: From your nose to your blood

kinds.where_en: The entrance
kinds.text_en: Hairs and mucus trap dust and germs. Breathing through your nose gives your lungs cleaner, warmer air.
kinds.text_zh: 鼻毛和鼻涕攔住灰塵與病菌。用鼻子呼吸，肺得到的空氣更乾淨、更溫暖。

kinds.where_en: Down the front of the neck
kinds.text_en: The rings keep the tube open, like the ridges on a vacuum cleaner hose. Feel them gently below your Adam's apple.
kinds.text_zh: 軟骨環讓管子不會塌陷，就像吸塵器軟管上的一圈圈紋路。在喉結下方輕輕摸得到。

kinds.where_en: Inside each lung
kinds.text_en: The right bronchus is shorter and steeper than the left, which is why a peanut that goes down the wrong way more often ends up in the right lung.
kinds.text_zh: 右支氣管比左邊短、比較陡，所以不小心吸進去的花生，比較常掉進右肺。

kinds.where_en: At the tips of the branches
kinds.text_en: Walls thinner than a soap bubble, wrapped in capillaries. This is where oxygen crosses into the blood.
kinds.text_zh: 壁比肥皂泡還薄，外面包著微血管；氧氣就在這裡進入血液。

kinds.where_en: Pulmonary veins to the heart
kinds.text_en: Oxygen-rich blood goes to the left side of the heart, which pumps it out to every cell in the body.
kinds.text_zh: 充滿氧氣的血回到左心，再被打到全身每一個細胞。

lessons.kinds_note_en: On its way from the tip of your nose to an air sac, the air passes through more than 20 branchings, and the whole trip takes about as long as one breath in.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 從鼻尖到肺泡，空氣一路要經過二十多次分岔，整趟旅程大約只要吸一口氣的時間。

measure.title_en: Count your breaths and breathe with the model
measure.title_zh: 數一數呼吸，跟模型一起呼吸
measure.lead_en: Breathe normally; do not try to breathe faster or slower. It helps to have a partner count for you, because counting your own breaths tends to change them.
measure.lead_zh: 正常呼吸就好，不要刻意變快或變慢。請同伴幫你數會更準，因為自己數的時候，呼吸常常會不自覺地改變。

steps.en: Hand on belly
steps.zh: 手放肚子上
steps.text_en: Sit still with one hand on your belly and one on your chest. Which hand moves more when you breathe quietly?
steps.text_zh: 安靜坐好，一手放肚子、一手放胸口。安靜呼吸時，哪一隻手動得比較多？

steps.en: Count
steps.zh: 數一數
steps.text_en: Count how many times you breathe in during 30 seconds, then multiply by 2. The model does the math for you.
steps.text_zh: 數 30 秒內吸氣幾次，再乘以 2。模型會幫你算。

steps.en: Hold and let go
steps.zh: 按住、放開
steps.text_en: Press and hold the breathe-in button while you breathe in, and let go as you breathe out. Watch the diaphragm move with you.
steps.text_zh: 吸氣時按住「按住吸氣」，吐氣時放開，看橫膈膜跟著你動。

myths.myth_en: Your lungs suck in air by themselves.
myths.myth_zh: 肺會自己把空氣吸進來。
myths.fact_en: Lungs have no muscles to do that. The diaphragm and the muscles between your ribs make the chest bigger, and the air rushes in on its own.
myths.fact_zh: 肺沒有能做這件事的肌肉；是橫膈膜和肋間肌把胸腔撐大，空氣才自己湧進來。

myths.myth_en: We breathe in oxygen and breathe out only carbon dioxide.
myths.myth_zh: 我們吸進氧氣，吐出來的全是二氧化碳。
myths.fact_en: Breathed-out air is still about 16 percent oxygen and only about 4 percent carbon dioxide. That leftover oxygen is why rescue breaths can help someone who has stopped breathing.
myths.fact_zh: 吐出來的空氣仍有約 16% 是氧氣，二氧化碳只有約 4%。正因為還剩下這些氧氣，人工呼吸才救得了停止呼吸的人。

myths.myth_en: Your two lungs are exactly the same.
myths.myth_zh: 左右兩片肺一模一樣。
myths.fact_en: The right lung has three sections, called lobes, and the left lung has two. The left one is a little smaller, with a notch that makes room for the heart.
myths.fact_zh: 右肺分成三葉，左肺只有兩葉。左肺稍微小一點，還有一個凹口讓出位置給心臟。

myths.myth_en: We yawn because our body needs more oxygen.
myths.myth_zh: 打哈欠是因為身體缺氧。
myths.fact_en: Scientists are still studying why we yawn. In experiments, people who breathed extra oxygen yawned just as often, so a lack of oxygen is probably not the reason.
myths.fact_zh: 科學家還在研究人為什麼會打哈欠。實驗中，多吸氧氣的人打哈欠的次數並沒有變少，所以缺氧大概不是原因。

tricks.body_en: Down and in, up and out. The diaphragm moves one way, and the air moves to match.
tricks.body_zh: 往下就吸進、往上就吐出：橫膈膜往哪邊動，空氣就跟著配合。

tricks.body_en: Trunk = trachea, big branches = bronchi, twigs = bronchioles, and the leaves = the alveoli, where the real work happens.
tricks.body_zh: 樹幹＝氣管，大樹枝＝支氣管，細枝＝細支氣管，葉子＝真正在工作的肺泡。

tricks.body_en: The right lung has three lobes and the left has two, because the heart takes up room on the left.
tricks.body_zh: 右肺三葉、左肺兩葉，因為心臟在左邊占了位置。

tricks.body_en: Your nose is a filter, a heater, and a humidifier all in one. Your mouth is none of them.
tricks.body_zh: 鼻子同時是濾網、暖氣和加濕器；嘴巴三樣都不是。

materials.en: A small plastic bottle with the bottom cut off (an adult should do the cutting)
materials.zh: 一個剪掉底部的小寶特瓶（請大人剪）

materials.en: A small balloon (the lung)
materials.zh: 一顆小氣球（肺）

materials.en: A large balloon cut in half, or a piece of a rubber glove (the diaphragm)
materials.zh: 剪成一半的大氣球，或一片橡膠手套（橫膈膜）

materials.en: A rubber band and tape
materials.zh: 橡皮筋和膠帶

steps.en: Push the small balloon into the bottle and stretch its mouth over the bottle's neck.
steps.zh: 把小氣球塞進瓶子裡，氣球口反套在瓶口上。

steps.en: Stretch the cut balloon or glove over the open bottom and hold it with the rubber band. Tie a knot or tape a tab in the middle to pull on.
steps.zh: 把剪開的氣球或手套撐開套住瓶底，用橡皮筋固定；在中間打個結或貼一小段膠帶當把手。

steps.en: Gently pull the bottom sheet down. What happens to the balloon inside?
steps.zh: 輕輕把底部的膜往下拉。裡面的氣球怎麼了？

steps.en: Let it go. What happens now? Which part of your body is the bottom sheet?
steps.zh: 放開。現在又怎麼了？瓶底那片膜代表身體的哪個部位？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: nobody blows into the balloon, yet it fills. That is the big idea of the lesson: the lungs are filled by the space around them getting bigger. Compare with the diaphragm in the 3D model.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：沒有人對著氣球吹氣，它卻鼓起來了——這正是本課的大觀念：肺是因為周圍的空間變大才被撐滿的。對照 3D 模型裡的橫膈膜看看。

materials.en: A new balloon for each student (never share)
materials.zh: 每人一顆新氣球（不可共用）

materials.en: A tape measure or a piece of string and a ruler
materials.zh: 捲尺，或一條棉線加一把尺

materials.en: A worksheet
materials.zh: 學習單

steps.en: Take a normal breath, then blow it all into the balloon in one go. Pinch it closed and measure around the widest part.
steps.zh: 正常吸一口氣，一口氣全部吹進氣球，捏住氣球口，量最寬處的圓周。

steps.en: Let the air out. Now take the deepest breath you can and blow it all in. Measure again.
steps.zh: 把氣放掉。這次盡量深吸一口氣，全部吹進去，再量一次。

steps.en: Compare the two numbers. How much bigger is a deep breath than a normal one?
steps.zh: 比較兩個數字：深呼吸比平常的一口氣大了多少？

steps.en: Discuss: when might your body need those deep breaths?
steps.zh: 討論：什麼時候身體會需要這麼深的呼吸？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: a quiet breath for an adult is about half a liter, and the deepest breath can be several liters. Stop anyone who feels dizzy, and check for latex allergies first.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：成人安靜時一口氣大約半公升，最深的一口氣可以到好幾公升。有人覺得頭暈就停下來；活動前先確認有沒有乳膠過敏。

culture.title_en: Out-In: The Chinese Word for Breathing
culture.body_en: English says “breathe in and out,” but the Chinese word 呼吸 (hūxī) puts them the other way around: 呼 means to breathe out, and 吸 means to breathe in. The word 氣 (qì) means air and breath in everyday Chinese, as in 一口氣, “one breath,” and 深呼吸, “take a deep breath,” and it is also the qi of traditional Chinese medicine. The phrase 上氣不接下氣, “the upper breath does not meet the lower breath,” describes someone gasping for air after running.
culture.body_zh: 英文說 breathe in and out（先吸再吐），中文的「呼吸」卻反過來：「呼」是吐氣，「吸」是吸氣。「氣」在日常中文裡就是空氣和氣息，例如「一口氣」「深呼吸」，也是中醫講的「氣」。「上氣不接下氣」則是形容跑完步喘不過氣的樣子。
culture.link_en: Read about qi in the TCM series
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列讀「氣」

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If you have trouble breathing, your chest feels tight, or your lips look blue, tell an adult right away. Never play breath-holding games or breathe very fast on purpose; both can make people faint.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果呼吸困難、胸口悶，或嘴唇發紫，請馬上告訴大人。不要玩憋氣比賽，也不要故意快速呼吸，兩者都可能讓人昏倒。

lessons.title: How Do Your Joints Move?
lessons.blurb_en: A knee swings like a door, but a shoulder can draw a circle. Move six real joints in 3D, then measure how far your own joints bend.
lessons.blurb_zh: 膝蓋像門一樣擺動，肩膀卻能畫圓。在 3D 骨架上動動六個真實的關節，再量一量自己的關節能彎多少。
lessons.big_idea_en: A joint is a place where bones meet. Its shape decides how it moves: a hinge swings one way, a ball in a socket turns every way, and a pivot twists.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 關節是骨頭相接的地方，它的形狀決定它怎麼動：鉸鏈只往一個方向擺，球窩往哪裡都能轉，樞軸則是扭轉。

lab.how_en: Pick a joint below the model. The bones that move turn gold, and the shaded fan shows how far that joint can usually go. Drag the sliders: a hinge has one, a ball-and-socket has three. Then press the circle button. Which joints can draw a circle, and which can only swing back and forth?
lab.how_zh: 在模型下方選一個關節。會動的骨頭變成金色，淡淡的扇形是這個關節一般能動的範圍。拖動滑桿：鉸鏈關節只有一條，球窩關節有三條。再按「畫圓圈」：哪些關節畫得出圓，哪些只能來回擺？

legend.en: Gold bones: the part that moves at this joint
legend.zh: 金色骨頭：這個關節帶動的部分

legend.en: Shaded fan: the usual range of motion for an adult
legend.zh: 淡色扇形：成人一般的活動範圍

legend.en: Blue line: the path the end of the bone traces
legend.zh: 藍線：骨頭末端走過的路徑

lab.scale_en: The bones are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1. The ranges are typical adult numbers; everyone is a little different. In a real body, raising your arm high also turns your shoulder blade, and turning your head uses all seven neck bones, not just the top two. The model simplifies both.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架。活動範圍是成人常見的數字，每個人都有點不同。真實的身體裡，手臂舉高時肩胛骨也會跟著轉，轉頭則會用到全部七節頸椎，不只最上面兩節；模型把這兩件事簡化了。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, turned the model upright, and set the joint movements. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀、轉正方向並設定關節動作。

paras: Try walking across the room without bending your knees. You will waddle like a penguin. Now try eating lunch without bending your elbows. Every time you move, bones change their angle at places where two bones meet. These places are called joints, and your body has several hundred of them, from your jaw to your smallest toe.

Not every joint moves. The bones of your skull are joined by wavy seams called sutures, which lock them together like puzzle pieces to protect your brain. A newborn baby's skull still has soft spots between the bones so that the head can grow, but they close by about the age of two. The joints between the bones of your spine move only a little each, but together they let you bend and twist. The joints that move the most are in your arms and legs.

Inside a moving joint, the ends of the bones never grind against each other. Each end is covered with cartilage, a smooth, rubbery layer that is more slippery than ice sliding on ice. The whole joint is wrapped in a capsule filled with a little slippery liquid called synovial fluid, which works like oil in a machine. Strong straps called ligaments hold the bones together, so they can move without coming apart.

The shape of a joint decides how it moves. Your knee and elbow are hinge joints: like a door, they swing one way and back. Your shoulder and hip are ball-and-socket joints: a round ball at the top of the arm or thigh bone sits in a cup, so the limb can swing forward, backward, out to the side, and even in a circle. At the top of your neck, a pivot joint lets your head turn to say “no.” And at the base of your thumb is a saddle joint, which rocks two ways and lets your thumb touch the tip of every other finger.

There is always a trade-off between freedom and strength. Your shoulder has a shallow cup, which gives it the widest range of any joint in the body, but it is also the large joint that most often slips out of place. Your hip has a deep cup that holds the ball tightly. It cannot move as freely, but it can carry your whole weight when you run and jump. Your knee, the largest joint in the body, has two rubbery cushions inside and several strong ligaments to keep it steady.

Joints stay healthy when you use them. Moving squeezes fluid in and out of the cartilage, which keeps it fed, and strong muscles around a joint help protect it. Warm up before sports, and never force a joint past where it wants to go. And the popping sound when someone cracks their knuckles? It is a tiny gas bubble forming in the joint fluid. Now make a simple tool to measure how far your own joints can bend.
paras_zh: 試試看不彎膝蓋走過教室，你會像企鵝一樣搖搖擺擺。再試試看不彎手肘吃午餐。你每動一下，骨頭都會在兩塊骨頭相接的地方改變角度。這些地方叫做關節，從下巴到最小的腳趾，你全身有好幾百個關節。
不是每個關節都會動。頭顱骨之間由彎彎曲曲的接縫——骨縫——連在一起，像拼圖一樣卡緊，保護大腦。新生兒的頭顱骨之間還有軟軟的囟門，讓頭可以長大，但大約兩歲就會閉合。脊椎骨之間的關節每一節只能動一點點，合起來卻讓你能彎腰、扭身。動得最多的關節，在手臂和腿上。
在會動的關節裡，骨頭的末端從來不會直接互相磨擦。每個末端都包著一層軟骨，光滑又有彈性，比冰在冰上滑還要滑。整個關節外面包著一層關節囊，裡面有一點點滑滑的液體，叫做滑液，作用就像機器裡的潤滑油。強韌的帶子——韌帶——把骨頭綁在一起，讓它們能動卻不會分開。
關節的形狀決定它怎麼動。膝蓋和手肘是鉸鏈關節：像一扇門，只能往一個方向擺、再擺回來。肩膀和髖部是球窩關節：手臂或大腿骨頂端的圓球卡在一個杯狀的窩裡，所以四肢可以往前、往後、往旁邊擺，甚至畫圓。頸部頂端有一個樞軸關節，讓你能轉頭說「不」。拇指根部則是鞍狀關節，可以朝兩個方向搖，讓拇指碰得到其他每一根手指的指尖。
自由和穩固之間，總是要取捨。肩膀的窩很淺，讓它成為全身活動範圍最大的關節，但它也是最常脫臼的大關節。髖關節的窩很深，把球緊緊包住；它不能動得那麼自由，卻能在你跑跳時撐起全身的重量。膝蓋是全身最大的關節，裡面有兩塊有彈性的軟墊，還有好幾條強韌的韌帶讓它保持穩定。
關節要常常用才會健康。活動會把液體擠進、擠出軟骨，為它帶來養分；關節周圍強壯的肌肉也能保護它。運動前要暖身，也絕對不要硬把關節扳到超過它能到的地方。那折手指時的「啪」一聲呢？那是關節液裡形成的一個小小氣泡。現在做一個簡單的工具，量一量你自己的關節能彎多少度。
questions: Why do the bones in a moving joint not grind against each other?
What is the difference between how a hinge joint and a ball-and-socket joint move?
Why can the hip carry more weight than the shoulder, even though the shoulder moves more freely?
answers: The ends of the bones are covered with smooth, slippery cartilage, and the joint is filled with synovial fluid that works like oil.
A hinge joint swings in only one direction and back, like a door. A ball-and-socket joint can move in every direction, even in a circle.
The hip has a deep cup that holds the ball tightly, so it is strong and stable. The shoulder has a shallow cup, which lets it move more but makes it less stable.

vocab.ex: The door squeaks because its hinge needs oil.
vocab.exzh: 門會吱吱叫，是因為鉸鏈需要上油。

vocab.ex: Plug the lamp into the socket on the wall.
vocab.exzh: 把檯燈插進牆上的插座。

vocab.ex: The tip of your nose is made of cartilage, not bone.
vocab.exzh: 鼻尖是軟骨做的，不是骨頭。

vocab.ex: She hurt a ligament in her ankle during the game.
vocab.exzh: 她在比賽中弄傷了腳踝的韌帶。

vocab.ex: Gymnasts are very flexible and can touch their toes easily.
vocab.exzh: 體操選手非常柔軟，可以輕鬆碰到腳趾。

vocab.ex: Earth rotates once every day.
vocab.exzh: 地球每天自轉一圈。

vocab.ex: This shop sells a wide range of fruit.
vocab.exzh: 這家店賣各式各樣的水果。

vocab.ex: Be careful: the floor is slippery after it rains.
vocab.exzh: 小心，下雨後地板很滑。
