kinds_head.eyebrow: Inside Your Skin · 皮膚的構造
kinds_head.zh: 三層皮膚和它們的幫手

kinds.where_en: The thin top layer
kinds.text_en: Flat, dead cells on the outside flake off all the time. Pigment cells at its base make melanin.
kinds.text_zh: 外面扁平的死細胞一直在剝落；底部的色素細胞製造黑色素。

kinds.where_en: The thick middle layer
kinds.text_en: Holds blood vessels, nerves, sweat glands, and hair roots, all packed into stretchy fibers.
kinds.text_zh: 有彈性的纖維裡，塞滿了血管、神經、汗腺和毛髮的根。

kinds.where_en: The bottom layer
kinds.text_en: Soft fat cushions bumps, keeps you warm, and stores energy.
kinds.text_zh: 軟軟的脂肪緩衝撞擊、保暖，還能儲存能量。

kinds.where_en: Coiled tubes deep in the dermis
kinds.where_zh: 真皮深處捲起來的小管子
kinds.text_en: Two to four million of them. Sweat cools you as it evaporates from your skin.
kinds.text_zh: 有兩百萬到四百萬個。汗水從皮膚蒸發時幫你降溫。

kinds.where_en: All through the skin
kinds.text_en: Different sensors feel light touch, pressure, heat, cold, itching, and pain. Fingertips have the most.
kinds.text_zh: 不同的感受器分別感覺輕觸、壓力、熱、冷、癢和痛；指尖最多。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a house: the epidermis is the roof, the dermis is the walls with all the pipes and wires inside, and the fat layer is the insulation under the floor.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把皮膚想成一棟房子：表皮是屋頂，真皮是牆壁，裡面藏著水管和電線，皮下脂肪則是地板下的隔熱層。

measure.lead_en: The sun tool below the model works out how high the sun is over Changhua at any time today and estimates the UV index for a clear sky. Then go outside and check with your own shadow.
measure.lead_zh: 模型下方的太陽小工具會算出今天任何時刻太陽在彰化有多高，並估算晴天的紫外線指數。再到戶外用自己的影子確認一下。

steps.en: Check the number
steps.zh: 看看指數
steps.text_en: Look at today's UV index chart. Find the hours when it is 3 or higher: those are the hours when you need protection.
steps.text_zh: 看今天的紫外線指數圖，找出指數 3 以上的時段：那些時候就需要防護。

steps.en: Measure your shadow
steps.zh: 量量你的影子
steps.text_en: At recess, stand in the sun and have a partner mark the end of your shadow. If your shadow is shorter than you are tall, the sun is strong.
steps.text_zh: 下課時站在太陽下，請同伴在你影子的尾端做記號。如果影子比你的身高短，太陽就很強。

steps.en: Compare
steps.zh: 比一比
steps.text_en: Compare with the UV forecast from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. Clouds and haze usually make the real number lower than our clear-sky estimate.
steps.text_zh: 和中央氣象署的紫外線預報比一比。有雲或霾的時候，實際的數字通常比我們估算的晴天數字低。

myths.myth_en: You can't get sunburned on a cloudy day.
myths.myth_zh: 陰天不會曬傷。
myths.fact_en: Most UV passes through light clouds. You can get burned on a cloudy day, especially around noon in summer.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分的紫外線能穿過薄雲。陰天一樣會曬傷，尤其是夏天的中午前後。

myths.myth_en: A tan means your skin is healthy.
myths.myth_zh: 曬黑代表皮膚很健康。
myths.fact_en: A tan is your skin's way of protecting itself after UV has already damaged it.
myths.fact_zh: 曬黑是皮膚在被紫外線傷害之後，努力保護自己的結果。

myths.myth_en: Sweat itself smells bad.
myths.myth_zh: 汗本身就很臭。
myths.fact_en: Fresh sweat has almost no smell. The smell comes from bacteria on your skin breaking the sweat down.
myths.fact_zh: 剛流出來的汗幾乎沒有味道；臭味是皮膚上的細菌分解汗水產生的。

myths.myth_en: Goosebumps keep people warm.
myths.myth_zh: 雞皮疙瘩能讓人保暖。
myths.fact_en: In furry animals, raised fur traps a layer of warm air. People have so little body hair that goosebumps help only a little.
myths.fact_zh: 毛很多的動物把毛豎起來，可以留住一層暖空氣；人的體毛太少，雞皮疙瘩只能幫一點點忙。

tricks.body_en: If your shadow is shorter than you are, the sun is high and its UV is strong.
tricks.body_zh: 影子比身高短，表示太陽很高，紫外線很強。

tricks.body_en: A famous sun-safety rule from Australia: slip on a shirt, slop on sunscreen, slap on a hat.
tricks.body_zh: 澳洲有名的防曬口號：穿上衣服、擦上防曬乳、戴上帽子。

tricks.body_en: The epidermis sits on top of the dermis. Derma is Greek for skin.
tricks.body_zh: epidermis（表皮）在 dermis（真皮）的上面；derma 是希臘文的「皮膚」。

tricks.body_en: Sweat cools you only when it evaporates. Dripping sweat that just falls off does not help much.
tricks.body_zh: 汗水要蒸發才會帶走熱；直接滴下來的汗幫助不大。

materials.en: A soft pencil and a sheet of paper
materials.zh: 一支軟芯鉛筆和一張紙

materials.en: Clear tape and a magnifying glass
materials.zh: 透明膠帶和一個放大鏡

steps.en: Rub the pencil hard on the paper to make a dark patch.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆在紙上用力塗出一塊黑黑的區域。

steps.en: Rub your fingertip on the patch, then press a piece of tape onto your fingertip.
steps.zh: 用指尖在黑色區域上抹一抹，再把一段膠帶貼在指尖上。

steps.en: Peel off the tape and stick it on white paper. Look at it with the magnifying glass.
steps.zh: 把膠帶撕下來貼在白紙上，用放大鏡看。

steps.en: Is it a loop, a whorl, or an arch? Count each kind in the class.
steps.zh: 它是箕形、斗形還是弓形？統計全班每種各有幾個。

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: loops are the most common pattern, then whorls, and arches are the rarest. Even identical twins have different fingerprints, because tiny differences in the womb shape the ridges.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：箕形最常見，其次是斗形，弓形最少。連同卵雙胞胎的指紋都不一樣，因為在媽媽肚子裡的小小差異，就會影響紋路的形成。

materials.en: Two thermometers, or just your two hands
materials.zh: 兩支溫度計，或直接用兩隻手

materials.en: A wet paper towel and a fan or a piece of cardboard
materials.zh: 一張濕紙巾，以及電風扇或一塊紙板

steps.en: Wrap a wet paper towel around the end of one thermometer. Leave the other one dry.
steps.zh: 用濕紙巾包住一支溫度計的末端，另一支保持乾的。

steps.en: Fan both thermometers for three minutes.
steps.zh: 對兩支溫度計搧風三分鐘。

steps.en: Read both temperatures. Which one is cooler?
steps.zh: 讀出兩支的溫度，哪一支比較低？

steps.en: No thermometers? Wet the back of one hand, then blow on both hands. Which feels cooler?
steps.zh: 沒有溫度計？把一隻手的手背弄濕，再對兩隻手吹氣，哪一隻覺得比較涼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the wet one cools down because evaporating water carries heat away, just like sweat. On a humid day, sweat evaporates slowly, which is why sticky summer days in Taiwan feel so hot.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：濕的那一支溫度比較低，因為水蒸發時把熱帶走，就像汗水一樣。潮濕的日子汗水不容易蒸發，所以台灣悶熱的夏天特別難受。

culture.body_en: English says goosebumps, and Chinese says 雞皮疙瘩 (jīpí gēda), “chicken-skin bumps.” Both languages compared our cold skin to a plucked bird. The classic 《孝經》 (Classic of Filial Piety) begins with a line many Taiwanese students know: 身體髮膚，受之父母 (shēntǐ fàfū, shòu zhī fùmǔ), “your body, hair, and skin come from your parents,” so taking care of them is the first way to show respect. Hats and sunscreen count!
culture.body_zh: 英文說 goosebumps（鵝的疙瘩），中文說「雞皮疙瘩」：兩種語言都把冷到起疙瘩的皮膚，比作拔了毛的鳥。《孝經》開頭有一句很多台灣學生都背過：「身體髮膚，受之父母，不敢毀傷，孝之始也。」好好照顧自己的身體和皮膚，就是孝順的開始——戴帽子、擦防曬也算喔！
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Use shade, hats, and sunscreen when the UV index is 3 or higher. If a sunburn blisters, a rash spreads, a cut gets red, hot, and swollen, or a mole changes shape or color, tell an adult.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。紫外線指數 3 以上時，要找陰涼處、戴帽子、擦防曬乳。如果曬傷起水泡、疹子越來越大、傷口又紅又熱又腫，或痣的形狀、顏色改變，請告訴大人。

lessons.title: Why Do We Get Two Sets of Teeth?
lessons.blurb_en: Baby teeth hold the place while adult teeth grow inside your jaw. Slide from age 3 to 20 and watch them trade places, then count your own teeth.
lessons.blurb_zh: 乳牙先占位置，恆牙在頷骨裡慢慢長。把年齡從 3 歲拉到 20 歲，看它們換班，再數數你自己的牙。
lessons.big_idea_en: Baby teeth hold the place while adult teeth grow inside your jaw. From about age 6 to 12, twenty baby teeth fall out and up to thirty-two adult teeth take over, and you only get one adult set.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 乳牙先占位置，恆牙在頷骨裡長大。大約 6 到 12 歲，20 顆乳牙一顆顆掉，最多 32 顆恆牙接班，而恆牙只有這一套。

lab.how_en: Slide the age from 3 to 20. White baby teeth fall out one by one, while ivory adult teeth climb up out of the jaw bone to take their place, and the big molars arrive at the back. Tap any tooth to see its name and when it usually comes in. Then use the tooth chart below the model to count your own teeth.
lab.how_zh: 把年齡從 3 歲拉到 20 歲：白色的乳牙一顆顆掉落，象牙色的恆牙從頷骨裡往上長出來接班，後面的大臼齒也一顆顆報到。點任何一顆牙，看它的名字和大約幾歲長出來。再用模型下方的牙齒圖，數數你自己的牙。

legend.en: Bright white: baby teeth
legend.zh: 亮白色：乳牙

legend.en: Ivory: adult teeth
legend.zh: 象牙色：恆牙

legend.en: Pale: adult teeth still waiting inside the bone
legend.zh: 淡淡的：還在骨頭裡等待的恆牙

legend.en: Gold: the tooth you picked
legend.zh: 金色：你點選的牙

lab.scale_en: The skull and jaws are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1, which has no teeth; the teeth are our own drawing, at about life size. Every child is different: the ages in the model are typical averages from dental charts, and a year or two early or late is normal. The jaw itself also grows a lot during childhood, which the model does not show.
lab.scale_zh: 頭骨和上下頷骨是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架（資料裡沒有牙齒）；牙齒是本站自繪，大約是真實大小。每個孩子都不一樣：模型用的是牙科資料上的平均年齡，早一兩年或晚一兩年都很正常。真實的頷骨在成長過程中也會長大很多，模型沒有畫出來。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the teeth are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，牙齒為本站自繪示意。

paras: Smile in a mirror and count your teeth. Most children have all 20 of their baby teeth by about age 3. Starting around age 6, the baby teeth fall out one by one, and adult teeth take their place. By about age 12 or 13, most children have lost all of their baby teeth. An adult can have up to 32 teeth, but there is no third set. Adult teeth have to last for the rest of your life.

Baby teeth are not just for practice. They help you chew and speak clearly, and they hold space in your jaw for the adult teeth. The adult teeth have been growing inside your jaw bone for years, right under the baby teeth. As an adult tooth moves up, the roots of the baby tooth above it slowly melt away. That is why a loose baby tooth has almost no root when it finally falls out.

Different teeth do different jobs. The flat incisors at the front bite and cut, like scissors. The pointed canines next to them grip and tear. The premolars and molars at the back have wide, bumpy tops for grinding food into a mash. Your first adult molars come in around age 6, behind the baby teeth, without pushing any baby tooth out, so many people do not even notice them. They are called six-year molars.

A tooth has layers. The outside is enamel, the hardest substance in your body. Under it is dentin, which is softer and a little yellow, and in the center is the pulp, which has nerves and blood vessels. The roots hold the tooth tightly in the jaw bone. Teeth are hard like bones, but they are not bones: a broken bone can heal, but enamel cannot grow back, so a hole in a tooth stays a hole until a dentist fills it.

Cavities start with bacteria that live on your teeth in a sticky film called plaque. When you eat sugar, the bacteria eat it too and make acid, which slowly dissolves the enamel. If the hole reaches the dentin and then the pulp, the tooth can really hurt. Fluoride helps enamel stay strong and can even repair the very earliest damage, which is why most toothpaste has fluoride in it.

Brush for two minutes, twice a day, with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between your teeth. In Taiwan, elementary students rinse with a fluoride mouthwash at school once a week, and first and second graders can get sealants: a thin coating that fills the deep grooves of the six-year molars, where food likes to hide. Eat fewer sweets and sugary drinks, and see a dentist every six months. Now count your own teeth with the tooth chart below the model.
paras_zh: 對著鏡子笑一笑，數數你的牙齒。大多數孩子大約 3 歲時就長齊 20 顆乳牙。從 6 歲左右開始，乳牙一顆顆掉落，恆牙接著長出來。大約 12、13 歲時，多數孩子的乳牙都換完了。大人最多可以有 32 顆牙，但是沒有第三套：恆牙要用一輩子。
乳牙可不只是拿來練習的。它們幫你咀嚼、讓你說話清楚，還在頷骨裡幫恆牙保留位置。恆牙早就在頷骨裡長了好幾年，就在乳牙的正下方。恆牙往上移動時，上面那顆乳牙的牙根會慢慢被吸收掉，所以搖搖欲墜的乳牙掉下來時，幾乎已經沒有牙根了。
不同的牙齒做不同的工作。前面扁扁的門牙負責咬斷、切開，像剪刀一樣；旁邊尖尖的犬齒負責抓住、撕開；後面的小臼齒和大臼齒頂端寬寬的、凹凸不平，負責把食物磨碎。第一顆恆牙大臼齒大約 6 歲時長在乳牙的後面，不會把任何乳牙推掉，所以很多人根本沒注意到它，大家叫它「六歲臼齒」。
牙齒是一層一層的。最外面是琺瑯質，是全身最堅硬的物質；下面是比較軟、帶點黃色的象牙質；中間是牙髓，裡面有神經和血管。牙根把牙齒牢牢固定在頷骨裡。牙齒和骨頭一樣硬，但牙齒不是骨頭：骨頭斷了會癒合，琺瑯質卻長不回來，所以牙齒上的洞會一直是個洞，直到牙醫把它補起來。
蛀牙是從住在牙齒上的細菌開始的，它們藏在一層黏黏的薄膜裡，叫做牙菌斑。你吃糖的時候，細菌也跟著吃，並且產生酸，酸會慢慢溶解琺瑯質。洞如果深到象牙質、再到牙髓，牙齒就會很痛。氟能讓琺瑯質保持堅固，甚至能修補最早期的損傷，所以大部分的牙膏都含氟。
每天刷牙兩次、每次兩分鐘，使用含氟牙膏，也要清潔牙縫。在台灣，國小學生每週在學校用含氟漱口水漱口一次，一、二年級的學生還可以做窩溝封填：用一層薄薄的材料填平六歲臼齒上深深的溝，那裡最容易卡食物。少吃甜食、少喝含糖飲料，每六個月看一次牙醫。現在用模型下方的牙齒圖，數數你自己的牙。
questions: Why are baby teeth important even though they fall out?
Why does a loose baby tooth have almost no root?
How do cavities form?
answers: They help you chew and speak clearly, and they hold space in the jaw for the adult teeth.
As the adult tooth underneath moves up, the roots of the baby tooth slowly melt away.
Bacteria in plaque eat sugar and make acid, and the acid slowly dissolves the enamel.

vocab.ex: My little sister lost her first tooth today.
vocab.exzh: 我妹妹今天掉了第一顆牙。

vocab.ex: A baby tooth gets loose before it falls out.
vocab.exzh: 乳牙掉下來之前會先鬆動。

vocab.ex: My front tooth is so loose that it wiggles.
vocab.exzh: 我的門牙鬆到會搖來搖去。

vocab.ex: Chew your food well before you swallow.
vocab.exzh: 吞下去之前，要把食物好好嚼碎。

vocab.ex: The dentist found a small cavity in my molar.
vocab.exzh: 牙醫在我的臼齒上發現一個小蛀洞。

vocab.ex: I brush my teeth after breakfast and before bed.
vocab.exzh: 我在早餐後和睡前刷牙。

vocab.ex: Enamel protects the outside of each tooth.
vocab.exzh: 琺瑯質保護每顆牙齒的外層。

vocab.ex: We visit the dentist every six months.
vocab.exzh: 我們每六個月去看一次牙醫。

What are the flat front teeth that bite and cut called?
What is the hardest substance in your body?

According to the reading, what do sealants do?
options: Fill the deep grooves of the molars

kinds_head.eyebrow: Kinds of Teeth · 牙齒的種類

kinds.where_en: At the very front
kinds.text_en: 8 in both the baby set and the adult set. They are usually the first teeth to fall out, around age 6 or 7.
kinds.text_zh: 乳牙和恆牙都是 8 顆；通常最先掉，大約 6、7 歲。

kinds.where_en: Next to the incisors
kinds.text_en: 4 in each set. Their roots are the longest of all your teeth.
kinds.text_zh: 每一套 4 顆；它們的牙根是所有牙齒裡最長的。

kinds.where_en: Between the canines and the molars
kinds.text_en: Adults only: 8 premolars grow in where the baby molars were, at about ages 10 to 12.
kinds.text_zh: 只有恆牙有：8 顆小臼齒大約 10 到 12 歲時，長在原本乳臼齒的位置。

kinds.where_en: At the back
kinds.text_en: The six-year molars come in behind the baby teeth, and the twelve-year molars come in behind those.
kinds.text_zh: 六歲臼齒長在乳牙後面，十二歲臼齒再長在它們後面。

kinds.where_en: The very last molars
kinds.text_en: Up to 4, coming in between about 17 and 25, if at all. Some people never get them.
kinds.text_zh: 最多 4 顆，大約 17 到 25 歲才長；有些人一輩子都沒有。

lessons.kinds_note_en: A baby set has 8 incisors, 4 canines, and 8 molars: 20 teeth. An adult set adds 8 premolars and 4 more molars, plus up to 4 wisdom teeth: up to 32.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 一套乳牙有 8 顆門牙、4 顆犬齒、8 顆臼齒，共 20 顆。恆牙多了 8 顆小臼齒和 4 顆大臼齒，再加上最多 4 顆智齒，最多 32 顆。

measure.title_en: Count your teeth and find your tooth age
measure.title_zh: 數一數牙齒，算出牙齒年齡
measure.lead_en: Use a mirror and the tooth chart below the model. Tap each spot to mark a baby tooth, an adult tooth, or a gap, and the chart works out about how old your teeth look.
measure.lead_zh: 準備一面鏡子，搭配模型下方的牙齒圖。點每個位置，標出乳牙、恆牙或空位，牙齒圖會算出你的牙齒大約像幾歲。

steps.en: Look in a mirror
steps.zh: 照鏡子
steps.text_en: Wash your hands, smile wide, and look at one side at a time. New adult front teeth are bigger and often have little bumps along the edge.
steps.text_zh: 先洗手，張大嘴笑，一次看一邊。剛長出來的恆牙門牙比較大，邊緣常常有小小的鋸齒。

steps.en: Tap the chart
steps.zh: 點牙齒圖
steps.text_en: Mark each spot as a baby tooth, an adult tooth, or a gap. Six-year molars are the big teeth right behind your baby molars.
steps.text_zh: 把每個位置標成乳牙、恆牙或空位。六歲臼齒就是乳臼齒後面那顆大大的牙。

steps.en: Find your tooth age
steps.zh: 算出牙齒年齡
steps.text_en: The chart compares your mouth with typical ages and shows that age in 3D. Every child is different, so being a year or two early or late is normal.
steps.text_zh: 牙齒圖會拿你的嘴巴和一般的年齡比較，並在 3D 模型裡顯示那個年齡。每個孩子都不一樣，早一兩年或晚一兩年都很正常。

myths.myth_en: Baby teeth don't matter, because they fall out anyway.
myths.myth_zh: 乳牙反正會掉，蛀了也沒關係。
myths.fact_en: Cavities in baby teeth can hurt and spread. Losing a baby tooth too early can let other teeth drift into the space the adult tooth needs.
myths.fact_zh: 乳牙蛀了一樣會痛，還可能越來越嚴重。乳牙太早掉，旁邊的牙會移過來，占掉恆牙需要的位置。

myths.myth_en: Sugar itself makes holes in your teeth.
myths.myth_zh: 糖本身會在牙齒上蛀出洞。
myths.fact_en: Bacteria eat the sugar and make acid, and the acid makes the holes. How often you snack matters as much as how much sugar you eat.
myths.fact_zh: 是細菌吃了糖產生酸，酸才把牙齒蛀出洞。多常吃零食，和吃了多少糖一樣重要。

myths.myth_en: Brushing harder cleans your teeth better.
myths.myth_zh: 刷牙越用力，牙齒越乾淨。
myths.fact_en: Scrubbing hard can hurt your gums and wear down your teeth. Gentle brushing for two minutes does the job.
myths.fact_zh: 太用力會傷到牙齦、磨損牙齒。輕輕地刷兩分鐘就夠了。

myths.myth_en: Teeth are bones.
myths.myth_zh: 牙齒是骨頭。
myths.fact_en: Teeth and bones are both hard and full of calcium, but teeth are not bones. A bone can heal itself; enamel cannot. That is why teeth are not counted in your 206 bones.
myths.fact_zh: 牙齒和骨頭都很硬、都有很多鈣，但牙齒不是骨頭：骨頭會自己癒合，琺瑯質不會。所以 206 塊骨頭裡沒有算牙齒。

tricks.body_en: Big new molars arrive at the back at about age 6 and again at about age 12.
tricks.body_zh: 大約 6 歲和 12 歲時，後面各長出一組新的大臼齒。

tricks.body_en: Incisors cut, canines grip, and molars grind.
tricks.body_zh: 門牙切、犬齒勾、臼齒磨。

tricks.body_en: Brush two times a day, for two minutes each time, and see the dentist two times a year.
tricks.body_zh: 一天刷兩次、每次刷兩分鐘、一年看兩次牙醫。

tricks.body_en: No sugar for the bacteria means no acid for your teeth.
tricks.body_zh: 不給細菌吃糖，牙齒就不會泡在酸裡。

materials.en: Three hard-boiled eggs and three clear cups
materials.zh: 三顆白煮蛋和三個透明杯子

materials.en: Water, white vinegar, and cola
materials.zh: 清水、白醋和可樂

steps.en: Put one egg in each cup. Cover one with water, one with vinegar, and one with cola.
steps.zh: 每個杯子放一顆蛋，分別倒入清水、白醋和可樂，淹過雞蛋。

steps.en: Watch the vinegar cup for a few minutes. What do you see on the shell?
steps.zh: 觀察白醋杯幾分鐘，蛋殼上出現了什麼？

steps.en: Leave the cups overnight, then take the eggs out and gently feel and look at each shell.
steps.zh: 放置一個晚上，再把蛋拿出來，輕輕摸摸看、仔細看看每個蛋殼。

steps.en: Try brushing the cola egg with a toothbrush and toothpaste. What comes off, and what does not?
steps.zh: 用牙刷和牙膏刷刷看可樂杯的蛋，什麼刷得掉、什麼刷不掉？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: eggshell is not enamel, but both are hard minerals made with calcium, and acid dissolves them. The bubbles in the vinegar show the shell breaking down. The cola egg shows both stains and acid. Remind students that teeth have saliva and fluoride to help them, but they still need brushing and fewer sugary drinks.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：蛋殼不是琺瑯質，但兩者都是含鈣的堅硬礦物，都會被酸溶解。白醋裡冒出的泡泡，就是蛋殼正在分解；可樂杯同時看得到染色和酸的作用。提醒學生：牙齒有口水和氟幫忙，但還是需要刷牙、少喝含糖飲料。

materials.en: Sticky notes or a tally chart on the board
materials.zh: 便利貼，或黑板上的劃記表

materials.en: The 3D model and the tooth chart on this page
materials.zh: 本頁的 3D 模型和牙齒圖

steps.en: Each student counts how many baby teeth they have lost so far.
steps.zh: 每位同學數一數自己到目前為止掉了幾顆乳牙。

steps.en: Make a bar graph: number of lost teeth across the bottom, number of students up the side.
steps.zh: 畫長條圖：橫軸是掉了幾顆牙，縱軸是有幾位同學。

steps.en: Set the 3D model to your class's age. How many baby teeth has it lost?
steps.zh: 把 3D 模型調到你們班的年齡，模型掉了幾顆乳牙？

steps.en: Is everyone the same? What is the most common number?
steps.zh: 每個人都一樣嗎？最常見的是幾顆？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the graph usually spreads out widely, which is a good way to show that a typical age is only an average. Be kind to students who have lost many teeth or none at all: both are normal.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：統計圖通常分布得很開，正好說明「一般的年齡」只是平均值。掉了很多顆或一顆都沒掉的同學都很正常，請溫和地對待。

culture.title_en: Up on the Roof, Down Under the Bed
culture.title_zh: 上牙丟床底，下牙丟屋頂
culture.body_en: In Taiwan, many families have a custom for a lost baby tooth: a lower tooth is thrown up onto the roof, and an upper tooth goes under the bed, so the new tooth will grow in the right direction, toward where the old one went. In many English-speaking countries, children put the tooth under their pillow, and the Tooth Fairy swaps it for a coin. And in Chinese, a wisdom tooth is 智齒 (zhìchǐ), just like in English: it comes in when you are old enough to be wise.
culture.body_zh: 在台灣，很多家庭對掉下來的乳牙有個習俗：下排的牙丟到屋頂上，上排的牙丟到床底下，希望新牙朝著舊牙去的方向，長得又快又直。在許多說英語的國家，孩子會把牙齒放在枕頭下，牙仙子（Tooth Fairy）會把它換成一枚硬幣。還有，中文的「智齒」和英文的 wisdom tooth 意思一樣：等你長到夠有智慧的年紀，它才會長出來。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If a tooth hurts, your gums bleed or swell, or a tooth gets knocked out, tell an adult right away. A knocked-out adult tooth can sometimes be saved if you see a dentist quickly.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果牙齒痛、牙齦流血或腫起來，或牙齒被撞掉，請馬上告訴大人。被撞掉的恆牙如果很快去看牙醫，有時還救得回來。

lessons.title: How Does Your Body Fight Germs?
lessons.blurb_en: Your body has three walls against germs, and it remembers every enemy it has beaten. Watch white blood cells chase bacteria through a tiny cut, and see why the second fight is so much faster.
lessons.blurb_zh: 身體有三道防線，而且記得每個打敗過的敵人。看白血球在一個小傷口裡追著細菌跑，再看看為什麼第二次交手快得多。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your body fights germs with three walls: skin and mucus keep most germs out, white blood cells attack the ones that get in, and your body remembers each germ so it can win faster next time. That memory is how vaccines work.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 身體用三道防線對抗病菌：皮膚和黏液擋住大部分，白血球攻擊闖進來的，身體還會記住每一種病菌，下次贏得更快——疫苗就是靠這份記憶。

lab.how_en: A paper cut on your fingertip, blown up 2,000 times. Slide the time forward: bacteria slip in and double, the area turns red and swollen, white blood cells squeeze out of a blood vessel to eat them, and Y-shaped antibodies finally tag every last one. Then switch to the second time the same germ shows up, and compare the two fights on the chart.
lab.how_zh: 指尖上一道被紙割到的小傷口，放大 2,000 倍。把時間往後拉：細菌溜進來、一變二、二變四，傷口附近又紅又腫，白血球從血管裡擠出來吃掉它們，最後 Y 字形的抗體把剩下的細菌全部標記起來。再切換到「第二次遇到同一種病菌」，在圖上比一比兩場仗。

legend.en: Green rods: bacteria
legend.zh: 綠色小棒：細菌

legend.en: Big pale cells: white blood cells
legend.zh: 大大的淡色細胞：白血球

legend.en: Red discs: red blood cells in a tiny blood vessel
legend.zh: 紅色圓盤：微血管裡的紅血球

legend.en: Gold Ys: antibodies
legend.zh: 金色的 Y：抗體

lab.scale_en: The hand bones are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1; the cut, the cells, and the germs are our own drawing, shown about 2,000 times bigger than life. The bacteria are drawn a little bigger than they really are so you can see them. Real cuts hold far more germs and cells, and the timeline is squeezed: hours at the start, days at the end. The two fights follow the typical pattern of a first and a second immune response.
lab.scale_zh: 手部骨頭是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架；傷口、細胞和病菌是本站自繪的示意圖，放大約 2,000 倍。細菌畫得比真實的大一點，方便看清楚。真實的傷口裡病菌和細胞多得多，時間軸也壓縮過：開頭以小時計，後面以天計。兩場仗依照第一次與第二次免疫反應的典型樣子。

We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the germs and cells are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，病菌與細胞為本站自繪示意。

paras: Germs are tiny living things, such as bacteria and viruses, that are too small to see. Most bacteria are harmless, and many, like the ones in your gut, even help you. But some can make you sick. Your body is attacked by germs every day, and it wins almost every time, usually without you noticing. It does this with three walls of defense.

The first wall keeps germs out. Your skin is a tough, dry barrier that most germs cannot get through. Your nose, mouth, and throat are lined with sticky mucus that traps germs, and tiny hairs sweep the mucus away so you can swallow or sneeze it out. Tears and saliva contain substances that kill bacteria, and your stomach is filled with strong acid. Germs get in mainly through cuts, or through your eyes, nose, and mouth, often from your own hands.

If germs get past the first wall, the second wall attacks right away. Bacteria can double every 20 minutes, so speed matters. Damaged cells send out alarm signals, and blood vessels nearby widen and leak fluid. That is why a cut turns red, warm, swollen, and sore. Then white blood cells squeeze out of the blood vessels and hunt the germs, swallowing them whole. A single drop of blood carries hundreds of thousands of white blood cells. A fever can help too, because many germs grow more slowly when your body is warmer.

The third wall is the smartest. Special white blood cells study the invader and make antibodies, Y-shaped proteins that fit only that one germ, like a key fits a lock. Antibodies stick to the germs, making them easier to catch and destroy. The first time your body meets a new germ, making the right antibodies can take a week or more, so you may feel sick for days.

But your body remembers. After the fight, memory cells stay on guard for years. If the same germ comes back, they make antibodies in a day or two, and the germ is often gone before you feel sick at all. Vaccines use this memory. A vaccine shows your body a harmless piece or a weakened form of a germ, so your body learns to recognize it without having to get sick first.

You can help your three walls. Wash your hands with soap for at least 20 seconds, especially before eating and after using the toilet. Cover coughs and sneezes with your elbow. Clean cuts and keep them covered. Sleep well and eat well, because a tired body fights germs less well. And remember that antibiotics kill bacteria but do nothing against viruses like colds and flu. Now try the germ calculator and the handwashing timer below the model.
paras_zh: 病菌是像細菌和病毒這樣的小生物，小到眼睛看不見。大部分細菌是無害的，很多甚至對你有幫助，例如腸道裡的細菌；但有些會讓你生病。你的身體每天都受到病菌攻擊，而且幾乎每次都贏，通常你根本沒發現。它靠的是三道防線。
第一道防線把病菌擋在外面。皮膚是一道堅韌、乾燥的屏障，大部分病菌穿不過去。鼻子、嘴巴和喉嚨裡有黏黏的黏液，能黏住病菌，細細的纖毛再把黏液掃走，讓你吞下去或打噴嚏噴出來。眼淚和口水裡有能殺死細菌的物質，胃裡則裝滿了強酸。病菌主要是從傷口，或從眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴進來，常常就是被自己的手帶進來的。
病菌如果闖過第一道防線，第二道防線馬上出動。細菌每 20 分鐘就能多一倍，所以速度很重要。受傷的細胞發出警報，附近的血管變寬、滲出液體，所以傷口會紅、熱、腫、痛。接著白血球從血管裡擠出來追捕病菌，把它們整個吞下去。一滴血裡就有幾十萬個白血球。發燒也能幫忙，因為很多病菌在體溫比較高時長得比較慢。
第三道防線最聰明。特別的白血球會研究入侵者，製造抗體：一種 Y 字形的蛋白質，只配得上那一種病菌，就像一把鑰匙只開一把鎖。抗體黏在病菌上，讓它們更容易被抓住、被消滅。身體第一次遇到新的病菌時，做出對的抗體可能要一個星期以上，所以你可能會不舒服好幾天。
但是身體會記得。打完這一仗，記憶細胞會守候好幾年。同一種病菌再來的時候，它們一兩天就能做出抗體，病菌常常在你感覺不舒服之前就被消滅了。疫苗就是利用這份記憶：疫苗讓身體看到病菌無害的一小部分，或是減弱過的病菌，讓身體不必先生病，就學會認出它。
你也可以幫助這三道防線。用肥皂洗手至少 20 秒，尤其是吃東西前和上完廁所後。咳嗽、打噴嚏時用手肘遮住。傷口要清潔，並且蓋好。睡飽、吃好，因為疲累的身體比較打不贏病菌。還要記得：抗生素能殺細菌，但對感冒、流感這些病毒完全沒用。現在試試模型下方的病菌計算機和洗手計時器。
questions: What are the three walls your body uses against germs?
Why does a cut turn red, warm, and swollen?
Why do you often not get sick the second time the same germ comes back?
answers: First, skin and mucus keep germs out. Second, white blood cells attack germs that get in. Third, antibodies target each germ, and the body remembers it.
Damaged cells send alarm signals, and nearby blood vessels widen and leak fluid so that white blood cells can get to the germs.
Memory cells remember the germ and make antibodies in a day or two, so the germ is gone before you feel sick.

vocab.ex: Wash your hands to get rid of germs.
vocab.exzh: 洗手可以把病菌洗掉。

vocab.ex: Some bacteria help us digest our food.
vocab.exzh: 有些細菌會幫助我們消化食物。

vocab.ex: A cold is caused by a virus.
vocab.exzh: 感冒是病毒引起的。

vocab.ex: Clean the cut so it doesn't get an infection.
vocab.exzh: 把傷口清乾淨，才不會感染。

vocab.ex: She stayed home because she had a fever.
vocab.exzh: 她發燒了，所以待在家裡。

vocab.ex: Cover your nose with your elbow when you sneeze.
vocab.exzh: 打噴嚏時用手肘遮住鼻子。

vocab.ex: Use soap and scrub for twenty seconds.
vocab.exzh: 用肥皂搓洗二十秒。

vocab.ex: The nurse gave us a flu vaccine at school.
vocab.exzh: 護理師在學校幫我們打了流感疫苗。

kinds_head.eyebrow: Three Walls of Defense · 三道防線

kinds.where_en: All over the outside
kinds.text_en: A tough, dry wall. Most germs get in only through cuts, so clean and cover them.
kinds.text_zh: 堅韌又乾燥的牆；大部分病菌只能從傷口進來，所以傷口要清潔、蓋好。

kinds.where_en: Nose, throat, eyes, and stomach
kinds.text_en: Sticky mucus traps germs, tears and saliva fight bacteria, and stomach acid destroys most germs you swallow.
kinds.text_zh: 黏液黏住病菌，眼淚和口水對抗細菌，胃酸消滅大部分吞下去的病菌。

kinds.where_en: Wherever germs get in
kinds.text_en: Red, warm, swollen, and sore: blood vessels open up so white blood cells can rush in.
kinds.text_zh: 紅、熱、腫、痛：血管打開，讓白血球趕過來。

kinds.where_en: In the blood, ready to leave it
kinds.where_zh: 在血液裡，隨時可以出動
kinds.text_en: Hundreds of thousands in each drop of blood. They squeeze out of blood vessels and swallow germs whole.
kinds.text_zh: 每一滴血裡有幾十萬個；它們從血管擠出來，把病菌整個吞下去。

kinds.where_en: Made by special white blood cells
kinds.text_en: Each antibody fits one germ like a key in a lock. Memory cells remember it for years.
kinds.text_zh: 每一種抗體只配一種病菌，像鑰匙配鎖；記憶細胞能記住它好幾年。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a castle: the walls and the moat keep enemies out, the guards attack anyone who climbs in, and the castle keeps a wanted poster for every enemy it has ever caught.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把身體想成一座城堡：城牆和護城河把敵人擋在外面，衛兵攻擊爬進來的人，城堡還為每個抓過的敵人貼了一張通緝令。

measure.title_zh: 病菌數學與 20 秒洗手
measure.lead_en: Use the calculator below the model to see how fast one bacterium can multiply, then wash your hands with the timer the way Taiwan's CDC teaches: wet, scrub, rinse, scoop, and dry.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的計算機，看一隻細菌能多快變多；再跟著計時器，照疾管署教的「濕、搓、沖、捧、擦」洗手。

steps.en: Do the germ math
steps.zh: 算一算病菌
steps.text_en: Start with one bacterium that doubles every 20 minutes. Slide the hours and watch the number grow. How long until there are more than the 23 million people in Taiwan?
steps.text_zh: 從一隻每 20 分鐘多一倍的細菌開始。拉動時間看數字變大：要多久才會比台灣的 2,300 萬人還多？

steps.en: Wash with the timer
steps.zh: 跟著計時器洗手
steps.text_en: At a sink, press start and follow the five steps. Scrub for the full 20 seconds: palms, backs, between fingers, fingertips, thumbs, and wrists.
steps.text_zh: 到洗手台按下開始，跟著五個步驟做。搓滿 20 秒：手心、手背、指縫、指尖、大拇指和手腕。

steps.en: Check with glitter
steps.zh: 用亮粉檢查
steps.text_en: In class, put a little glitter or flour on your hands, then wash. Any sparkles left show the spots you usually miss.
steps.text_zh: 在課堂上，手上沾一點亮粉或麵粉再洗；還留著亮亮的地方，就是你平常洗不到的地方。

measure.button_en: Try the germ calculator and timer
measure.button_zh: 試試病菌計算機和洗手計時器

myths.myth_en: All bacteria are bad for you.
myths.myth_zh: 細菌都是壞的。
myths.fact_en: Most bacteria are harmless, and trillions of helpful bacteria live in your gut, where they help digest food and crowd out harmful germs.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分細菌是無害的；腸道裡住著好幾兆個有益的細菌，幫忙消化食物，還把有害的病菌擠走。

myths.myth_en: Antibiotics cure colds.
myths.myth_zh: 抗生素能治感冒。
myths.fact_en: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics work only on bacteria. Taking them when they are not needed helps bacteria learn to resist them.
myths.fact_zh: 感冒是病毒引起的，抗生素只對細菌有效。不需要時吃抗生素，反而讓細菌學會抵抗它。

myths.myth_en: A fever is always bad and should be stopped.
myths.myth_zh: 發燒一定是壞事，要馬上退燒。
myths.fact_en: A fever is often part of how your body fights germs. A doctor or a parent decides when medicine is needed, especially if the fever is very high or lasts a long time.
myths.fact_zh: 發燒常常是身體對抗病菌的一部分。要不要吃藥由醫生或家長決定，尤其是燒得很高或燒很久的時候。

myths.myth_en: If you can't see dirt, your hands are clean.
myths.myth_zh: 手看起來不髒，就是乾淨的。
myths.fact_en: Germs are far too small to see. Clean-looking hands can still carry them, so wash before you eat and after using the toilet.
myths.fact_zh: 病菌小到看不見，看起來乾淨的手也可能帶著病菌；吃東西前、上完廁所後都要洗手。

tricks.body_en: Skin and mucus keep germs out, white blood cells eat them, and antibodies help your body remember them.
tricks.body_zh: 皮膚和黏液把病菌擋住，白血球把它們吃掉，抗體幫身體記住它們。

tricks.body_en: The four signs of inflammation mean your body is already fighting.
tricks.body_zh: 發炎的四個徵兆，表示身體已經開始作戰。

tricks.body_en: Wet, scrub for 20 seconds, rinse, scoop water to clean the tap, and dry: Taiwan's five steps for washing hands.
tricks.body_zh: 淋濕、搓 20 秒、沖乾淨、捧水洗水龍頭、擦乾：台灣的洗手五步驟。

tricks.body_en: Bacteria yes, viruses no. Colds and flu are viruses.
tricks.body_zh: 細菌有效，病毒沒用；感冒和流感都是病毒。

materials.en: A shallow plate of water and some ground black pepper
materials.zh: 一個裝水的淺盤和一些黑胡椒粉

materials.en: Liquid soap or dish soap
materials.zh: 洗手乳或洗碗精

steps.en: Sprinkle pepper all over the water. The pepper is the “germs.”
steps.zh: 把胡椒粉撒滿整個水面，胡椒粉就是「病菌」。

steps.en: Dip a clean finger into the middle. What happens?
steps.zh: 用乾淨的手指點一下中間，發生了什麼事？

steps.en: Now put a drop of soap on your fingertip and dip it in again.
steps.zh: 在指尖沾一滴肥皂，再點一次。

steps.en: Where did the pepper go? Why?
steps.zh: 胡椒粉跑到哪裡去了？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: soap breaks the surface tension of the water, so the pepper rushes away. In real handwashing, soap also breaks up oils on your skin and lifts germs off so the water can rinse them away. That is why rinsing with water alone is not enough.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：肥皂破壞了水的表面張力，所以胡椒粉一下子散開。真正洗手時，肥皂也會分解皮膚上的油脂，把病菌拉起來，讓水把它們沖走——所以只用清水沖是不夠的。

materials.en: A little glitter, flour, or washable paint
materials.zh: 一點亮粉、麵粉或可洗的顏料

materials.en: Soap, water, and paper towels
materials.zh: 肥皂、水和擦手紙

steps.en: One student puts a little glitter on one hand. That is the “germ.”
steps.zh: 一位同學在一隻手上沾一點亮粉，那就是「病菌」。

steps.en: Shake hands down a line of five or six students.
steps.zh: 沿著一排五、六位同學依序握手。

steps.en: Check everyone's hands, then their desks, pencils, and faces. Where did the glitter end up?
steps.zh: 檢查每個人的手，再看看桌子、鉛筆和臉：亮粉跑到哪裡去了？

steps.en: Everyone washes with soap. Who got it all off?
steps.zh: 大家用肥皂洗手，誰洗得最乾淨？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: germs travel the same way, and the last student in line still gets some. Ask how many students touched their face without noticing. Washable materials only, and keep glitter away from eyes.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：病菌就是這樣傳出去的，排到最後的同學一樣會沾到。問問大家有幾個人不知不覺摸了臉。請只用可以洗掉的材料，亮粉不要碰到眼睛。

culture.body_en: The Chinese word for immunity, 免疫 (miǎnyì), means “escaping the plague”: 免 is to avoid, and 疫 is an epidemic. English immunity comes from the Latin immunis, “free from a duty,” so an immune person was free from the sickness. The old saying 病從口入 (bìng cóng kǒu rù), “sickness comes in through the mouth,” is why Taiwanese students learn to wash their hands before every meal, and why the five steps 濕、搓、沖、捧、擦 are posted next to so many sinks.
culture.body_zh: 中文的「免疫」，意思是「免除疫病」：免是避開，疫是流行病。英文 immunity 來自拉丁文 immunis，「免除義務」，所以 immune 的人就是不必生那場病的人。老話說「病從口入」，所以台灣的學生從小就學會飯前洗手，很多洗手台旁邊也貼著「濕、搓、沖、捧、擦」五個字。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If a cut gets more red, hot, swollen, or painful, or if you have a high fever or feel very sick, tell an adult. Take medicine only when a doctor or a parent says so, and follow the vaccine advice of your doctor and school.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果傷口越來越紅、熱、腫、痛，或發高燒、覺得非常不舒服，請告訴大人。只在醫生或家長說可以的時候吃藥，打疫苗請依照醫生和學校的建議。

lessons.title: Where Does the Water You Drink Go?
lessons.blurb_en: Your two kidneys clean all of your blood about 30 times a day. Follow the water through real 3D kidneys, zoom into one tiny filter, and check whether you are drinking enough today.
lessons.blurb_zh: 兩顆腎臟每天把全身的血洗大約 30 遍。跟著水走過真實的 3D 腎臟，放大看一個小小的過濾器，再看看你今天水喝得夠不夠。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your kidneys are filters. They clean your blood again and again, keep the water and salt your body needs, and send the rest to your bladder as urine.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 腎臟是濾水器：一遍又一遍把血過濾乾淨，留下身體需要的水和鹽，把其餘的變成尿液送到膀胱。

lab.how_en: These are real kidneys, in their real place beside your backbone. Blood flows in, clean blood flows out, and drops of urine run down two thin tubes to the bladder. Slide how much water you drank and watch the urine change. Zoom into a nephron to see the three steps: filter, take back, flush. When the bladder is full, send your model to the restroom!
lab.how_zh: 這是真實的腎臟，就在脊柱兩旁真正的位置。血流進去、乾淨的血流出來，一滴滴尿液沿著兩條細管流到膀胱。拉動「喝了多少水」，看尿液怎麼變。放大一顆腎元，看三個步驟：過濾、回收、排出。膀胱滿了，就讓模型去上廁所吧！

legend.en: Red-brown: the real kidneys
legend.zh: 紅褐色：真實的腎臟

legend.en: Bright red: blood coming in from the heart
legend.zh: 鮮紅色：從心臟來的血

legend.en: Dark red: cleaned blood going back
legend.zh: 暗紅色：過濾後流回去的血

legend.en: Yellow: urine on its way to the bladder
legend.zh: 黃色：流向膀胱的尿液

legend.en: Blue dots in the nephron: water
legend.zh: 腎元裡的藍點：水

lab.scale_en: The bones, kidneys, ureters, and bladder are real shapes from BodyParts3D, in their real places; the blood vessels and the nephron are our own drawing. A real nephron is far too thin to see, and each kidney has about a million of them. Time is sped up: one second here is 20 minutes. The amounts are for a child of about 30 kilograms; an adult's kidneys filter about 140 liters of blood a day.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭、腎臟、輸尿管和膀胱是 BodyParts3D 的真實形狀，位置也是真的；血管和腎元是本站自繪的示意圖。真正的腎元細到看不見，每顆腎臟大約有一百萬個。時間加快了：這裡的 1 秒是 20 分鐘。數量以體重約 30 公斤的孩子估算；大人的腎臟一天大約過濾 140 公升的血。
lab.credit_html: Bone and organ models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, the kidneys, the ureters, and the bladder, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the blood vessels and the nephron are our own drawing. · 骨骼與器官模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、腎臟、輸尿管與膀胱，簡化形狀並轉正方向，血管與腎元為本站自繪示意。

paras: Take a sip of water. In a few minutes it will be in your blood, and within an hour or two, some of it will be on its way out again. Your body is about 60 percent water, and it has to keep that amount just right. The organs in charge are your two kidneys. They are shaped like beans, each about the size of your fist, and they sit on either side of your backbone, just under your lowest ribs. The right one sits a little lower, because your liver is above it.

Your kidneys are filters for your blood. As your cells work, they make waste, and the blood carries it away. About a fifth of the blood your heart pumps goes straight to the kidneys. In an adult, they filter about half a cup of blood every minute. That adds up to about 140 liters a day, which means all of your blood gets cleaned about 30 times every day.

The cleaning is done by tiny filters called nephrons, and each kidney has about a million of them. A nephron works in three steps. First, it filters: water, salt, sugar, and waste are pushed out of the blood, while blood cells are too big to get through. Second, it takes back: almost all of the water, and all of the sugar your body needs, return to the blood. Third, it flushes: the waste and the extra water that are left become urine.

From 140 liters of filtered blood, only 1 to 2 liters become urine. Urine drips down two thin tubes called ureters into the bladder, a stretchy bag that slowly fills like a balloon. When it is about half full, nerves tell your brain that it is time to find a restroom. Urine is yellow because of a pigment left over when old red blood cells are broken down.

Your kidneys also decide how much water to keep. If you drink a lot, they let more water go, and your urine is pale. If you have not had enough, they hold water back, and your urine turns dark yellow. So the color is a message from your kidneys: pale yellow means you are doing fine, and dark yellow means it is time to drink. You lose water in your sweat and your breath too, so you need more on hot days and when you exercise.

Kidneys work quietly, and people often do not notice a problem until it is serious. Taiwan has one of the highest rates of kidney failure in the world, often after years of diabetes or high blood pressure. You can look after your kidneys now. Drink water instead of sugary drinks: Taiwan's health agency says elementary students need at least 1,500 milliliters a day. Do not eat too much salt, and go to the restroom when you need to. Now count your cups with the water tracker below the model.
paras_zh: 喝一口水。幾分鐘後它就會進到你的血液裡，一兩個小時之內，其中一部分又要準備離開了。你的身體大約 60% 是水，而且必須把水量維持得剛剛好。負責這件事的器官是兩顆腎臟。它們的形狀像豆子，每顆大約和你的拳頭一樣大，位在脊柱兩旁、最下面幾根肋骨的下方。右邊那顆稍微低一點，因為它上面有肝臟。
腎臟是血液的過濾器。細胞工作時會產生廢物，由血液帶走。心臟打出來的血，大約有五分之一直接流向腎臟。大人的腎臟每分鐘大約過濾半杯血，一天加起來大約 140 公升，也就是說，你全身的血每天大約被洗 30 遍。
負責清洗的是很小的過濾器，叫做腎元，每顆腎臟大約有一百萬個。腎元的工作分成三步。第一步，過濾：水、鹽、糖和廢物被擠出血液，血球太大，過不去。第二步，回收：幾乎所有的水，以及身體需要的糖，全部回到血液裡。第三步，排出：剩下的廢物和多餘的水，就成了尿液。
140 公升過濾過的血，只有 1 到 2 公升變成尿液。尿液沿著兩條叫做輸尿管的細管，一滴滴流進膀胱。膀胱是一個有彈性的袋子，像氣球一樣慢慢裝滿。大約半滿的時候，神經會告訴大腦：該去找廁所了。尿液是黃色的，是因為老舊的紅血球被分解後留下了一種色素。
腎臟還會決定要留下多少水。水喝得多，腎臟就多放一些水出去，尿液顏色很淡；水喝得不夠，腎臟就把水留住，尿液變成深黃色。所以尿液的顏色是腎臟給你的訊息：淡黃色表示沒問題，深黃色表示該喝水了。流汗和呼吸也會讓你失去水分，所以天氣熱和運動的時候要喝更多。
腎臟默默工作，等到有感覺時，問題往往已經很嚴重了。台灣是全世界腎臟衰竭比率最高的地方之一，常常是多年的糖尿病或高血壓造成的。你現在就可以照顧自己的腎臟：喝白開水，不要喝含糖飲料——國民健康署說，國小學生每天至少要喝 1,500 毫升的水。不要吃太鹹，想上廁所就去上。現在用模型下方的喝水紀錄，數數你今天喝了幾杯。
questions: What are the three steps a nephron uses to clean the blood?
Why is only a small part of the filtered liquid turned into urine?
What does the color of your urine tell you?
answers: It filters water, salt, sugar, and waste out of the blood; it takes back the water and sugar the body needs; and it flushes the waste and extra water out as urine.
Because the nephrons take almost all of the water, and the things the body needs, back into the blood.
Pale yellow means you have had enough water. Dark yellow means your kidneys are holding water back, and you need to drink.

vocab.ex: You have two kidneys, one on each side of your backbone.
vocab.exzh: 你有兩顆腎臟，脊柱兩邊各一顆。

vocab.ex: This bottle filters the water before you drink it.
vocab.exzh: 這個水壺會先把水過濾，你再喝。

vocab.ex: Please put your waste in the right bin.
vocab.exzh: 請把垃圾丟進正確的桶子。

vocab.ex: The doctor asked for a sample of my urine.
vocab.exzh: 醫生請我留一份尿液檢體。

vocab.ex: My bladder is full. I need a restroom!
vocab.exzh: 我的膀胱滿了，我要上廁所！

vocab.ex: We were so thirsty after the race.
vocab.exzh: 賽跑之後我們好渴。

vocab.ex: Take a sip of water between classes.
vocab.exzh: 下課時喝一小口水。

vocab.ex: May I go to the restroom, please?
vocab.exzh: 請問我可以去上廁所嗎？

About how many nephrons does each kidney have?
Why can't blood cells pass through the filter in a nephron?
Where is urine stored before it leaves your body?
According to the reading, what does dark yellow urine mean?
options: You need to drink more water

kinds_head.eyebrow: Your Water System · 身體的排水系統

kinds.where_en: Beside your backbone, under the lowest ribs
kinds.where_zh: 脊柱兩旁、最下面的肋骨下方
kinds.text_en: Two bean-shaped filters, each about the size of your fist. You can live a healthy life with just one.
kinds.text_zh: 兩顆豆子形狀的過濾器，每顆大約和拳頭一樣大；只有一顆也能健康地生活。

kinds.where_en: About a million in each kidney
kinds.where_zh: 每顆腎臟大約一百萬個
kinds.text_en: Each one filters a little blood, returns the water and sugar you need, and sends the waste on.
kinds.text_zh: 每個腎元過濾一點點血，把需要的水和糖送回去，把廢物往下送。

kinds.where_en: From the body's main artery and back to its main vein
kinds.where_zh: 從主動脈來，回到大靜脈
kinds.text_en: About a fifth of the blood from every heartbeat goes to the kidneys.
kinds.text_zh: 每一下心跳打出的血，大約有五分之一流向腎臟。

kinds.where_en: One thin tube from each kidney
kinds.text_en: Each tube is about as long as a ruler. Their walls squeeze in waves, so urine goes down even if you are lying flat.
kinds.text_zh: 每條大約一把尺那麼長；管壁像波浪一樣收縮，所以就算躺著，尿液也會往下流。

kinds.where_en: Low in your belly, inside the hip bones
kinds.text_en: A stretchy bag of muscle. It tells your brain when it is about half full.
kinds.text_zh: 一個有彈性的肌肉袋子；大約半滿時，它會通知大腦。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a water treatment plant: pipes bring dirty water in, a million tiny filters clean it, the clean water goes back to the city, and the waste goes to a holding tank.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一座淨水廠：水管把髒水送進來，一百萬個小濾網把它洗乾淨，乾淨的水送回城市，廢水送到儲水槽。

measure.lead_en: Use the water tracker below the model to count what you drink today, and check the color card the next time you go to the restroom.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的喝水紀錄，數一數你今天喝了多少水；下次上廁所時，對照一下顏色卡。

steps.en: Find your goal
steps.zh: 找出你的目標
steps.text_en: Enter your weight. A common rule is 30 milliliters for each kilogram, and elementary students in Taiwan need at least 1,500 milliliters a day.
steps.text_zh: 輸入你的體重。常用的算法是每公斤 30 毫升；台灣的國小學生每天至少要喝 1,500 毫升。

steps.en: Count your cups
steps.zh: 數一數喝了幾杯
steps.text_en: Tap a cup every time you finish one. Measure your own cup or bottle once so you know how much it holds.
steps.text_zh: 每喝完一杯就點一個杯子。先量一次自己的杯子或水壺裝多少，才知道喝了多少。

steps.en: Check the color
steps.zh: 看看顏色
steps.text_en: Pale yellow is the goal. If it is dark yellow, drink a cup of water now. You need more on hot days and after sports.
steps.text_zh: 淡黃色就是目標。如果是深黃色，現在就喝一杯水。天氣熱和運動之後要喝更多。

myths.myth_en: Everyone needs exactly eight glasses of water a day.
myths.myth_zh: 每個人每天都剛好要喝八杯水。
myths.fact_en: It depends on your size, the weather, and how active you are. A rule many people use is 30 milliliters for each kilogram of body weight.
myths.fact_zh: 要看你的體型、天氣和活動量。很多人用的算法是每公斤體重 30 毫升。

myths.myth_en: The more water you drink, the better.
myths.myth_zh: 水喝得越多越好。
myths.fact_en: Your kidneys can only handle so much at a time, and gulping down a huge amount very fast can make you sick. Small sips through the day work best.
myths.fact_zh: 腎臟一次能處理的量有限，一下子猛灌一大堆水反而會不舒服。一整天小口小口地喝最好。

myths.myth_en: You only need to drink when you feel thirsty.
myths.myth_zh: 口渴的時候再喝就好。
myths.fact_en: By the time you feel thirsty, you are already a little short of water, and children at play often do not notice. Drink at every break.
myths.fact_zh: 覺得口渴時，身體其實已經有點缺水了；小朋友玩得正開心時常常沒發現。每節下課都喝一點吧。

myths.myth_en: You need two kidneys to stay alive.
myths.myth_zh: 要有兩顆腎臟才活得下去。
myths.fact_en: One healthy kidney can do the whole job. That is why a living person can give a kidney to someone whose kidneys have failed.
myths.fact_zh: 一顆健康的腎臟就能完成全部的工作，所以活著的人可以把一顆腎臟捐給腎臟衰竭的人。

tricks.body_en: The three steps of every nephron: push the small stuff out, take back what you need, and flush the rest.
tricks.body_zh: 每個腎元的三個步驟：把小東西擠出去、把需要的拿回來、把剩下的排掉。

tricks.body_en: Pale yellow urine means enough water. Dark yellow means drink up.
tricks.body_zh: 尿液淡黃色表示水喝夠了；深黃色表示快去喝水。

tricks.body_en: Your weight in kilograms times 30 gives a daily water goal in milliliters: 30 kilograms means 900, but schoolchildren need at least 1,500.
tricks.body_zh: 體重（公斤）乘以 30，就是一天喝水的毫升數；30 公斤算出來是 900，但國小學生至少要喝 1,500。

tricks.body_en: Your right kidney is a little lower than your left, because the liver takes up the space above it.
tricks.body_zh: 右邊的腎臟比左邊低一點，因為上面的空間被肝臟占走了。

materials.en: A coffee filter or paper towel, a funnel, and two clear cups
materials.zh: 一張咖啡濾紙或紙巾、一個漏斗和兩個透明杯子

materials.en: Water, a spoonful of sand or rice, and a few drops of food coloring
materials.zh: 水、一匙沙子或米，以及幾滴食用色素

steps.en: Mix the sand and the food coloring into a cup of water. This is your “blood.”
steps.zh: 把沙子和食用色素攪進一杯水裡，這就是你的「血液」。

steps.en: Put the filter in the funnel and pour the mixture through it into the second cup.
steps.zh: 把濾紙放進漏斗，把混合液倒過去，流進第二個杯子。

steps.en: What stayed in the filter? What went through?
steps.zh: 什麼東西留在濾紙上？什麼東西通過了？

steps.en: The color went through with the water. How could you get the water back without the color?
steps.zh: 顏色跟著水一起通過了。要怎麼把水拿回來，卻不要顏色呢？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the paper filter is like the first step of a nephron: big things, like blood cells, stay behind, and small things go through. But a kidney is much smarter than paper. In the second step, it takes back the water and sugar it wants and leaves the waste, something no simple filter can do.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：濾紙就像腎元的第一步：大的東西（例如血球）留下來，小的東西通過。但腎臟比濾紙聰明得多：第二步，它把想要的水和糖拿回來、把廢物留下，這是簡單的濾紙做不到的。

materials.en: A measuring cup and everyone's own bottle or cup
materials.zh: 一個量杯，和每個人自己的水壺或杯子

materials.en: A tally chart on the board
materials.zh: 黑板上的劃記表

steps.en: Measure how many milliliters each bottle or cup holds.
steps.zh: 量一量每個水壺或杯子可以裝幾毫升。

steps.en: For one school day, make a tally mark every time you finish a bottle or cup.
steps.zh: 上學的一整天，每喝完一壺或一杯就畫一筆。

steps.en: At the end of the day, work out how many milliliters you drank.
steps.zh: 放學前算一算，你總共喝了幾毫升。

steps.en: Who reached 1,500? What could help the class drink more tomorrow?
steps.zh: 誰喝到 1,500 毫升了？明天可以怎麼做，讓全班喝更多水？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: this is good practice with multiplication and units. Most students are surprised by how little they drink at school. Agree on a class habit, such as a sip at every bell, and let students go to the restroom when they ask.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這是練習乘法和單位換算的好機會。大多數學生會很驚訝自己在學校喝得這麼少。全班可以約定一個習慣，例如每次鐘響喝一口；學生想上廁所時，也請讓他們去。

culture.body_en: In everyday Chinese and Taiwanese, a kidney is often called 腰子 (yāozi), “the waist one,” because the kidneys sit at the waist. That is also why a cashew is a 腰果 (yāoguǒ), “waist nut”: it is curved just like a kidney. English noticed the same shape in a different food: the kidney bean. And when a Taiwanese family asks 你今天喝水了沒？, “Have you had water today?”, they are looking after two small organs most people never think about.
culture.body_zh: 日常的中文和台語常把腎臟叫做「腰子」，因為腎臟就在腰的位置。腰果也是這樣得名的：它彎彎的形狀就像一顆腰子。英文在另一種食物上看到同樣的形狀：kidney bean，中文正好也叫「紅腰豆」。家人問你「今天喝水了沒？」的時候，其實是在照顧兩顆大多數人從來沒想過的小器官。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If it hurts when you go to the restroom, if your urine looks red or brown, or if you are very thirsty all the time, tell an adult. Take medicine only when a doctor or a parent says so, because some medicines are hard on the kidneys.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果上廁所時會痛、尿液看起來是紅色或褐色，或是一直覺得非常口渴，請告訴大人。只在醫生或家長說可以的時候吃藥，因為有些藥會傷腎。

lessons.title: How Do You Taste and Smell?
lessons.blurb_en: Most of what you call taste is really smell. Send food molecules to a real 3D tongue and up the back way to the nose, then pinch your nose and taste the difference.
lessons.blurb_zh: 你以為的「味道」，大部分其實是嗅覺。在 3D 裡把食物分子送到真實的舌頭、再從後門送進鼻子，然後捏住鼻子吃一口，嚐嚐差別。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your tongue senses only five basic tastes. Your nose senses thousands of smells, and your brain mixes the two into flavor.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 舌頭只分得出五種基本味道，鼻子卻聞得出幾千種氣味；大腦把兩者混在一起，才是你吃到的「風味」。

lab.how_en: The head is cut down the middle so you can look inside. Pick a food and watch its molecules take two roads. Some dissolve in saliva and reach the taste buds, which sit all over the tongue. Others float up behind the roof of the mouth into the nose: the back door. Now pinch the nose. The second road is closed, and the brain can only say sweet, sour, salty, bitter, or umami. Try the chili, too!
lab.how_zh: 頭從正中間剖開，讓你看到裡面。選一種食物，看它的分子走兩條路：一些溶在口水裡、到達遍布整個舌頭的味蕾；另一些從上顎後面往上飄進鼻子——這是「後門」。現在捏住鼻子：第二條路關起來了，大腦只說得出甜、酸、鹹、苦、鮮。也試試辣椒吧！

legend.en: Pink: the real tongue
legend.zh: 粉紅色：真實的舌頭

legend.en: Dots on the tongue: taste buds lighting up
legend.zh: 舌頭上的點：亮起來的味蕾

legend.en: Light blue: smell molecules in the air
legend.zh: 淡藍色：空氣裡的氣味分子

legend.en: Yellow: the smell patch at the top of the nose
legend.zh: 黃色：鼻腔頂端的嗅覺區

legend.en: Red sparks: pain and heat nerves (chili)
legend.zh: 紅色火花：痛覺與溫度神經（辣椒）

lab.scale_en: The skull bones and the tongue are real shapes from BodyParts3D, in their real places; the face outline, the soft palate, the taste buds, the smell patch, the nerves, and the two magnified views are our own drawing. Real taste buds and smell cells are far too small to see, and real molecules are about a million times smaller than these dots. The colors and the bars are for teaching: a real food has many more molecules than the few shown here. The model has no teeth, because BodyParts3D does not include them.
lab.scale_zh: 頭骨和舌頭是 BodyParts3D 的真實形狀，位置也是真的；臉的輪廓、軟顎、味蕾、嗅覺區、神經和兩個放大圖是本站自繪的示意圖。真正的味蕾和嗅覺細胞小到看不見，真正的分子更比這些小點小了大約一百萬倍。顏色和長條是為了教學：真實食物裡的分子種類比這裡畫的多得多。模型沒有牙齒，因為 BodyParts3D 沒有牙齒的資料。
lab.credit_html: Bone and organ models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the skull bones and the tongue, simplified the shapes, turned the model upright, and cut the skull down the middle; the face outline, soft palate, taste buds, smell patch, and nerves are our own drawing. · 骨骼與器官模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選頭骨與舌頭，簡化形狀、轉正方向並從正中剖開，臉的輪廓、軟顎、味蕾、嗅覺區與神經為本站自繪示意。

foods.open_en: Sweet, a little sour, and it smells like strawberry. That is a strawberry gummy!
foods.open_zh: 甜甜的、有一點酸，還有草莓的香味——是草莓軟糖！
foods.pinch_en: Sweet and a little sour. It is some kind of candy, but which flavor? No idea.
foods.pinch_zh: 甜甜的、有一點酸。是某種糖果，可是什麼口味？完全猜不出來。

foods.open_en: Very sour, with a fresh lemon smell. That is a lemon!
foods.open_zh: 非常酸，加上清新的檸檬香——是檸檬！
foods.pinch_en: Very sour! But is it lemon, lime, or vinegar? The tongue alone cannot tell.
foods.pinch_zh: 好酸！可是這是檸檬、萊姆，還是醋？光靠舌頭分不出來。

foods.open_en: Salty, with a warm baked smell. That is a pretzel!
foods.open_zh: 鹹鹹的，帶著烤過的香味——是脆餅！
foods.pinch_en: Salty and crunchy. A cracker? A chip? Hard to say.
foods.pinch_zh: 鹹鹹脆脆的。是餅乾？還是洋芋片？很難說。

foods.open_en: Bitter and a little sweet, with that rich chocolate smell. Dark chocolate!
foods.open_zh: 苦苦的、有一點甜，還有濃濃的巧克力香——是黑巧克力！
foods.pinch_en: Bitter, a little sweet, and it is melting. Without the smell, chocolate is hard to recognize.
foods.pinch_zh: 苦苦的、有一點甜，正在融化。少了香味，巧克力很難認出來。

foods.open_en: Savory and a little salty, with a smell of the sea. That is umami: a good broth!
foods.open_zh: 鮮鮮的、有一點鹹，還有海的香氣——這就是鮮味：一碗好高湯！
foods.pinch_en: Savory and a little salty. The umami is still there, because it is a taste, not a smell.
foods.pinch_zh: 鮮鮮的、有一點鹹。鮮味還在，因為它是味覺，不是嗅覺。

foods.open_en: Ouch, hot! None of the five tastes is strong. The burn comes from pain and heat nerves, not from taste buds.
foods.open_zh: 哇，好辣！五種味道都不強——那種燒燒的感覺來自痛覺和溫度神經，不是味蕾。
foods.pinch_en: Still hot! Pinching your nose does not stop the burn, because spicy is not a smell either. It is pain.
foods.pinch_zh: 還是好辣！捏住鼻子也擋不住，因為辣也不是氣味——它是痛覺。

paras: Pinch your nose shut and pop a fruit candy into your mouth. It is sweet, and maybe a little sour, but which fruit is it? You cannot tell. Now let go of your nose. Strawberry! What happened? The thing you call “taste” is really two senses working together. Your tongue does one part of the job, your nose does the other, and your brain mixes them into one thing: flavor.

Look at your tongue in a mirror. The little bumps are called papillae, and they are not taste buds. The taste buds are hidden in the sides of many of those bumps, and they are much too small to see. You have several thousand of them: most are on your tongue, and some are on the roof of your mouth and in your throat. Each taste bud is a tiny bundle of taste cells with a small opening at the top. When food dissolves in your saliva, its molecules wash into that opening, and the taste cells send a signal along nerves to your brain. Taste cells wear out fast, so your body replaces them about every ten days. That is why a burned tongue feels normal again so soon.

Taste cells can report only five basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami. Scientists think each one is a useful message. Sweet means sugar, and sugar means energy. Salty means minerals your body needs. Sour means acid, as in a lemon or in fruit that is not ripe. Bitter is a warning, because many poisons are bitter. Umami is the savory taste of broth, mushrooms, and cheese, and it tells you that a food has protein. It was the last of the five to be named: in 1908, the Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda found it in kelp broth.

You may have seen a map of the tongue that puts sweet at the tip, sour and salty on the sides, and bitter at the back. The map is wrong. Every part of your tongue that has taste buds can sense all five tastes. The mistake is more than eighty years old. In 1901, a German scientist measured very small differences from one part of the tongue to another. In 1942, an American textbook drew those results as a simple chart, and readers took it to mean that each area senses just one taste. You can test this yourself with a little sugar: you will taste it wherever it touches.

So where does “strawberry” come from? From your nose. High inside it is a small patch of smell cells, with about 400 kinds of smell sensors. Every smell switches on its own mix of sensors, like a chord played on a piano, and that is how you can tell thousands of smells apart. Smells reach the patch by two roads. The front door is your nostrils: you sniff. The back door is a passage that joins the top of your throat to your nose. While you chew, smell molecules from the food float up through this back door. Pinch your nose, or catch a cold, and that air cannot move. The food seems to have almost no flavor at all.

And what about spicy food? Spicy is not a taste. The chemical in chili peppers switches on nerves that feel pain and heat, the same nerves that warn you about soup that is too hot. That is why spicy food “burns.” Mint plays the opposite trick: it switches on nerves that feel cold. Your brain adds these feelings to taste and smell, along with the crunch and the warmth of the food, and the result is the flavor of your lunch. Now find a partner and try the pinch test below the model.
paras_zh: 捏住鼻子，把一顆水果糖放進嘴裡。甜甜的，也許有一點酸，可是這是什麼水果？你說不出來。現在放開鼻子——是草莓！發生了什麼事？你說的「味道」，其實是兩種感覺一起合作的結果：舌頭做一部分，鼻子做另一部分，大腦再把它們混成一樣東西——風味。
照鏡子看看你的舌頭。那些小小的突起叫做舌乳頭，它們不是味蕾。味蕾藏在許多舌乳頭的側面，小到眼睛看不見。你有好幾千個味蕾：大部分在舌頭上，有些在上顎和喉嚨裡。每個味蕾是一小束味覺細胞，頂端有一個小開口。食物溶在口水裡，分子流進那個開口，味覺細胞就沿著神經把訊號送到大腦。味覺細胞耗損得很快，所以身體大約每十天就把它們換新一次——這就是為什麼燙到的舌頭很快就恢復正常。
味覺細胞只能回報五種基本味道：甜、酸、鹹、苦、鮮。科學家認為，每一種都是有用的訊息。甜代表糖，糖就是能量。鹹代表身體需要的礦物質。酸代表酸性的東西，像檸檬，或是還沒熟的水果。苦是警告，因為很多有毒的東西是苦的。鮮是高湯、香菇和起司那種鮮美的味道，告訴你食物裡有蛋白質。它是五種裡面最晚被命名的：1908 年，日本化學家池田菊苗在昆布高湯裡找到了它。
你可能看過一張舌頭地圖：舌尖嚐甜、兩側嚐酸和鹹、舌根嚐苦。這張地圖是錯的。舌頭上只要有味蕾的地方，五種味道都嚐得到。這個錯誤已經流傳八十多年了：1901 年，一位德國科學家量到舌頭各處有非常微小的差別；1942 年，美國一本教科書把結果畫成一張簡單的圖，讀者就以為每一區只嚐得到一種味道。你可以自己用一點糖來測試：糖碰到哪裡，哪裡就嚐得到甜。
那麼「草莓味」是哪裡來的？來自鼻子。鼻腔裡很高的地方有一小片嗅覺細胞，上面大約有 400 種氣味感應器。每一種氣味會打開自己的一組感應器，就像在鋼琴上彈一個和弦，所以你分得出幾千種氣味。氣味到達那裡有兩條路。前門是鼻孔：用聞的。後門是一條把喉嚨頂端和鼻子連起來的通道：咀嚼的時候，食物的氣味分子就從這個後門往上飄。捏住鼻子，或是感冒鼻塞，空氣流不動，食物就好像幾乎沒有味道了。
那辣呢？辣不是味覺。辣椒裡的化學物質打開的是感覺痛和熱的神經——也就是湯太燙時警告你的那些神經，所以吃辣才會「燒燒的」。薄荷玩的是相反的把戲：它打開感覺冷的神經。大腦把這些感覺，連同食物的脆度和溫度，一起加進味覺和嗅覺裡，結果就是你午餐的風味。現在找一位同伴，試試模型下方的捏鼻子測驗吧。
questions: What are the five basic tastes, and where on the tongue can you sense them?
How do smells from the food in your mouth reach your nose?
Why does spicy food “burn”?
answers: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami. You can sense all five on every part of the tongue that has taste buds.
Through the back door: a passage that joins the top of the throat to the nose. While you chew, smell molecules float up through it.
Because the chemical in chili peppers switches on nerves that feel pain and heat. Spicy is not a taste.

vocab.ex: The doctor asked me to stick out my tongue.
vocab.exzh: 醫生請我把舌頭伸出來。

vocab.ex: Your taste buds are too small to see.
vocab.exzh: 你的味蕾小到看不見。

vocab.ex: What flavor of ice cream do you want?
vocab.exzh: 你想要什麼口味的冰淇淋？

vocab.ex: Saliva helps you taste and swallow your food.
vocab.exzh: 口水幫助你嚐味道、把食物吞下去。

vocab.ex: This lemon candy is really sour!
vocab.exzh: 這顆檸檬糖真的好酸！

vocab.ex: The medicine tasted bitter, so I drank some water.
vocab.exzh: 藥吃起來很苦，所以我喝了一些水。

vocab.ex: Is this hot pot spicy?
vocab.exzh: 這個火鍋會辣嗎？

vocab.ex: Pinch your nose and take a bite.
vocab.exzh: 捏住鼻子，然後咬一口。

quiz.q: How many basic tastes can your tongue sense?
Where are your taste buds?
options: All over the tongue, hidden in many of its bumps
Only at the tip of the tongue
Only at the back of the tongue

quiz.q: Which taste did Kikunae Ikeda find in kelp broth in 1908?
Why is it hard to tell the flavor of a candy when you pinch your nose?
options: Smell molecules cannot travel up to the smell cells

quiz.q: According to the reading, what is “spicy”?
options: A feeling of pain and heat
One of the five basic tastes
A sixth taste found only at the back of the tongue

kinds_head.eyebrow: Your Flavor Team · 風味小隊
kinds_head.zh: 五個成員，合成一種風味

kinds.where_en: The bumps all over the top of your tongue
kinds.where_zh: 舌頭表面一粒一粒的突起
kinds.control_en: Grip food; hold the taste buds
kinds.text_en: These are the bumps you can see. The most common kind has no taste buds at all: it just makes the tongue rough.
kinds.text_zh: 這些是你看得見的突起。數量最多的那一種根本沒有味蕾，只是讓舌頭表面粗粗的。

kinds.where_en: Hidden in the papillae, on the roof of the mouth, and in the throat
kinds.where_zh: 藏在舌乳頭裡，上顎和喉嚨也有
kinds.text_en: Each one is a bundle of taste cells shaped like an onion. The cells are replaced about every ten days.
kinds.text_zh: 每個味蕾是一束味覺細胞，形狀像一顆洋蔥；細胞大約每十天換新一次。

kinds.where_en: Made by glands around your mouth
kinds.where_zh: 由嘴巴周圍的腺體製造
kinds.text_en: Taste cells can only sense what is dissolved. Dry your tongue with a clean tissue, and a bit of sugar has almost no taste until it gets wet.
kinds.text_zh: 味覺細胞只嚐得到溶開的東西。用乾淨的衛生紙把舌頭擦乾，放一點糖，在它變濕之前幾乎沒有味道。

kinds.where_en: At the very top of the inside of your nose
kinds.text_en: It has about 400 kinds of smell sensors. Smells get there through the nostrils or through the back door from your throat.
kinds.text_zh: 上面大約有 400 種氣味感應器。氣味從鼻孔進來，或是從喉嚨的後門上來。

kinds.where_en: Everywhere in your mouth and nose
kinds.where_zh: 嘴巴和鼻子裡到處都有
kinds.text_en: Chili switches on the “hot” nerves, and mint switches on the “cold” ones. Neither is a taste or a smell.
kinds.text_zh: 辣椒打開「熱」的神經，薄荷打開「冷」的神經。兩者都不是味覺，也不是嗅覺。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a band: the tongue plays five notes, the nose plays thousands, the nerves add the drums, and your brain hears one song. That song is flavor.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一個樂團：舌頭只彈五個音，鼻子彈幾千個音，神經負責打鼓，而大腦聽到的是一首歌——這首歌就是風味。

measure.lead_en: Work with a partner. You need small fruit gummies or jelly beans in three or four flavors. Use the score card below the model to keep count for your pair, or for the whole class.
measure.lead_zh: 兩個人一組，準備三、四種口味的小水果軟糖或雷根糖。用模型下方的計分卡，記錄你們這一組（或全班）的結果。

steps.en: Eyes closed, nose pinched
steps.zh: 閉上眼睛、捏住鼻子
steps.text_en: Sit down, close your eyes, and pinch your nose. Your partner gives you one small candy. Chew it slowly for five seconds and guess the flavor. Your partner taps right or wrong in the first row.
steps.text_zh: 坐好、閉上眼睛、捏住鼻子。同伴給你一小顆糖，慢慢嚼五秒鐘，猜猜是什麼口味。同伴在第一列點「猜對」或「猜錯」。

steps.en: Let go and guess again
steps.zh: 放開鼻子，再猜一次
steps.text_en: Keep chewing, let go of your nose, and breathe out. Guess again. Your partner taps right or wrong in the second row.
steps.text_zh: 繼續嚼，放開鼻子，吐一口氣，再猜一次。同伴在第二列點「猜對」或「猜錯」。

steps.en: Compare
steps.zh: 比一比
steps.text_en: Switch roles and repeat with a new candy. After a few rounds, compare the two rows. How much did your nose help?
steps.text_zh: 兩人交換，換一顆新的糖再做一次。做幾輪之後，比較兩列的結果：鼻子幫了多少忙？

myths.myth_en: Different parts of the tongue sense different tastes.
myths.myth_zh: 舌頭的不同部位負責不同的味道。
myths.fact_en: Every part of the tongue that has taste buds can sense all five tastes. The famous tongue map came from a 1901 study that was misread in a 1942 textbook.
myths.fact_zh: 舌頭上只要有味蕾的地方，五種味道都嚐得到。那張有名的舌頭地圖，來自 1942 年一本教科書對 1901 年一份研究的誤讀。

myths.myth_en: Spicy is one of the basic tastes.
myths.myth_zh: 辣是一種基本味道。
myths.fact_en: Spicy is pain and heat. Chili switches on the same nerves that warn you when food is too hot, not the taste buds.
myths.fact_zh: 辣是痛覺和熱的感覺。辣椒打開的是食物太燙時警告你的那些神經，不是味蕾。

myths.myth_en: The bumps on your tongue are your taste buds.
myths.myth_zh: 舌頭上一粒一粒的就是味蕾。
myths.fact_en: The bumps are papillae. Taste buds are hidden inside many of them and are too small to see without a microscope.
myths.fact_zh: 那些突起是舌乳頭。味蕾藏在許多舌乳頭裡面，不用顯微鏡是看不見的。

myths.myth_en: When you have a cold, your tongue stops working.
myths.myth_zh: 感冒的時候，舌頭就失靈了。
myths.fact_en: Your tongue is fine: you can still tell sweet from salty. It is your stuffy nose that keeps smells away from the smell cells, so food seems to have little flavor.
myths.fact_zh: 舌頭沒事：你還是分得出甜和鹹。是鼻塞讓氣味到不了嗅覺細胞，所以食物好像沒什麼味道。

tricks.body_en: The tongue gives five tastes, the nose gives thousands of smells, and the brain adds them up.
tricks.body_zh: 舌頭給五種味道，鼻子給幾千種氣味，大腦把它們加起來。

tricks.body_en: Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami. In Chinese: 甜、酸、鹹、苦、鮮. All five, all over the tongue.
tricks.body_zh: 甜、酸、鹹、苦、鮮。五種味道，整個舌頭都嚐得到。

tricks.body_en: The front door is your nostrils, for sniffing. The back door is behind the roof of your mouth, for the food you are chewing.
tricks.body_zh: 前門是鼻孔，用來聞；後門在上顎後面，給你正在嚼的食物用。

tricks.body_en: Chili talks to your pain and heat nerves. Your taste buds have nothing to do with it.
tricks.body_zh: 辣椒找上的是痛覺和溫度神經，和味蕾沒有關係。

materials.en: An apple and a pear, peeled and cut into small cubes of the same size
materials.zh: 一顆蘋果和一顆梨子，削皮、切成一樣大的小丁

materials.en: Toothpicks, a blindfold, and a tally chart
materials.zh: 牙籤、眼罩和一張劃記表

steps.en: Work in pairs. The taster puts on the blindfold and pinches their nose.
steps.zh: 兩人一組。試吃的人戴上眼罩、捏住鼻子。

steps.en: The partner gives one cube on a toothpick. Apple or pear? Record the guess.
steps.zh: 同伴用牙籤給一塊小丁。是蘋果還是梨子？記下答案。

steps.en: Do it five times in a mixed-up order. Then do five more with the nose open.
steps.zh: 打亂順序做五次；然後放開鼻子，再做五次。

steps.en: Count the right answers each way. Which sense told the two fruits apart?
steps.zh: 數一數兩種情況各猜對幾次。是哪一種感覺分出這兩種水果的？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: check for food allergies first, and have everyone wash their hands. Apple and pear are both sweet and crisp, so with the nose pinched, many students do little better than guessing. Ask older students: why do we need five tries, not one?
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：先確認有沒有人對食物過敏，並請大家洗手。蘋果和梨子都是甜甜脆脆的，所以捏住鼻子的時候，很多學生猜對的次數和亂猜差不多。可以問高年級學生：為什麼要試五次，而不是一次？

materials.en: Three cups: sugar water, salt water, and water with a little lemon juice
materials.zh: 三個杯子：糖水、鹽水，以及加了一點檸檬汁的水

materials.en: Clean cotton swabs (a new one for every touch), drinking water, and a drawing of a tongue for each student
materials.zh: 乾淨的棉花棒（每碰一次換一支新的）、開水，以及每人一張舌頭的圖

steps.en: Dip a swab in the sugar water and touch the tip of your tongue. Can you taste sweet?
steps.zh: 用棉花棒沾糖水，碰一下舌尖。嚐得到甜嗎？

steps.en: With a new swab each time, touch one side, then the middle near the back. Mark on your drawing where you tasted it.
steps.zh: 每次換一支新的棉花棒，碰舌頭的一側，再碰靠後面的中間。嚐得到的地方，就在圖上做記號。

steps.en: Rinse with water. Repeat with the salt water, and then with the lemon water.
steps.zh: 用開水漱口，換鹽水再做一次，然後換檸檬水。

steps.en: Compare your drawing with the old tongue map. Is there a part of your tongue that tastes only one thing?
steps.zh: 把你的圖和舊的舌頭地圖比一比：你的舌頭有哪一塊只嚐得到一種味道嗎？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: do not touch too far back, which can make students gag, and never share swabs. Students may find that the very middle of the tongue is weak for every taste, because it has few taste buds. That is a real finding. What they will not find is a “sweet-only” tip or a “sour-only” side.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：不要碰太後面，會讓學生想吐；棉花棒絕對不要共用。學生可能會發現舌頭正中間對每一種味道都比較遲鈍，因為那裡味蕾很少——這是真的。但他們不會找到「只嚐得到甜」的舌尖，或「只嚐得到酸」的兩側。

culture.title_en: Five Flavors and One More Word
culture.body_en: Chinese has talked about 五味 (wǔwèi), the “five flavors,” for more than two thousand years: 酸甜苦辣鹹, sour, sweet, bitter, spicy, and salty. Four of them match the basic tastes of modern science. The fifth, 辣 (là), turns out to be pain, not taste. And the one that science added in 1908, umami, already had a Chinese word: 鮮 (xiān), written with the characters for fish 魚 and sheep 羊. When people feel happy, sad, and sorry all at once, they say 五味雜陳, “the five flavors are all mixed together.” Your brain mixes flavors, and it mixes feelings too.
culture.body_zh: 中文講「五味」已經兩千多年了：酸、甜、苦、辣、鹹。其中四種和現代科學的基本味道一樣；第五種「辣」，後來才知道其實是痛覺，不是味覺。而科學在 1908 年才加進來的 umami，中文早就有一個字：「鮮」，由「魚」和「羊」組成。心裡又高興、又難過、又抱歉的時候，我們說「五味雜陳」——大腦會把味道混在一起，也會把感覺混在一起。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Before any tasting activity, check for food allergies, and wash your hands. Sit down, take small pieces, and chew well, especially while your nose is pinched. Never taste something if you do not know what it is. If you cannot smell or taste for more than a few days, tell an adult.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。做任何試吃活動之前，先確認有沒有人對食物過敏，並把手洗乾淨。坐好、小口吃、慢慢嚼，捏住鼻子的時候更要注意。不知道是什麼的東西絕對不要放進嘴裡嚐。如果好幾天都聞不到或嚐不到味道，請告訴大人。

lessons.title: Why Do You Need Sleep?
lessons.blurb_en: While you sleep, your brain saves what you learned and your body grows and repairs itself. Travel through a whole night of sleep in 3D, and count your own sleep hours.
lessons.blurb_zh: 睡覺時，大腦把學到的東西存起來，身體長高、修補。在 3D 裡走過一整晚的睡眠，再算算你自己睡了幾小時。
lessons.big_idea_en: Sleep is not switching off. Your brain moves through stages all night, saving what you learned, while your body releases growth hormone and repairs itself.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 睡覺不是關機：大腦整晚在不同的階段之間切換，把學到的東西存起來；身體則分泌生長激素、修補自己。

lab.how_en: Press play, or drag the time from bedtime to morning. The chart under the model shows the stages of a typical night: light sleep, deep sleep, and REM sleep, the stage with the most vivid dreams. Watch what changes. In deep sleep the brain waves turn big and slow, and growth hormone flows. In REM sleep the eyes dart, the brain lights up, and the big muscles are switched off. Outside the window, the moon crosses the sky.
lab.how_zh: 按播放，或是把時間從睡前拖到早上。模型下方的圖是典型一晚的睡眠階段：淺睡、深睡，以及夢最鮮明的快速動眼期（REM）。看看什麼在變：深睡時腦波又大又慢，生長激素流出來；快速動眼期眼球快速轉動、大腦亮起來，大肌肉卻被關掉了。窗外，月亮慢慢走過天空。

legend.en: Colors on the brain: the areas that are busy right now
legend.zh: 大腦上的顏色：現在正在忙的區域

legend.en: Green dots: growth hormone
legend.zh: 綠點：生長激素

legend.en: Purple glow: melatonin, the “it is night” signal
legend.zh: 紫色光暈：褪黑激素，「現在是晚上」的訊號

legend.en: Gold sparks: memories being saved
legend.zh: 金色火花：正在存檔的記憶

legend.en: Blue arms and legs: big muscles switched off (REM)
legend.zh: 藍色的手腳：大肌肉被關掉（快速動眼期）

lab.scale_en: The skeleton is a real one from BodyParts3D, lying down; the brain, the eyes, the heart, the two small glands, and the room are our own drawing. The night shown here is a typical pattern, not a measurement: real nights differ from person to person and from night to night. Time is sped up: one second here is 15 minutes. The brain-wave line is a drawing of what a sleep lab records, and the dots show when hormones are released, not how much.
lab.scale_zh: 骨架是 BodyParts3D 的真實骨架，讓它躺下來；大腦、眼睛、心臟、兩個小腺體和房間是本站自繪的示意圖。這裡的一晚是典型的樣子，不是實際測量：每個人、每一晚都不一樣。時間加快了：這裡的 1 秒是 15 分鐘。腦波那條線是照睡眠實驗室的紀錄畫的示意圖；小點表示激素什麼時候分泌，不代表分泌多少。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and laid the skeleton down; the brain, eyes, heart, glands, and room are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並讓骨架躺下，大腦、眼睛、心臟、腺體與房間為本站自繪示意。

W.text_en: Awake. The whole brain is busy, and the brain waves are small and fast.
W.text_zh: 醒著。整個大腦都在忙，腦波又小又快。

L.text_en: Light sleep. The muscles relax, the heartbeat and breathing slow down, and the eyes are still. It is easy to wake up from this stage. About half of the night is spent here.
L.text_zh: 淺睡。肌肉放鬆，心跳和呼吸變慢，眼睛不動。這個階段很容易被叫醒。一整晚大約有一半的時間在這裡。

D.text_en: Deep sleep. The brain waves are big and slow, and it is very hard to wake up. Growth hormone is released, the body repairs itself, and the brain saves what you learned today.
D.text_zh: 深睡。腦波又大又慢，很難被叫醒。生長激素分泌出來，身體修補自己，大腦把今天學到的東西存起來。

R.text_en: REM sleep. The eyes dart under the eyelids, and the brain is almost as busy as when you are awake: this is when you have your most vivid dreams. The big muscles are switched off, so you do not act your dreams out.
R.text_zh: 快速動眼期。眼球在眼皮底下快速轉動，大腦幾乎和醒著時一樣忙——最鮮明的夢就在這時候。大肌肉被關掉了，所以你不會把夢裡的動作真的做出來。

pre.text_en: Bedtime. The light is low, and melatonin is rising: the body clock says night is coming. A yawn or two, and the eyes feel heavy.
pre.text_zh: 睡前。燈光調暗了，褪黑激素正在上升：生理時鐘說，晚上要來了。打一兩個呵欠，眼皮越來越重。

post.text_en: Good morning! Daylight tells the body clock to start the day, and melatonin is almost gone. After more than nine hours of sleep, the brain is ready to learn again.
post.text_zh: 早安！陽光告訴生理時鐘：新的一天開始了，褪黑激素幾乎消失。睡了九個多小時，大腦又準備好學習了。

paras: You will spend about a third of your life asleep. It can seem like a waste of time: you lie still, your eyes are closed, and nothing happens. But sleep is not like switching off a light. Your brain stays busy all night, and your body uses the quiet hours to do jobs it cannot do well while you are running around.

Sleep comes in stages. First comes light sleep: your muscles relax, and your heartbeat and breathing slow down. Next comes deep sleep, when your brain waves turn big and slow and it is very hard to wake you. Then comes REM sleep. REM stands for rapid eye movement, because your eyes dart around under your eyelids. In REM sleep your brain is almost as busy as when you are awake, and you have your most vivid dreams. Your big muscles are switched off, so you do not act your dreams out. Scientists in Chicago first described REM sleep in 1953.

The stages repeat in cycles, and in an adult one cycle takes about an hour and a half. You go through several cycles each night, but they are not all the same. Most of your deep sleep comes in the first few hours. The REM periods start short and grow longer toward morning. So if you go to bed too late, you lose deep sleep, and if you get up too early, you lose dreams.

What is all this for? One job is memory. Sleep helps your brain turn what you learned today into long-term memories. That is why a good night's sleep before a test helps more than staying up late to study. Another job is growing. Your body releases growth hormone during deep sleep, which helps you grow and helps your body repair itself. Sleep also helps you fight germs: people who do not sleep enough are more likely to catch colds.

How does your body know when to sleep? You have a body clock deep inside your brain, and it is set by light. When your eyes see daylight, the clock knows it is day. In the evening, as it gets dark, your brain starts to release a hormone called melatonin, which tells the body that night has come. Bright light late in the evening, including the light from screens, can stop your brain from releasing melatonin. Then you do not feel sleepy, even when your body needs rest.

How much sleep do you need? More than adults do. Sleep doctors say children from 6 to 12 years old need 9 to 12 hours every night, and teenagers need 8 to 10. You can help your body clock. Go to bed and get up at the same time every day, even on weekends. Turn off screens at least 30 minutes before bedtime. Keep your room dark, quiet, and cool, and skip tea and cola in the evening. Now use the sleep calculator below the model: how many hours did you sleep last night?
paras_zh: 你的一生大約有三分之一的時間在睡覺。這聽起來好像很浪費：躺著不動、眼睛閉著，什麼事都沒發生。但是睡覺並不像關燈。你的大腦整晚都在忙，身體也利用這段安靜的時間，做那些你跑來跑去時做不好的工作。
睡眠分成幾個階段。先是淺睡：肌肉放鬆，心跳和呼吸變慢。接著是深睡，腦波變得又大又慢，很難把你叫醒。然後是快速動眼期，英文叫 REM（rapid eye movement），因為眼球會在眼皮底下快速轉動。這個階段大腦幾乎和醒著時一樣忙，最鮮明的夢就在這時候。你的大肌肉被關掉了，所以不會把夢裡的動作真的做出來。1953 年，芝加哥的科學家首次描述了快速動眼期。
這些階段會一輪一輪地重複，大人的一輪大約一個半小時。每晚你會經過好幾輪，但每一輪並不一樣：深睡大多集中在前幾個小時；快速動眼期一開始很短，越接近早上越長。所以太晚睡，少掉的是深睡；太早起，少掉的是夢。
這一切是為了什麼？第一件事是記憶：睡眠幫助大腦把今天學到的東西變成長期記憶。所以考試前好好睡一覺，比熬夜念書更有用。第二件事是長大：身體在深睡時分泌生長激素，幫助你長高，也幫助身體修補自己。睡眠還幫你對抗病菌：睡不夠的人比較容易感冒。
身體怎麼知道什麼時候該睡？你的大腦深處有一個生理時鐘，它是用光來對時的。眼睛看到日光，時鐘就知道現在是白天。到了傍晚，天色變暗，大腦開始分泌一種叫做褪黑激素的激素，告訴身體：晚上到了。深夜的強光——包括螢幕的光——會讓大腦停止分泌褪黑激素，於是身體明明需要休息，你卻不覺得想睡。
你需要睡多久？比大人多。睡眠醫學專家說，6 到 12 歲的孩子每晚需要 9 到 12 小時，青少年需要 8 到 10 小時。你可以幫生理時鐘一個忙：每天在同樣的時間上床、起床，週末也一樣；睡前至少 30 分鐘關掉螢幕；房間保持黑暗、安靜、涼爽；晚上不要喝茶和可樂。現在用模型下方的睡眠計算機算一算：你昨晚睡了幾個小時？
questions: What happens in your brain and body during REM sleep?
Why do you lose deep sleep if you go to bed too late?
How can light from a screen keep you awake?
answers: Your eyes dart around, your brain is almost as busy as when you are awake, and you have your most vivid dreams. Your big muscles are switched off.
Because most deep sleep comes in the first few hours of the night.
Bright light late in the evening can stop the brain from releasing melatonin, the hormone that tells the body night has come.

vocab.ex: The baby fell asleep in the car.
vocab.exzh: 寶寶在車上睡著了。

vocab.ex: I was still awake at midnight.
vocab.exzh: 半夜十二點我還醒著。

vocab.ex: I had a funny dream about a flying bus.
vocab.exzh: 我做了一個好笑的夢，夢到會飛的公車。

vocab.ex: Deep sleep is one stage of sleep.
vocab.exzh: 深睡是睡眠的一個階段。

vocab.ex: Sleep helps your memory.
vocab.exzh: 睡眠對記憶有幫助。

vocab.ex: Growth hormone helps children grow.
vocab.exzh: 生長激素幫助孩子長大。

vocab.ex: I always yawn when I am tired.
vocab.exzh: 我累的時候都會打呵欠。

vocab.ex: My bedtime is nine o'clock.
vocab.exzh: 我的就寢時間是九點。

quiz.q: In which stage do you have your most vivid dreams?
When does most of your deep sleep happen?
options: In the first few hours of the night
In the middle of the day
It is spread evenly through the night

quiz.q: What does growth hormone do?
options: It helps you grow and helps your body repair itself
It wakes you up in the morning
It makes your eyes move in your sleep
It tells your brain it is night

quiz.q: What sets your body clock?
