kinds_head.eyebrow: The Night Shift · 夜班小隊

kinds.where_en: Deep inside your brain
kinds.text_en: It runs on a cycle of about one day, and light coming in through your eyes resets it every morning.
kinds.text_zh: 它大約一天轉一圈；每天早上，從眼睛進來的光會幫它重新對時。

kinds.where_en: Made by a tiny gland in the middle of your brain
kinds.where_zh: 由大腦中央一個很小的腺體製造
kinds.text_en: It starts to rise in the evening and is highest in the early morning hours. Bright light late in the evening can hold it back.
kinds.text_zh: 它從傍晚開始上升，凌晨最高。深夜的強光會把它壓下去。

kinds.where_en: Made by a gland about the size of a pea, under your brain
kinds.where_zh: 由大腦下方一個豌豆大的腺體製造
kinds.text_en: It is released during deep sleep, which mostly comes early in the night. That is one reason bedtime matters.
kinds.text_zh: 它在深睡時分泌，而深睡大多在前半夜——這就是就寢時間很重要的原因之一。

kinds.where_en: Deep in the brain, and all over its surface
kinds.where_zh: 大腦深處，以及整個表面
kinds.text_en: Sleep helps turn today's lessons into long-term memories.
kinds.text_zh: 睡眠幫助你把今天學到的東西變成長期記憶。

kinds.where_en: In the brain stem, at the base of your brain
kinds.control_en: Turns off the big muscles in REM sleep
kinds.control_zh: 在快速動眼期關掉大肌肉
kinds.text_en: It keeps you from acting your dreams out. Your heart, your breathing muscles, and your eyes keep working.
kinds.text_zh: 它讓你不會把夢裡的動作真的做出來；心臟、呼吸的肌肉和眼睛則照常工作。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a school at night: the students have gone home, but the cleaners, the repair crew, and the librarian who files the day's papers are all hard at work.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成晚上的學校：學生回家了，但清潔人員、修繕師傅，還有把當天資料歸檔的圖書館員，都正在努力工作。

measure.title_en: How many hours did you sleep?
measure.lead_en: Use the sleep calculator below the model. It works out your hours and keeps a record for one week.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的睡眠計算機，算出你睡了幾個小時，並記錄一個星期。

steps.en: Bedtime
steps.zh: 幾點睡
steps.text_en: Enter the time you fell asleep last night, not the time you got into bed.
steps.text_zh: 輸入你昨晚睡著的時間，不是躺上床的時間。

steps.en: Wake-up time
steps.zh: 幾點起床
steps.text_en: Enter the time you woke up this morning. The calculator shows your hours next to the 9 to 12 hours that children from 6 to 12 need.
steps.text_zh: 輸入你今天早上醒來的時間。計算機會算出時數，並和 6 到 12 歲孩子需要的 9 到 12 小時比一比。

steps.en: Keep a week
steps.zh: 記錄一週
steps.text_en: Tap the day to save it. Do this every morning for a week. Are your school nights and your weekends the same?
steps.text_zh: 點一下星期幾，把它存起來。連續一個星期，每天早上記一次。上學日和週末睡得一樣多嗎？

myths.myth_en: When you sleep, your brain switches off.
myths.myth_zh: 睡覺的時候，大腦就關機了。
myths.fact_en: Your brain stays busy all night. In REM sleep it is almost as active as when you are awake.
myths.fact_zh: 大腦整晚都在忙。快速動眼期時，它幾乎和醒著時一樣活躍。

myths.myth_en: Some people never dream.
myths.myth_zh: 有些人從來不做夢。
myths.fact_en: Almost everyone dreams every night. We forget most dreams unless we wake up in the middle of one.
myths.fact_zh: 幾乎每個人每晚都會做夢。除非剛好在夢的中途醒來，否則大部分的夢都會忘記。

myths.myth_en: Staying up late to study helps you remember more.
myths.myth_zh: 熬夜念書可以記得更多。
myths.fact_en: Sleep is when your brain turns the day's lessons into long-term memories. Cut the sleep, and you cut the saving.
myths.fact_zh: 睡覺時，大腦才把當天學的東西變成長期記憶。少睡了，存檔也就少了。

myths.myth_en: Watching videos in bed is a good way to get sleepy.
myths.myth_zh: 躺在床上看影片，比較容易想睡。
myths.fact_en: Bright light late in the evening can stop your brain from releasing melatonin. Turn screens off at least 30 minutes before bedtime.
myths.fact_zh: 深夜的強光會讓大腦停止分泌褪黑激素。睡前至少 30 分鐘就把螢幕關掉。

tricks.title_zh: 淺睡、深睡、做夢，再來一次
tricks.body_en: The stages come in cycles, again and again, all night long.
tricks.body_zh: 睡眠階段一輪一輪地重複，整晚都是。

tricks.body_en: Most deep sleep comes early in the night. The long dreams come toward morning.
tricks.body_zh: 深睡大多在前半夜；長長的夢在接近早上的時候。

tricks.title_zh: 6 到 12 歲，睡 9 到 12 小時
tricks.body_en: Children from 6 to 12 need 9 to 12 hours of sleep. The numbers almost match!
tricks.body_zh: 6 到 12 歲的孩子需要睡 9 到 12 小時——數字幾乎一樣！

tricks.body_en: Darkness lets melatonin rise. Give your brain 30 screen-free minutes before bedtime.
tricks.body_zh: 黑暗讓褪黑激素上升。睡前留 30 分鐘不看螢幕的時間給大腦。

materials.en: A chart with seven rows: bedtime, wake-up time, hours of sleep, and “How do I feel?” (1 to 5)
materials.zh: 一張七列的表格：幾點睡、幾點起床、睡了幾小時，以及「精神如何？」（1 到 5 分）

materials.en: A pencil next to your bed
materials.zh: 床邊放一枝鉛筆

steps.en: Every morning for one week, write down when you fell asleep and when you woke up.
steps.zh: 連續一個星期，每天早上寫下你幾點睡著、幾點醒來。

steps.en: Work out the hours. Give yourself a score from 1 (very sleepy) to 5 (wide awake) at 10 o'clock in the morning.
steps.zh: 算出睡了幾小時。早上十點時，幫自己的精神打分數：1 分（很想睡）到 5 分（非常清醒）。

steps.en: Make a bar graph of your seven nights. Draw a line at 9 hours.
steps.zh: 把七個晚上畫成長條圖，在 9 小時的地方畫一條線。

steps.en: On which days did you feel best? What was different about the night before?
steps.zh: 哪幾天精神最好？前一晚有什麼不一樣？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: this is good practice with time: the hours cross midnight, so students cannot simply subtract. Keep the results private or anonymous, because bedtimes depend on family schedules that children do not control. Look for patterns in the whole class instead of comparing students.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這是練習時間計算的好機會——時數會跨過半夜，不能直接相減。結果請保密或匿名，因為就寢時間常常取決於家裡的作息，不是孩子能決定的。請看全班的趨勢，不要比較個別學生。

materials.en: Your sleep diary from Activity 1
materials.zh: 活動一的睡眠日記

materials.en: A book, drawing paper, or a quiet game for the last half hour of the day
materials.zh: 一本書、圖畫紙，或是一個安靜的遊戲，給睡前半小時用

steps.en: For three nights, do what you usually do before bed. Record how long it takes you to fall asleep, and your morning score.
steps.zh: 前三個晚上，照平常的方式度過睡前時間。記下你花多久才睡著，以及隔天早上的精神分數。

steps.en: For the next three nights, turn off all screens 30 minutes before bedtime and do something quiet.
steps.zh: 接下來三個晚上，睡前 30 分鐘關掉所有螢幕，做一件安靜的事。

steps.en: Compare the two sets of nights.
steps.zh: 比較這兩組晚上。

steps.en: Was there a difference? What else might explain it?
steps.zh: 有差別嗎？還有什麼原因可能造成這個差別？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: this is a real experiment with a real weakness, and it is worth saying so: three nights is a small sample, and students know which nights are which. Ask them how they would make the test fairer. Send a note home first, so that families can join in.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這是一個真正的實驗，也有真正的弱點，值得直接告訴學生：三個晚上的樣本很小，而且學生自己知道哪幾晚是實驗組。問問他們：要怎麼讓這個實驗更公平？請先發一張通知單回家，讓家人一起參與。

culture.body_en: Taiwanese grandparents say 一暝大一寸 (chi̍t-mî tōa chi̍t-chhùn) to a sleeping baby: “one night, one inch bigger.” Nobody grows an inch in a night, but the saying holds a truth that science found much later: the body releases growth hormone during deep sleep. Mandarin has 早睡早起身體好, “early to bed and early to rise is good for your health,” and English has an old rhyme that says almost the same thing: “Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.”
culture.body_zh: 台灣的阿公阿嬤會對睡著的寶寶說「一暝大一寸」：睡一晚，長大一寸。沒有人真的一個晚上長一寸，但這句話裡藏著科學很久以後才發現的道理：身體在深睡時分泌生長激素。華語說「早睡早起身體好」，英文也有一句幾乎一樣的老話：“Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy, and wise.”（早睡早起，使人健康、富有又聰明。）
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Everyone's sleep is a little different. If you often cannot fall asleep, if you snore loudly, or if you feel very sleepy in class most days, tell an adult. Do not take anything to help you sleep unless a doctor says so.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。每個人的睡眠都有一點不一樣。如果你常常睡不著、打呼很大聲，或是大部分的日子上課都很想睡，請告訴大人。除非醫生說可以，不要吃任何幫助睡眠的東西。

lessons.title: How Do You Grow Taller?
lessons.blurb_en: Bones grow at soft growth plates near their ends. Watch real 3D leg bones grow from age 2 to 18, look at them the way an X-ray does, and measure how much taller you are in the morning.
lessons.blurb_zh: 骨頭在兩端附近軟軟的生長板長長。看真實的 3D 腿骨從 2 歲長到 18 歲，用 X 光的方式看一看，再量量你早上比晚上高多少。
lessons.big_idea_en: You grow taller because cartilage at the growth plates keeps making new bone. When the plates close after the teenage years, growing taller stops.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 你會長高，是因為生長板的軟骨不斷變成新的骨頭；青春期過後生長板閉合，就不再長高了。

lab.how_en: Slide the age from 2 to 18, or press play. On the left, a whole skeleton grows beside a ruler. On the right, the thighbone and the shinbone are magnified. The glowing bands near their ends are the growth plates: sparks show new bone being added on the side toward the middle of the bone. Switch to the X-ray view, and the plates turn into dark gaps, just as a doctor sees them. Keep sliding: in the late teens the gaps close, and the bones stop getting longer.
lab.how_zh: 把年齡從 2 歲拉到 18 歲，或按播放。左邊是一整副骨架，站在一把尺旁邊長大；右邊是放大的股骨和脛骨。兩端附近發亮的帶子就是生長板：小火花表示新的骨頭正加在靠近骨頭中段的那一側。切換到 X 光畫面，生長板變成暗色的縫隙，就像醫生看到的那樣。繼續拉：十幾歲後期，縫隙閉合，骨頭就不再變長了。

legend.en: Glowing bands: growth plates (cartilage)
legend.zh: 發亮的帶子：生長板（軟骨）

legend.en: Sparks: new bone being added
legend.zh: 小火花：正在加上去的新骨頭

legend.en: Thin line: a closed growth plate
legend.zh: 細線：已經閉合的生長板

legend.en: X-ray view: bone is light, cartilage is dark
legend.zh: X 光畫面：骨頭是亮的，軟骨是暗的

lab.scale_en: The bones are real adult shapes from BodyParts3D, made smaller for younger ages; a real child's bones are not just small adult bones, and their ends are shaped differently. The growth plates are drawn thicker than they really are, and the sparks are only a sign that bone is being added. The heights are for one example child, not a rule: healthy children of the same age can differ by many centimeters, and they start and finish growing at different times.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是 BodyParts3D 的真實成人形狀，依年齡縮小；真正的兒童骨頭並不只是縮小的成人骨頭，兩端的形狀也不一樣。生長板畫得比實際厚，小火花只是表示「這裡正在加骨頭」。身高是一個舉例的孩子，不是標準：同年齡的健康孩子可能相差好幾公分，開始和結束長高的時間也不一樣。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, turned the model upright, and scaled it by age; the growth plates are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀、轉正方向並依年齡縮放，生長板為本站自繪示意。

steady.en: The growth plates are open and busy. Cartilage cells divide and stack up, and the oldest ones turn into bone. This child is growing at a steady pace.
steady.zh: 生長板開著，而且很忙。軟骨細胞不斷分裂、疊起來，最老的那些變成骨頭。這個孩子正以穩定的速度長高。

fast.en: A few years of faster growth. The plates are working at top speed. This begins at a different age for every child, sometime between about 9 and 15.
fast.zh: 長得比較快的幾年，生長板全速工作。每個孩子開始的年齡都不一樣，大約在 9 到 15 歲之間。

closing.en: The plates are getting thinner. Bone is replacing the cartilage faster than new cartilage is made, and growth is slowing down.
closing.zh: 生長板越來越薄。骨頭取代軟骨的速度，比新軟骨長出來還快，長高慢下來了。

closed.en: The plates have closed. The cartilage is now solid bone, and only a thin line shows where it was. The bones will not get longer, but they stay alive and keep rebuilding themselves.
closed.zh: 生長板閉合了。軟骨已經變成堅硬的骨頭，只剩一條細線留在原處。骨頭不會再變長，但它們仍然是活的，會不斷重建自己。

paras: Stand against a door frame and ask someone to make a mark above your head. Come back in a year, and the mark will be too low. You have grown. But think about that for a moment. Your bones are as hard as rock. How can something so hard get longer?

The answer is that a bone does not stretch. It grows only in special places called growth plates. A long bone, like your thighbone, has a growth plate near each end. A growth plate is a thin layer of cartilage, the same bendy stuff that shapes your ears and the tip of your nose.

Inside a growth plate, cartilage cells divide again and again, and the new cells stack up in columns like coins. The oldest cells, on the side toward the middle of the bone, die, and hard bone takes their place. So the plate stays about the same thickness while the bone behind it grows longer, and the two ends of the bone move farther apart. A chemical messenger called growth hormone tells the cartilage cells to keep dividing. Your body releases growth hormone while you are in deep sleep.

Doctors can see growth plates on an X-ray. Bone shows up white, but cartilage hardly shows at all, so an open growth plate looks like a dark gap across the bone. Growth plates are the last part of a bone to harden, and they are weaker than the bone around them. That is why a child who falls hard and has a sore, swollen joint should see a doctor.

Children do not grow at the same speed every year. From about age 2 to age 10, most children grow at a steady pace. Then come a few years of faster growth, which begin at a different age for each child, sometime between about 9 and 15. Later, the growth plates slowly close: bone replaces the last of the cartilage, and only a thin line is left. This usually happens in the middle or late teens. After that, you do not grow taller. Your bones are still alive, though, and they keep rebuilding themselves all your life.

What decides how tall you will be? Mostly the genes you got from your parents. You cannot make your growth plates work faster by stretching or by hanging from a bar. What you can do is give them what they need: enough sleep, food with protein and calcium, some sunshine for vitamin D, and plenty of active play. One more surprise: you are taller in the morning than in the evening. During the day, the soft discs between the bones of your spine get squeezed, and at night they fill out again. Try the measuring tool below the model and see for yourself.
paras_zh: 靠著門框站好，請人在你頭頂上方畫一條線。一年後再回來，那條線就太低了——你長高了。但請想一想：你的骨頭像石頭一樣硬。這麼硬的東西，怎麼會變長呢？
答案是：骨頭並不會被拉長，它只在一些特別的地方生長，那些地方叫做生長板。長長的骨頭，例如股骨，兩端附近各有一片生長板。生長板是薄薄的一層軟骨，就是讓耳朵和鼻尖有形狀的那種有彈性的東西。
在生長板裡，軟骨細胞一次又一次地分裂，新的細胞像硬幣一樣一疊一疊地排成一行行。靠近骨頭中段那一側、最老的細胞會死掉，由堅硬的骨頭取代。所以生長板本身的厚度差不多不變，它後面的骨頭卻越來越長，骨頭的兩端也就越離越遠。有一種叫做生長激素的化學信差，會叫軟骨細胞繼續分裂；身體是在深睡的時候分泌生長激素的。
醫生可以在 X 光片上看到生長板。骨頭在 X 光片上是白色的，軟骨卻幾乎照不出來，所以還沒閉合的生長板看起來就像橫過骨頭的一道暗色縫隙。生長板是骨頭最後才變硬的部分，也比周圍的骨頭脆弱。所以小朋友重重摔一跤之後，如果關節又痛又腫，就應該去看醫生。
孩子並不是每年都長得一樣快。大約從 2 歲到 10 歲，大部分的孩子以穩定的速度長高；接著有幾年長得比較快，每個孩子開始的年齡都不一樣，大約在 9 到 15 歲之間。之後生長板慢慢閉合：骨頭取代了最後的軟骨，只留下一條細線。這通常發生在十幾歲的中後期。在那之後，你就不會再長高了。不過骨頭仍然是活的，一輩子都在不斷重建自己。
是什麼決定你會長多高？主要是你從父母那裡得到的基因。拉筋或吊單槓並不能讓生長板工作得更快；你能做的，是給它們需要的東西：足夠的睡眠、含有蛋白質和鈣的食物、曬一點太陽來得到維生素 D，還有多多活動、玩耍。還有一個驚喜：你早上比晚上高。白天，脊椎骨之間柔軟的椎間盤被壓扁了；到了晚上，它們又恢復飽滿。用模型下方的測量工具，自己量量看。
questions: Where does a long bone grow, and what is that place made of?
Why does a growth plate look like a dark gap on an X-ray?
Why are you taller in the morning than in the evening?
answers: It grows at the growth plates near its two ends. A growth plate is a thin layer of cartilage.
Because bone shows up white on an X-ray, but cartilage hardly shows at all.
Because the soft discs between the bones of the spine get squeezed during the day and fill out again at night.

vocab.ex: Plants grow fast in the summer.
vocab.exzh: 植物在夏天長得很快。

vocab.ex: The nurse measured my height at school.
vocab.exzh: 護理師在學校幫我量了身高。

vocab.ex: Let's measure the table before we move it.
vocab.exzh: 搬桌子之前，我們先量一量吧。

vocab.ex: Your ears are made of cartilage, so they can bend.
vocab.exzh: 你的耳朵是軟骨做的，所以可以彎。

vocab.ex: A growth plate is near each end of the bone.
vocab.exzh: 骨頭的兩端附近各有一片生長板。

vocab.ex: The thighbone is the longest bone in your body.
vocab.exzh: 股骨是你身體裡最長的骨頭。

vocab.ex: The doctor looked at an X-ray of my wrist.
vocab.exzh: 醫生看了我手腕的 X 光片。

vocab.ex: An adult does not grow taller anymore.
vocab.exzh: 大人不會再長高了。

quiz.q: Where does a long bone grow longer?
options: At the growth plates near its ends
In the very middle of the bone
All along its length, by stretching

quiz.q: What is a growth plate made of?
What does growth hormone do in a growth plate?
options: It tells the cartilage cells to keep dividing
It turns the bone into cartilage

quiz.q: What happens when the growth plates close?
According to the reading, when are you tallest?

kinds_head.eyebrow: A Growing Bone · 一根會長大的骨頭
kinds_head.en: The parts that make you taller

kinds.where_en: The long middle part of the bone
kinds.control_en: Gets longer as new bone is added
kinds.control_zh: 新骨頭加上去，它就變長
kinds.text_en: The shaft itself does not stretch. It gets longer only because the growth plates keep adding bone to its ends.
kinds.text_zh: 骨幹本身不會被拉長；它會變長，完全是因為生長板不斷在它的兩端加上新的骨頭。

kinds.where_en: Near each end of a long bone
kinds.text_en: Thin layers of cartilage. Each long bone has at least two. They are the last part of a bone to harden.
kinds.text_zh: 薄薄的一層軟骨，每根長骨至少有兩片；它們是骨頭最後才變硬的部分。

kinds.where_en: Inside the growth plates
kinds.text_en: They stack up like coins. The oldest ones die, and bone takes their place.
kinds.text_zh: 它們像硬幣一樣疊起來；最老的細胞死掉，由骨頭取代。

kinds.where_en: Made by a gland under your brain
kinds.where_zh: 由大腦下方的腺體製造
kinds.text_en: It travels in the blood to the growth plates. Your body releases it during deep sleep.
kinds.text_zh: 它隨著血液來到生長板；身體在深睡的時候分泌它。

kinds.where_en: Between the bones of your backbone
kinds.where_zh: 在脊椎骨和脊椎骨之間
kinds.text_en: They get squeezed during the day and fill out again at night. That is why you are taller in the morning.
kinds.text_zh: 它們白天被壓扁，晚上又恢復飽滿——這就是你早上比較高的原因。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of building a tower with blocks: you cannot stretch the blocks, but you can keep adding new ones at the top. A growth plate is the place where the new blocks are made.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成用積木蓋塔：積木不能被拉長，但你可以一直在上面加新的。生長板就是製造新積木的地方。

measure.lead_en: Measure your height twice in one day, and use the tool below the model to see the difference. You can also compare your arm span with your height.
measure.lead_zh: 同一天量兩次身高，用模型下方的工具看看差多少。你也可以比一比臂展和身高。

steps.en: In the morning
steps.zh: 早上
steps.text_en: Right after you get up, take off your shoes and stand with your heels, back, and head against a wall. Ask a helper to lay a book flat on your head, mark the wall, and measure to the nearest millimeter.
steps.text_zh: 一起床就量：脫掉鞋子，腳跟、背和頭貼著牆站好。請人把一本書平放在你頭上，在牆上做記號，量到公釐。

steps.en: In the evening
steps.zh: 晚上
steps.text_en: Just before bed, measure again in exactly the same way. Enter both numbers in the tool.
steps.text_zh: 睡覺前，用完全一樣的方法再量一次。把兩個數字輸入工具裡。

steps.en: Your arm span
steps.zh: 你的臂展
steps.text_en: Stretch your arms out to the sides, and have a helper measure from fingertip to fingertip. For many people, it is close to their height.
steps.text_zh: 兩手往兩邊平舉伸直，請人從一邊的指尖量到另一邊的指尖。很多人的臂展和身高差不多。

myths.myth_en: Bones grow by stretching all along their length.
myths.myth_zh: 骨頭是整根一起被拉長的。
myths.fact_en: A long bone grows only at the growth plates near its ends. The middle of the bone just gets pushed along.
myths.fact_zh: 長骨只在兩端附近的生長板生長，中間的部分只是被往外推。

myths.myth_en: Stretching or hanging from a bar makes you grow taller.
myths.myth_zh: 拉筋或吊單槓可以長高。
myths.fact_en: Exercise is good for your bones, but it cannot make the growth plates work faster. Sleep, good food, and time do that job.
myths.fact_zh: 運動對骨頭很好，但沒辦法讓生長板工作得更快。那是睡眠、好的食物和時間的工作。

myths.myth_en: Everyone has a growth spurt at the same age.
myths.myth_zh: 每個人都在同樣的年紀突然長高。
myths.fact_en: The years of fast growth begin sometime between about 9 and 15. Classmates who are the same age can be at very different points, and all of them can be healthy.
myths.fact_zh: 長得比較快的那幾年，大約在 9 到 15 歲之間開始。同年齡的同學可能處在很不一樣的階段，而他們都可以是健康的。

myths.myth_en: You are the same height all day.
myths.myth_zh: 一整天身高都一樣。
myths.fact_en: You are tallest in the morning. In one study of 100 children, the average child was about 1.5 centimeters shorter in the late afternoon.
myths.fact_zh: 早上最高。有一項研究量了 100 個孩子，到了傍晚平均矮了大約 1.5 公分。

tricks.body_en: Not in the middle, and not by stretching: at the growth plates near each end.
tricks.body_zh: 不是從中間，也不是被拉長：是在兩端附近的生長板。

tricks.body_en: New cartilage is made, and old cartilage turns into bone. When the cartilage is all gone, growing taller stops.
tricks.body_zh: 新的軟骨長出來，舊的軟骨變成骨頭。軟骨全部用完，就不再長高了。

tricks.body_en: You cannot rush your growth plates, but you can give them what they need.
tricks.body_zh: 生長板催不得，但你可以給它們需要的東西。

tricks.body_en: Your spine's discs fill out at night and get squeezed by day. Always measure at the same time of day.
tricks.body_zh: 椎間盤晚上恢復飽滿、白天被壓扁。量身高要固定在同一個時段量。

materials.en: A strip of paper about 2 meters long, taped to a wall or a door frame
materials.zh: 一張大約 2 公尺長的紙條，貼在牆上或門框上

materials.en: A hardcover book, a pencil, and a tape measure
materials.zh: 一本精裝書、一枝鉛筆和一把捲尺

steps.en: Take off your shoes and stand with your heels, back, and head against the paper strip.
steps.zh: 脫掉鞋子，腳跟、背和頭貼著紙條站好。

steps.en: A helper lays the book flat on your head and draws a short line under it. Write the date next to the line.
steps.zh: 請人把書平放在你頭上，在書底下畫一條短線，旁邊寫上日期。

steps.en: Measure again on the first school day of every month, at the same time of day.
steps.zh: 每個月第一個上學日再量一次，而且要在同一個時段量。

steps.en: At the end of the school year, work out how much you grew. In which months did you grow the most?
steps.zh: 學年結束時，算一算你長高了多少。哪幾個月長得最多？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: keep each student's strip private, and compare each child only with himself or herself. The point is the change, not the number. Height can be a sensitive subject, and children of the same age really do grow at very different times.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：每個學生的紙條請保密，只拿孩子和自己比較。重點是「變化」，不是數字。身高可能是敏感的話題，而同年齡的孩子長高的時間真的差很多。

materials.en: A tape measure and masking tape
materials.zh: 一把捲尺和紙膠帶

materials.en: Graph paper, or a large grid on the board
materials.zh: 方格紙，或是黑板上的一大張方格

steps.en: Work in pairs. Measure your partner's height, then the arm span from fingertip to fingertip.
steps.zh: 兩人一組。先量同伴的身高，再量從一邊指尖到另一邊指尖的臂展。

steps.en: Put a dot on the graph: height across, arm span up. Do not write names.
steps.zh: 在方格紙上點一個點：橫軸是身高，縱軸是臂展。不要寫名字。

steps.en: When the whole class has added a dot, look at the pattern. Do the dots make a line?
steps.zh: 全班都點完之後，看看整體的樣子：這些點排成一條線嗎？

steps.en: Draw the line where arm span equals height. Are most dots close to it?
steps.zh: 畫出「臂展＝身高」的那條線。大部分的點都靠近它嗎？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: this is a first scatter plot. Anonymous dots keep the focus on the pattern instead of on who is tallest. Ask why the two measurements go together: arms and legs both grow at growth plates, under the same growth hormone.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這是學生的第一張散布圖。匿名的點讓大家看的是整體趨勢，而不是誰最高。問問學生：為什麼這兩個數字會一起變大？因為手臂和腿都靠生長板生長，聽的是同一種生長激素的指揮。

culture.body_en: More than two thousand years ago, the Chinese thinker Mencius told a story about a farmer who thought the young plants in his field were growing too slowly. So he pulled each one up a little to help it grow. When his son ran out to look, every one of them had withered. The story became the saying 拔苗助長 (bá miáo zhù zhǎng), “pulling up the sprouts to help them grow”: you cannot rush something that needs time. Growth plates work the same way. Here is a language tip, too. In Chinese, 長高 means to get taller and 長大 means to get older. In English, “grow taller” is about your height, but “grow up” is about becoming an adult.
culture.body_zh: 兩千多年前，中國思想家孟子講過一個故事：有個農夫嫌自己的秧苗長得太慢，就把每一株都往上拔高一點，想幫它們長大。他的兒子跑去田裡一看，秧苗全都枯死了。這個故事後來變成成語「拔苗助長」：需要時間的事情，急不得。生長板也是一樣。順便學一個語言小知識：中文的「長高」是變高，「長大」是年紀變大；英文的 grow taller 講的是身高，grow up 講的則是長大成人。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Everyone grows at a different time and at a different speed, and being taller or shorter does not make anyone better. Doctors follow each child's growth on a growth chart. If you have a question about your own growth, or if a joint hurts or swells after a fall, tell an adult. Do not use any product that promises to make you taller.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。每個人長高的時間和速度都不一樣，長得高或矮並不會讓誰比較好。醫生會用生長曲線追蹤每個孩子的成長。如果你對自己的成長有疑問，或是跌倒之後關節會痛、會腫，請告訴大人。不要使用任何宣稱能讓你長高的產品。

lessons.title: How Do You Speak?
lessons.blurb_en: Your voice starts as a buzz in your throat, and your tongue and lips shape it into words. Watch the vocal folds open and close in 3D, change the pitch and the mouth shape, and feel the difference between “sss” and “zzz.”
lessons.blurb_zh: 聲音一開始只是喉嚨裡的嗡嗡聲，舌頭和嘴唇再把它捏成一個個字。在 3D 裡看聲帶一開一合，改變音高和嘴型，再摸摸喉嚨，感覺 sss 和 zzz 的差別。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your voice is made in three steps: air from your lungs, a buzz from your vocal folds, and a shape from your tongue, lips, and jaw.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 聲音分三步：肺送出空氣，聲帶把它變成嗡嗡聲，舌頭、嘴唇和下巴再把它捏出形狀。

lab.how_en: The head is cut down the middle again. Air comes up the real windpipe and passes between the vocal folds. Switch the voice on, and the folds close and buzz; switch it off, and they stay open. Slide the pitch and watch the folds stretch. Then pick a mouth shape: “ah,” “ee,” and “oo” use the same buzz with a different tongue and jaw. For “sss” and “fff,” the voice switch is the only difference from “zzz” and “vvv.” Press Listen to hear a simple computer voice do the same thing.
lab.how_zh: 頭又從正中間剖開了。空氣沿著真實的氣管往上，穿過兩片聲帶之間。把「聲音」打開，聲帶就合起來、嗡嗡地振動；關掉，聲帶就一直開著。拉動音高，看聲帶被拉長。然後選一個嘴型：ah、ee、oo 用的是同一個嗡嗡聲，只是舌頭和下巴的位置不同。sss 和 zzz、fff 和 vvv 之間唯一的差別，就是聲音的開關。按「聽聽看」，聽電腦合成的簡單聲音做同樣的事。

legend.en: Pale bands: the vocal folds, seen from above
legend.zh: 淡色的兩片：從上面看的聲帶

legend.en: Light blue dots: air from the lungs
legend.zh: 淡藍色的點：從肺來的空氣

legend.en: Yellow dots: air carrying the buzz
legend.zh: 黃色的點：帶著嗡嗡聲的空氣

legend.en: Pink: the real tongue
legend.zh: 粉紅色：真實的舌頭

legend.en: Light tube: the real windpipe
legend.zh: 淺色的管子：真實的氣管

lab.scale_en: The skull bones, the tongue, and the windpipe are real shapes from BodyParts3D, in their real places; the face outline, the voice box, the vocal folds, and the air are our own drawing. The real tongue changes its shape for every sound; here it only moves and tilts, so the mouth shapes are rough sketches. Real vocal folds open and close more than a hundred times a second, far too fast to see, so the model shows them in slow motion. The Listen button plays a very simple computer voice at a low volume: a buzz and a few filters, not a recording of a person.
lab.scale_zh: 頭骨、舌頭和氣管是 BodyParts3D 的真實形狀，位置也是真的；臉的輪廓、喉頭、聲帶和空氣是本站自繪的示意圖。真正的舌頭每發一個音都會改變形狀；這裡的舌頭只會移動和傾斜，所以嘴型只是大概的樣子。真正的聲帶每秒開合一百多次，快到看不見，所以模型用慢動作呈現。「聽聽看」播放的是音量很小、非常簡單的電腦合成聲音：一個嗡嗡聲加上幾個濾波器，不是真人的錄音。
lab.credit_html: Bone and organ models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the skull bones, the tongue, and the windpipe, simplified the shapes, turned the model upright, and cut the skull down the middle; the face outline, voice box, and vocal folds are our own drawing. · 骨骼與器官模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選頭骨、舌頭與氣管，簡化形狀、轉正方向並從正中剖開，臉的輪廓、喉頭與聲帶為本站自繪示意。

shapes.text_en: Jaw wide open, tongue low and back. The doctor asks for this sound because it gets the tongue out of the way.
shapes.text_zh: 下巴張得很開，舌頭又低又後面。醫生請你說「啊」，就是因為這樣舌頭不會擋住視線。

shapes.text_en: Jaw almost closed, tongue high and forward, lips spread. The space in front of the tongue is small, so the sound is bright.
shapes.text_zh: 下巴幾乎合起來，舌頭又高又前面，嘴角往兩邊拉。舌頭前面的空間很小，所以聲音聽起來很亮。

shapes.text_en: Tongue high and back, lips pushed forward into a small circle. The mouth becomes a longer tube, so the sound is darker.
shapes.text_zh: 舌頭又高又後面，嘴唇往前嘟成一個小圓圈。嘴巴變成比較長的管子，所以聲音聽起來比較暗。

shapes.text_en: The tip of the tongue comes close to the ridge behind the upper teeth, and air hisses through the narrow gap. With the voice off, it is “sss.” With the voice on, it is “zzz.”
shapes.text_zh: 舌尖靠近上排牙齒後面的突起，空氣從窄窄的縫隙嘶嘶地擠過去。聲音關掉是 sss，打開就是 zzz。

shapes.text_en: The lower lip touches the upper teeth, and air squeezes out between them. With the voice off, it is “fff.” With the voice on, it is “vvv.”
shapes.text_zh: 下嘴唇碰到上排牙齒，空氣從中間擠出去。聲音關掉是 fff，打開就是 vvv。

paras: Put two fingers gently on the front of your throat and say “ahh.” Do you feel a buzz? Now whisper “ahh.” The buzz is gone. That buzz is your voice being made. Your body does it in three steps, and you can remember them with three words: air, buzz, and shape.

The first step is air. To speak, you breathe out. Your lungs push air up your windpipe, the tube that you met in the lesson about breathing. Without moving air, there is no voice at all. Try to speak while you hold your breath, and you will see.

The second step is the buzz. At the top of your windpipe is your voice box, which is also called the larynx. Inside it are two small folds of soft tissue called the vocal folds, or vocal cords. When you breathe, they stay open, and air passes between them without a sound. When you speak, they close. The air pushes them apart, and they snap back together, again and again, chopping the stream of air into tiny puffs. That is the buzz you felt with your fingers.

How fast do the vocal folds open and close? Much faster than you can see. In a man's voice, they do it about 125 times every second. In a woman's voice, it is about 210 times, and in a child's voice, more than 300. Faster means a higher sound. To sing a high note, tiny muscles stretch your vocal folds longer and tighter, like a rubber band pulled tight. Children have high voices because their vocal folds are short. As you grow, they get longer, and your voice gets lower.

The third step is the shape. A buzz is not a word yet. The sound travels up through your throat and your mouth, and you change it by moving your tongue, your lips, and your jaw. Say “ah,” “ee,” and “oo” on one note. The buzz stays the same, but your mouth makes a different shape for each one, and you hear three different vowels.

Some sounds use no buzz at all. Put your fingers on your throat again and say a long “sss,” and then a long “zzz.” Your mouth does exactly the same thing for both. The only difference is that your vocal folds buzz for “zzz” and rest for “sss.” The same is true for “fff” and “vvv.” English is full of pairs like these, and getting the buzz right is a big part of a clear accent. Now try the buzz check below the model.
paras_zh: 把兩根手指輕輕放在喉嚨前面，說「啊——」。有沒有感覺到震動？現在用氣音悄悄地說「啊——」，震動不見了。那個嗡嗡的震動，就是你的聲音正在被製造出來。身體分三個步驟來做這件事，你可以用三個詞記住：空氣、嗡嗡聲、形狀。
第一步是空氣。說話的時候，你是在吐氣：肺把空氣往上推進氣管——就是呼吸那一課認識的那條管子。沒有流動的空氣，就完全沒有聲音。憋住氣試著說話，你就知道了。
第二步是嗡嗡聲。氣管的頂端是喉頭，英文也叫 voice box（聲音盒）。喉頭裡面有兩片小小的、柔軟的組織，叫做聲帶。呼吸的時候，聲帶是打開的，空氣從中間通過，沒有聲音。說話的時候，聲帶合起來；空氣把它們推開，它們又彈回去，一次又一次，把一整道氣流切成一小口一小口的。這就是你用手指摸到的嗡嗡聲。
聲帶開合得多快？快到你根本看不見。男人說話時，聲帶每秒大約開合 125 次；女人大約 210 次；小孩超過 300 次。越快，聲音就越高。要唱高音的時候，細小的肌肉會把聲帶拉得更長、更緊，就像把橡皮筋拉緊一樣。小孩的聲音高，是因為聲帶短；隨著你長大，聲帶變長，聲音也就變低了。
第三步是形狀。嗡嗡聲還不是一個字。聲音往上經過喉嚨和嘴巴，你移動舌頭、嘴唇和下巴來改變它。用同一個音高說 ah、ee、oo：嗡嗡聲沒有變，但嘴巴為每一個音擺出不同的形狀，於是你聽到三個不同的母音。
有些音完全不用嗡嗡聲。再把手指放在喉嚨上，拉長說 sss，再拉長說 zzz。這兩個音，嘴巴做的事一模一樣；唯一的差別是：說 zzz 的時候聲帶在振動，說 sss 的時候聲帶在休息。fff 和 vvv 也是這樣。英文裡到處都是這種成對的音，把「有沒有嗡嗡聲」做對，是發音清楚的一大關鍵。現在試試模型下方的嗡嗡聲檢查吧。
questions: What are the three steps your body uses to make your voice?
What do the vocal folds do when you breathe, and what do they do when you speak?
What is the difference between “sss” and “zzz”?
answers: Air from the lungs, a buzz from the vocal folds, and a shape from the tongue, lips, and jaw.
When you breathe, they stay open. When you speak, they close and open again and again, chopping the air into tiny puffs.
The mouth does the same thing for both, but the vocal folds buzz for “zzz” and rest for “sss.”

vocab.ex: She has a soft voice.
vocab.exzh: 她的聲音很輕柔。

vocab.ex: My throat hurts when I swallow.
vocab.exzh: 我吞東西的時候喉嚨會痛。

vocab.ex: Air goes down your windpipe to your lungs.
vocab.exzh: 空氣沿著氣管往下進到肺。

vocab.ex: Your vocal folds buzz when you sing.
vocab.exzh: 唱歌的時候，你的聲帶會振動。

vocab.ex: I can feel a buzz in my throat.
vocab.exzh: 我感覺到喉嚨裡有震動。

vocab.ex: Please whisper in the library.
vocab.exzh: 在圖書館請小聲說話。

vocab.ex: A small bird sings at a high pitch.
vocab.exzh: 小鳥唱歌的音高很高。

vocab.ex: The word “see” has a long vowel.
vocab.exzh: see 這個字有一個長母音。

quiz.q: Where are your vocal folds?
options: In the voice box, at the top of the windpipe
On the tip of your tongue

quiz.q: What do the vocal folds do when you speak?
options: They move up into the mouth

quiz.q: Why do children have higher voices than adults?
What changes when you go from “ah” to “ee” on the same note?
options: The speed of your vocal folds
The amount of air in your lungs

quiz.q: According to the reading, which sound is made with a buzz in the throat?

kinds_head.eyebrow: Your Voice Team · 聲音小隊

kinds.where_en: In your chest
kinds.text_en: You speak while you breathe out. More air makes a louder voice.
kinds.text_zh: 你是在吐氣的時候說話的；空氣推得越多，聲音越大。

kinds.where_en: From your lungs up to your throat
kinds.text_en: A tube held open by rings of cartilage. You can feel the rings low on the front of your neck.
kinds.text_zh: 一條靠軟骨環撐開的管子；在脖子前面下方可以摸到一圈一圈的。

kinds.where_en: Inside the voice box, at the top of the windpipe
kinds.text_en: Two small folds. Open for breathing, closed and buzzing for voice. Stretched tight for high notes.
kinds.text_zh: 兩片小小的組織：呼吸時打開，發聲時合起來振動，唱高音時被拉緊。

kinds.where_en: In your mouth
kinds.text_en: High or low, front or back: every vowel has its own tongue position.
kinds.text_zh: 高或低、前或後：每個母音都有自己的舌頭位置。

kinds.where_en: At the front of your mouth
kinds.text_en: They squeeze or stop the air for sounds like f, v, p, b, and m.
kinds.text_zh: 它們擠住或擋住空氣，發出 f、v、p、b、m 這些音。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a guitar: your lungs are the hand that plucks, your vocal folds are the string, and your mouth is the hollow body that gives the sound its color.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一把吉他：肺是撥弦的手，聲帶是琴弦，嘴巴是讓聲音有音色的那個空心琴身。

measure.lead_en: Use the buzz check below the model. Put two fingers gently on the front of your throat for every sound.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的嗡嗡聲檢查。每發一個音，都把兩根手指輕輕放在喉嚨前面。

steps.en: Find the spot
steps.zh: 找到位置
steps.text_en: Rest two fingers lightly on the front of your throat. Hum “mmm” to find where the buzz is strongest.
steps.text_zh: 把兩根手指輕輕放在喉嚨前面。哼一聲 mmm，找出震動最明顯的地方。

steps.en: Buzz or no buzz?
steps.zh: 有震動，還是沒有？
steps.text_en: Say each sound for three seconds: sss, zzz, fff, vvv. For each one, tap Buzz or No buzz, and the card will tell you what scientists call it.
steps.text_zh: 每個音拉長三秒：sss、zzz、fff、vvv。每一個都點「有震動」或「沒有震動」，卡片會告訴你科學家怎麼稱呼它。

steps.en: One breath
steps.zh: 一口氣
steps.text_en: Take a breath and say “ahh” at a comfortable volume for as long as you can. Use the stopwatch, and try three times.
steps.text_zh: 吸一口氣，用舒服的音量說「啊——」，能拉多長就拉多長。用碼表計時，試三次。

myths.myth_en: Your voice is made in your mouth.
myths.myth_zh: 聲音是在嘴巴裡發出來的。
myths.fact_en: The sound starts in the voice box, in your throat. Your mouth only shapes it.
myths.fact_zh: 聲音是從喉嚨裡的喉頭開始的，嘴巴只是把它捏出形狀。

myths.myth_en: The vocal cords are strings, like the strings of a guitar.
myths.myth_zh: 聲帶是一條一條的線，像吉他的弦。
myths.fact_en: They are two soft folds of tissue. That is why scientists now prefer the name “vocal folds.”
myths.fact_zh: 它們是兩片柔軟的組織，所以科學家現在比較喜歡叫它們 vocal folds（聲褶）。

myths.myth_en: To speak louder, your vocal folds have to move faster.
myths.myth_zh: 要說得更大聲，聲帶就要動得更快。
myths.fact_en: Faster makes your voice higher, not louder. For a louder voice, your lungs push more air.
myths.fact_zh: 聲帶動得更快，聲音是變高，不是變大。要大聲，是肺推出更多的空氣。

myths.myth_en: “S” and “z” are made in different parts of the mouth.
myths.myth_zh: s 和 z 是嘴巴裡不同的地方發出來的。
myths.fact_en: The tongue and lips are in exactly the same place. Only the buzz is different.
myths.fact_zh: 舌頭和嘴唇的位置完全一樣，只差有沒有嗡嗡聲。

tricks.body_en: Lungs push the air, vocal folds make the buzz, and the mouth gives it a shape.
tricks.body_zh: 肺推空氣，聲帶做出嗡嗡聲，嘴巴捏出形狀。

tricks.body_en: Buzz means voiced: z, v, and all the vowels. No buzz means voiceless: s and f.
tricks.body_zh: 有震動就是有聲音：z、v 和所有的母音；沒有震動就是無聲音：s 和 f。

tricks.body_en: Like a rubber band: pull it tighter, and the note goes up.
tricks.body_zh: 像橡皮筋一樣：拉得越緊，音就越高。

tricks.body_en: “Ah,” “ee,” and “oo” are one buzz in three different mouth shapes.
tricks.body_zh: ah、ee、oo 是同一個嗡嗡聲，配上三種不同的嘴型。

materials.en: An empty tissue box or a plastic cup
materials.zh: 一個空的面紙盒或塑膠杯

materials.en: Three rubber bands of different thicknesses, and two pencils
materials.zh: 三條粗細不同的橡皮筋，和兩枝鉛筆

steps.en: Stretch the rubber bands around the box, over the opening. Slide a pencil under them at each end.
steps.zh: 把橡皮筋套在盒子上、跨過開口，兩端各塞一枝鉛筆墊高。

steps.en: Pluck each band. Which one makes the lowest sound? Which makes the highest?
steps.zh: 撥一撥每一條。哪一條聲音最低？哪一條最高？

steps.en: Pull one band tighter and pluck it again. What happens to the pitch?
steps.zh: 把其中一條拉緊一點再撥。音高有什麼變化？

steps.en: Press a finger on the middle of a band to make it shorter. What happens now?
steps.zh: 用手指按住橡皮筋的中間，讓它變短。現在呢？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: thinner, tighter, and shorter all give a higher note. Vocal folds follow the same rules, and that is why a child's short folds make a high voice. Ask students to watch a band closely as it sounds: the blur is the vibration. The box matters too: pluck a band in the air, and it is much quieter, just as a buzz without a mouth would be.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：越細、越緊、越短，音就越高。聲帶也遵守同樣的規則，所以小孩短短的聲帶發出高高的聲音。請學生仔細看發出聲音的橡皮筋：模糊的那一片就是振動。盒子也很重要：在空中撥橡皮筋，聲音小得多——就像只有嗡嗡聲、沒有嘴巴一樣。

materials.en: Word cards in pairs: sip / zip, fan / van, Sue / zoo, fine / vine
materials.zh: 成對的單字卡：sip／zip、fan／van、Sue／zoo、fine／vine

materials.en: A small mirror for each pair of students
materials.zh: 每兩個學生一面小鏡子

steps.en: Work in pairs. One student reads a card with two fingers on the throat.
steps.zh: 兩人一組。一個學生把兩根手指放在喉嚨上，念出一張卡片。

steps.en: Stretch the first sound: “sssip,” “zzzip.” Buzz or no buzz?
steps.zh: 把第一個音拉長：sssip、zzzip。有沒有震動？

steps.en: Look in the mirror while you say both words. Does your mouth look different?
steps.zh: 照著鏡子說這兩個字。嘴巴看起來有沒有不同？

steps.en: Now your partner says one word of a pair without showing the card. Can you tell which one it was?
steps.zh: 現在同伴不給你看卡片，只念出一對裡面的其中一個字。你聽得出是哪一個嗎？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: Mandarin has an “s” and an “f,” but it has no “z” as in “zoo” and no “v,” so many students in Taiwan say “sue” for “zoo” and “fan” for “van.” The finger test gives them something they can feel, not just hear. Praise the buzz, not the accent.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：華語有 s 和 f，卻沒有 zoo 的 z，也沒有 v，所以台灣很多學生會把 zoo 說成 sue、把 van 說成 fan。手指測試讓他們有東西可以「摸到」，而不只是用聽的。請稱讚那個震動，不要評論口音。

culture.body_en: Chinese has a four-character phrase for good speaking: 字正腔圓 (zì zhèng qiāng yuán), “the words are correct and the tone is round.” It comes from the world of traditional opera, where singers train for years to shape every sound. Notice the two halves: 字, the word, is made by the tongue and lips, and 腔, the tone, is made by the voice. That is the same split you learned in this lesson: the shape and the buzz. Chinese adds one more job for the vocal folds. In Mandarin and Taiwanese, the pitch of a syllable changes its meaning, so the folds are busy stretching and relaxing in every word. English uses pitch too, but for feeling and for questions, not to tell one word from another.
culture.body_zh: 中文用四個字形容說話說得好：「字正腔圓」。這個詞來自傳統戲曲，演員要花很多年練習把每個音發好。注意這四個字分成兩半：「字」靠舌頭和嘴唇，「腔」靠嗓音——正好就是這一課學到的兩件事：形狀和嗡嗡聲。中文還多給聲帶一份工作：華語和台語裡，一個音節的高低會改變它的意思，所以每說一個字，聲帶都忙著拉緊、放鬆。英文也用音高，但用來表達情緒和問句，不是用來分辨不同的字。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Be kind to your voice: drink water, and do not shout for a long time. Touch your throat only gently. If your voice stays hoarse for a few weeks, or if it hurts to speak, tell an adult.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。請愛護你的嗓子：多喝水，不要長時間大喊。摸喉嚨的時候只要輕輕地放著。如果聲音沙啞了好幾個星期，或是說話會痛，請告訴大人。

lessons.title: Why Are Your Hands So Clever?
lessons.blurb_en: Each hand has 27 bones, but the muscles that bend your fingers are up in your forearm. Pull the “strings” of a real 3D hand, make a fist and a pinch, and test what your thumb can do.
lessons.blurb_zh: 每隻手有 27 塊骨頭，可是彎手指的肌肉卻在前臂。在 3D 裡拉拉真實手骨的「線」，握拳、捏東西，再測測你的大拇指有多厲害。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your fingers have no muscles of their own. Muscles in your forearm pull on long tendons, like strings on a puppet, and your thumb can touch every other finger.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 手指裡面沒有肌肉：前臂的肌肉拉著長長的肌腱，像拉木偶的線；而大拇指碰得到其他每一根手指。

lab.how_en: This is a real right hand and forearm, held up with the palm toward you. The orange strings are tendons. Each one runs from a muscle in the forearm, through the wrist, and out to a fingertip. Tap a finger to pull its tendon and watch only that finger curl. Then try the hand shapes: a fist, a pinch, a point, and a thumbs-up. Turn the hand over to see the tendons on the back, the ones that open your hand again.
lab.how_zh: 這是一隻真實的右手和前臂，舉起來、手掌朝著你。橘色的線是肌腱：每一條都從前臂的肌肉出發，穿過手腕，一路到指尖。點一根手指，拉它的肌腱，看看是不是只有那根手指彎起來。然後試試幾個手勢：握拳、捏、指、比讚。把手翻過來，看手背上的肌腱——把手重新張開的就是它們。

legend.en: Orange strings: tendons that bend the fingers
legend.zh: 橘色的線：彎手指的肌腱

legend.en: Blue strings: tendons that straighten them
legend.zh: 藍色的線：伸直手指的肌腱

legend.en: Red: muscles (brighter when they pull)
legend.zh: 紅色：肌肉（用力時變亮）

legend.en: Ivory: the real bones
legend.zh: 象牙色：真實的骨頭

lab.scale_en: The bones are real shapes from BodyParts3D; the tendons and muscles are our own drawing, and there are far fewer of them than in a real arm. A real forearm has about twenty muscles, and most fingers have two bending tendons, not one. The small muscles inside the palm are shown only at the base of the thumb. Real finger joints do not bend around one simple line, so the fist here is a little stiffer than yours.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是 BodyParts3D 的真實形狀；肌腱和肌肉是本站自繪的示意圖，數量比真正的手臂少得多：真正的前臂大約有二十條肌肉，大部分的手指有兩條負責彎曲的肌腱，不是一條。手掌裡的小肌肉只畫了大拇指根部那一塊。真正的指關節並不是繞著一條簡單的直線彎，所以這裡的拳頭比你的僵硬一點。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones of the right forearm and hand, simplified the shapes, and added joints so the fingers can bend; the tendons and muscles are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選右前臂與右手的骨頭、簡化形狀，並加上關節讓手指能彎，肌腱與肌肉為本站自繪示意。

poses.text_en: Open hand. The muscles on the back of the forearm pull the blue tendons, and the fingers straighten.
poses.text_zh: 張開手。前臂背面的肌肉拉動藍色的肌腱，手指就伸直了。

poses.text_en: A fist. All the bending muscles pull at once. This is the power grip, the one you use on a bat or a heavy bag.
poses.text_zh: 握拳。所有負責彎曲的肌肉一起拉。這是「力量型的握法」，握球棒或提重袋子時用的就是它。

poses.text_en: A pinch. The thumb swings across the palm to meet the index finger, pad to pad. This is the precision grip, for a pencil, a needle, or a grain of rice.
poses.text_zh: 捏。大拇指橫過手掌，和食指的指腹碰在一起。這是「精細型的握法」，拿鉛筆、針，或是一粒米時用的。

poses.text_en: Pointing. The index finger has more freedom than the others, so it can stay straight while the rest curl.
poses.text_zh: 用手指。食指比其他手指更能單獨行動，所以其他手指彎起來時，它可以保持伸直。

poses.text_en: Thumbs-up. The thumb has its own muscles and its own special joint, so it can do the opposite of the four fingers.
poses.text_zh: 比讚。大拇指有自己的肌肉和一個特別的關節，所以能做出和其他四根手指相反的動作。

paras: Wiggle your fingers and watch the back of your hand. Do you see thin cords moving under the skin? Now hold your forearm with your other hand and wiggle again. You can feel muscles working near your elbow, far away from your fingers. Your hand is one of the cleverest tools in nature, and it works a little like a puppet.

Start with the bones. One hand has 27 of them: 8 small bones in the wrist, 5 in the palm, and 14 in the fingers. Each finger has three bones, but the thumb has only two. With so many bones and joints, your hand can wrap around a ball, fit into a glove, or flatten out to clap.

Now the surprise. There are no muscles in your fingers. The muscles that bend and straighten them are in your forearm, and they are joined to your finger bones by long, strong cords called tendons. When a forearm muscle gets shorter, it pulls its tendon, and the tendon pulls the finger, like the string of a puppet. That is why your fingers can be thin and quick: the heavy engines are kept somewhere else. The palm does have some small muscles of its own, for spreading the fingers and for moving the thumb.

The thumb is the star. At its base is a joint shaped like a saddle, which lets the thumb swing across the palm. It can touch the tip of every other finger. This is called an opposable thumb. Try it now: thumb to index finger, middle finger, ring finger, and little finger. Without that move, you could not hold a pencil, turn a key, or button a shirt.

Your hand has two main ways to hold things. In a power grip, all the fingers wrap around something and squeeze, as when you hold a bat or carry a bucket. In a precision grip, the thumb presses against the fingertips, as when you pick up a coin or thread a needle. Your hand switches between the two without your having to think about it.

A hand is not only for holding. Your fingertips have more nerve endings packed into them than almost any other part of your body, so they can feel a single hair or read the dots of braille. Most people use one hand more than the other: about nine people in ten are right-handed. Left-handed or right-handed, your hands learn from practice. Now tape down your thumb and try the thumb challenge below the model.
paras_zh: 動一動手指，看看你的手背。有沒有看到皮膚底下有細細的條索在動？現在用另一隻手握住前臂，再動一動手指：你會感覺到靠近手肘的地方有肌肉在用力，離手指好遠。手是大自然裡最靈巧的工具之一，而它運作的方式有點像提線木偶。
先從骨頭說起。一隻手有 27 塊骨頭：手腕 8 塊小骨頭，手掌 5 塊，手指 14 塊。每根手指有三節骨頭，只有大拇指是兩節。有這麼多骨頭和關節，手才能包住一顆球、套進手套，或是攤平了拍手。
接下來是驚喜：手指裡面沒有肌肉。負責彎曲和伸直手指的肌肉在前臂，靠著又長又結實的條索連到指骨上，這些條索叫做肌腱。前臂的肌肉一縮短，就拉動它的肌腱，肌腱再拉動手指——就像木偶的線。所以你的手指才能又細又靈活：笨重的引擎放在別的地方。手掌裡倒是有一些自己的小肌肉，負責把手指張開，以及移動大拇指。
大拇指是主角。它的根部有一個形狀像馬鞍的關節，讓大拇指能橫過手掌，碰到其他每一根手指的指尖——這叫做「可以對掌的拇指」。現在就試試：大拇指碰食指、中指、無名指、小指。少了這個動作，你就沒辦法握鉛筆、轉鑰匙，或是扣鈕扣。
手拿東西主要有兩種方式。「力量型的握法」是所有手指包住東西、用力握緊，例如握球棒或提水桶。「精細型的握法」是大拇指抵著指尖，例如撿硬幣或穿針。你的手會在這兩種握法之間自動切換，根本不用你去想。
手不只是用來拿東西。指尖裡擠滿了神經末梢，比身體幾乎任何其他地方都密，所以摸得出一根頭髮，也讀得出點字。大多數人比較常用其中一隻手：大約每十個人裡有九個是右撇子。不管你是左撇子還是右撇子，手都是越練越巧的。現在把大拇指貼起來，試試模型下方的拇指挑戰。
questions: How many bones are in one hand, and where are they?
Where are the muscles that bend your fingers, and how do they reach the fingers?
What is the difference between a power grip and a precision grip?
answers: There are 27: 8 in the wrist, 5 in the palm, and 14 in the fingers.
They are in the forearm. Long cords called tendons join them to the finger bones.
In a power grip, all the fingers wrap around something and squeeze. In a precision grip, the thumb presses against the fingertips.

vocab.ex: She wears a watch on her left wrist.
vocab.exzh: 她把手錶戴在左手腕上。

vocab.ex: Hold the coin in your palm.
vocab.exzh: 把硬幣放在手掌上。

vocab.ex: He gave me a thumbs-up.
vocab.exzh: 他對我比了一個讚。

vocab.ex: A tendon joins a muscle to a bone.
vocab.exzh: 肌腱把肌肉連到骨頭上。

vocab.ex: Keep a firm grip on the rope.
vocab.exzh: 把繩子握緊。

vocab.ex: Pinch the clay between your thumb and finger.
vocab.exzh: 用大拇指和手指捏住黏土。

vocab.ex: Make a fist, and then open your hand.
vocab.exzh: 握拳，然後把手張開。

vocab.ex: I can feel the bumps with my fingertips.
vocab.exzh: 我用指尖摸得出那些小突起。
