kinds_head.eyebrow: Parts of a Hand · 手的零件

kinds.where_en: 8 in the wrist, 5 in the palm, 14 in the fingers
kinds.text_en: Your two hands hold 54 of your 206 bones, more than a quarter of them.
kinds.text_zh: 兩隻手一共 54 塊骨頭，占了全身 206 塊的四分之一以上。

kinds.where_en: From the forearm, through the wrist, to the fingers
kinds.where_zh: 從前臂、穿過手腕，到手指
kinds.text_en: Strong cords that do not stretch. You can see some of them on the back of your hand when you spread your fingers.
kinds.text_zh: 結實、不會伸長的條索。把手指張開，在手背上就看得到其中幾條。

kinds.where_en: Between your elbow and your wrist
kinds.text_en: Muscles on the palm side bend the fingers. Muscles on the back straighten them.
kinds.text_zh: 手掌那一面的肌肉負責彎手指，背面的肌肉負責伸直。

kinds.where_en: On the side of your hand, with a saddle joint at its base
kinds.where_zh: 在手的側邊，根部有一個鞍狀關節
kinds.control_zh: 碰得到其他每一根手指
kinds.text_en: It has only two bones, but its own set of muscles. Most of the ways you hold things need it.
kinds.text_zh: 它只有兩節骨頭，卻有自己的一組肌肉。你拿東西的方式，大部分都少不了它。

kinds.where_en: At the end of each finger
kinds.text_en: Packed with nerve endings, and backed by a fingernail so that you can press on small things.
kinds.text_zh: 擠滿了神經末梢，背後還有指甲撐著，讓你能壓住很小的東西。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a puppet: the hands that move it are high above the stage, and thin strings do the rest. Your forearm is the puppeteer, and your fingers are the puppet.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成提線木偶：操縱它的手高高在舞台上方，其餘的全靠細細的線。你的前臂是操偶師，手指就是木偶。

measure.lead_en: How much do you need your thumb? Time three small jobs with your thumb, and then with your thumb taped down. Use the timer card below the model.
measure.lead_zh: 你有多需要大拇指？先正常做三件小事並計時，再把大拇指貼起來做一次。用模型下方的計時卡。

steps.en: With your thumb
steps.zh: 用大拇指
steps.text_en: Do each job as you always do: write your name, pick up five coins one at a time, and button one button. Tap the card to start and stop the timer.
steps.text_zh: 照平常的方式做每一件事：寫自己的名字、一次一個撿起五個硬幣、扣一顆鈕扣。點卡片開始計時，再點一次停止。

steps.en: Tape it down
steps.zh: 把它貼起來
steps.text_en: Ask a partner to tape your thumb gently against the side of your palm with paper tape. It should not hurt, and it should come off easily.
steps.text_zh: 請同伴用紙膠帶把你的大拇指輕輕貼在手掌側邊。不應該會痛，也要能輕鬆撕下來。

steps.en: Compare
steps.zh: 比一比
steps.text_en: Do the same three jobs again and time them. The card shows how many times slower you were. Which job was the hardest?
steps.text_zh: 同樣的三件事再做一次並計時。卡片會算出你慢了幾倍。哪一件事最難？

myths.myth_en: Your fingers are full of muscles.
myths.myth_zh: 手指裡面都是肌肉。
myths.fact_en: There are no muscles in the fingers. Forearm muscles move them by pulling on tendons, and small muscles in the palm help.
myths.fact_zh: 手指裡沒有肌肉。前臂的肌肉拉著肌腱來移動它們，手掌裡的小肌肉從旁幫忙。

myths.myth_en: The thumb is just a short finger.
myths.myth_zh: 大拇指只是比較短的手指。
myths.fact_en: The thumb has two bones instead of three, its own muscles, and a saddle joint that lets it swing across the palm.
myths.fact_zh: 大拇指只有兩節骨頭（不是三節），有自己的肌肉，還有一個鞍狀關節，讓它能橫過手掌。

myths.myth_en: Left-handed people are very rare.
myths.myth_zh: 左撇子非常少見。
myths.fact_en: About one person in ten is left-handed. In a class of thirty, that is likely to be about three students.
myths.fact_zh: 大約每十個人就有一個是左撇子。一個三十人的班級裡，大概會有三位。

myths.myth_en: Strong hands come from big hands.
myths.myth_zh: 手大，握力才會大。
myths.fact_en: Grip strength comes mostly from the forearm muscles that pull the tendons. That is why climbers have strong forearms.
myths.fact_zh: 握力主要來自拉動肌腱的前臂肌肉，所以攀岩的人前臂都很結實。

tricks.body_en: Wrist 8, palm 5, fingers 14. Together they make 27.
tricks.body_zh: 手腕 8、手掌 5、手指 14，加起來 27。

tricks.title_en: The engine is in the arm
tricks.body_en: Finger muscles live in the forearm. Tendons are the strings.
tricks.body_zh: 動手指的肌肉住在前臂，肌腱是那些線。

tricks.body_en: An opposable thumb can touch the tip of every other finger.
tricks.body_zh: 可以對掌的拇指，碰得到其他每一根手指的指尖。

tricks.title_en: Wrap for power, pinch for precision
tricks.title_zh: 包住是力量，捏住是精細
tricks.body_en: A bat needs a power grip. A pencil needs a precision grip.
tricks.body_zh: 握球棒用力量型的握法，拿鉛筆用精細型的握法。

materials.en: Thin cardboard, five drinking straws, and tape
materials.zh: 薄紙板、五根吸管和膠帶

materials.en: Five pieces of string, each about 40 centimeters long, and scissors
materials.zh: 五條大約 40 公分長的棉線，和剪刀

steps.en: Trace your hand on the cardboard and cut it out. Fold each finger gently where your own joints are.
steps.zh: 在紙板上描出自己的手並剪下來。在每根手指上，照自己關節的位置輕輕摺出摺痕。

steps.en: Cut the straws into short pieces and tape one piece on each part of every finger, with gaps at the folds. Tape a long piece on the palm below each finger.
steps.zh: 把吸管剪成小段，每一節指節貼一段，摺痕的地方留空；每根手指下方的手掌上各貼一段長的。

steps.en: Thread a string through the straws of each finger, and tape its end at the fingertip.
steps.zh: 每根手指穿一條線過那些吸管，線頭用膠帶固定在指尖。

steps.en: Hold the wrist and pull the strings one at a time. Can you make a fist? A pinch? A thumbs-up?
steps.zh: 握住手腕，一條一條地拉線。你能讓它握拳嗎？能捏嗎？能比讚嗎？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the straws are the bones, the strings are the tendons, and the student's own pulling hand is the forearm muscle. Notice that a string can only pull: to open the hand again, something else has to pull the other way. That is why the back of your hand has its own set of tendons.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：吸管是骨頭，棉線是肌腱，學生拉線的那隻手就是前臂的肌肉。請注意：線只能拉，不能推——要把手重新張開，得有別的東西往反方向拉。這就是手背另外有一組肌腱的原因。

materials.en: Paper and a pencil for each student
materials.zh: 每個學生一張紙和一枝鉛筆

materials.en: A tally chart on the board
materials.zh: 黑板上的劃記表

steps.en: Write your name with the hand you usually use. Time it.
steps.zh: 用平常慣用的那隻手寫名字，並計時。

steps.en: Now write it with your other hand. Time it again, and compare the two.
steps.zh: 換另一隻手再寫一次並計時，比較這兩次。

steps.en: On the board, tally how many students write with the right hand and how many with the left.
steps.zh: 在黑板上劃記：班上有幾個人用右手寫字，幾個人用左手。

steps.en: Is your class close to nine in ten? Practice with your other hand for a week. Does it get faster?
steps.zh: 你們班接近十分之九嗎？用另一隻手練習一個星期，有沒有變快？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: left-handed students should never be made to switch. Use the activity to show that the “other” hand is not weak, only less practiced: the muscles and tendons are the same, and the difference is in the brain's practice. A small class may be far from nine in ten, and that is a good chance to talk about small samples.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：絕對不要要求左撇子的學生改用右手。請用這個活動讓學生明白，「另一隻手」並不是比較弱，只是比較少練習：肌肉和肌腱都一樣，差別在大腦練得多不多。小班級的比例可能離十分之九很遠——這正是討論「樣本太小」的好機會。

culture.body_en: Chinese says 十指連心 (shí zhǐ lián xīn), “the ten fingers are joined to the heart”: hurt one finger, and the whole person feels it. Science agrees in its own way, because fingertips are packed with nerve endings. A skillful person is 手巧 (shǒu qiǎo), “hand-clever,” and when a job goes smoothly, people say 得心應手, “what the heart wants, the hand does.” Chinese even measures with the hand: 一把米 is a handful of rice that your fingers close around, and 一捧水 is the water you can carry in two cupped hands. English counts in hands too: a “handful,” a “pinch” of salt, and a horse's height is still measured in “hands.”
culture.body_zh: 中文說「十指連心」：傷了一根手指，整個人都感覺得到。科學用自己的方式同意這句話——指尖擠滿了神經末梢。手藝好的人叫「手巧」；事情做得順，就說「得心應手」：心裡想的，手就做得到。中文甚至用手來量東西：「一把米」是手指握得住的米，「一捧水」是兩手合起來捧得住的水。英文也用手來數：a handful（一把）、a pinch of salt（一小撮鹽），而馬的身高到今天還是用 hands（掌寬）來量。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Use paper tape for the thumb challenge, keep it loose, and take it off if anything hurts or tingles. If a finger is swollen, will not bend, or hurts after a fall, tell an adult.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。拇指挑戰請用紙膠帶，貼鬆一點；如果會痛或覺得麻，就馬上撕掉。如果手指腫起來、彎不了，或是跌倒之後會痛，請告訴大人。

lessons.title: How Does Your Body Fix Itself?
lessons.blurb_en: A scab, a bruise, a broken arm in a cast: your body is repairing itself. Watch a real 3D bone knit back together beside a healing cut, and keep a diary of a bruise or a fingernail.
lessons.blurb_zh: 結痂、瘀青、打石膏的手臂——身體正在修補自己。看真實的 3D 骨頭慢慢長回去，旁邊是一道正在癒合的傷口，再幫一塊瘀青或一片指甲寫日記。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your body repairs itself in the same order every time: stop the leak, clean up, build a quick patch, then slowly rebuild it properly.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 身體修補自己的順序每次都一樣：先止血、再清理、搭一個臨時的補丁，最後慢慢把它重新蓋好。

lab.how_en: On the right is a real forearm with a break in one bone. On the left is a small block of skin with a cut. Press play, or drag the slider through the four steps. The bone and the skin follow the same plan, but on very different clocks: the cut needs days, and the bone needs months. Watch the two clocks in the panel, and switch the cast on and off.
lab.how_zh: 右邊是一隻真實的前臂，其中一根骨頭斷了；左邊是一小塊有割傷的皮膚。按播放，或拖動滑桿走過四個步驟。骨頭和皮膚照的是同一套計畫，用的卻是很不一樣的時鐘：割傷只要幾天，骨頭卻要好幾個月。看看面板上的兩個時鐘，也試試把石膏打開、關掉。

legend.en: Dark red: the blood clot
legend.zh: 暗紅色：血塊

legend.en: White dots: white blood cells cleaning up
legend.zh: 白點：正在清理的白血球

legend.en: Pink: the quick patch (soft new tissue)
legend.zh: 粉紅色：臨時的補丁（柔軟的新組織）

legend.en: Ivory lump: new bone, later trimmed smooth
legend.zh: 象牙色的腫塊：新的骨頭，之後會被修平

legend.en: White shell: the cast
legend.zh: 白色的殼：石膏

lab.scale_en: The forearm bones are real shapes from BodyParts3D; the break, the clot, the lump of new bone, the cast, and the block of skin are our own drawing. A real break is jagged, and the skin block is greatly magnified. The times are typical ones for a simple break in a forearm and for a small clean cut. Real healing times depend on the injury, the bone, and the person, and children's bones usually heal faster than adults' bones.
lab.scale_zh: 前臂的骨頭是 BodyParts3D 的真實形狀；斷裂處、血塊、新骨頭的腫塊、石膏和那一小塊皮膚是本站自繪的示意圖。真正的骨折斷面是不規則的，皮膚塊是放大很多倍的示意。時間是前臂單純骨折和乾淨的小割傷的典型情況；實際要多久，要看傷勢、哪一根骨頭和每個人的狀況，而孩子的骨頭通常比大人癒合得快。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones of the right forearm and hand and simplified the shapes; the break, the healing tissue, the cast, and the skin are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選右前臂與右手的骨頭並簡化形狀，斷裂處、癒合中的組織、石膏與皮膚為本站自繪示意。

stages.bone_en: Blood vessels inside the bone tear, and blood pools around the break. Within a few hours it sets into a clot. A doctor lines the pieces up and puts on a cast.
stages.bone_zh: 骨頭裡的血管斷了，血積在斷裂處周圍，幾個小時內凝成血塊。醫生把骨頭對齊，打上石膏。
stages.skin_en: Within minutes, tiny blood cells called platelets stick together at the cut, and a net of threads glues them into a clot. The top dries into a scab.
stages.skin_zh: 幾分鐘之內，叫做血小板的小小血球在傷口黏在一起，一張絲線織成的網把它們黏成血塊，表面乾了就變成痂。

stages.bone_en: White blood cells move in and eat the dead cells and tiny chips of bone. The arm is swollen and sore: that is the cleanup crew at work, and it goes on for about a week.
stages.bone_zh: 白血球趕來，吃掉死掉的細胞和骨頭碎屑。手臂又腫又痛——那是清潔隊正在工作，大約持續一個星期。
stages.skin_en: White blood cells arrive within an hour and swallow germs and dirt. The skin around the cut turns red and warm for a few days.
stages.skin_zh: 白血球一小時內就到了，吞掉細菌和髒東西。傷口周圍的皮膚會紅紅熱熱的好幾天。

stages.bone_en: Cells from the bone's outer skin build a soft, rubbery bridge across the gap. In a few weeks, new bone replaces it and makes a hard lump around the break. Now the cast can come off.
stages.bone_zh: 骨頭外膜的細胞在缺口上搭起一座柔軟、有彈性的橋；幾個星期後，新的骨頭取代它，在斷裂處周圍形成硬硬的一團。這時就可以拆石膏了。
stages.skin_en: New blood vessels and soft pink tissue fill the cut from below, and skin cells creep across under the scab. In a week or two, the scab falls off by itself.
stages.skin_zh: 新的血管和柔軟的粉紅色組織從下面把傷口填滿，皮膚細胞在痂的底下爬過去。一兩個星期後，痂會自己掉下來。

stages.bone_en: The lump is stronger than it needs to be, and bulky. Over months and years, bone cells trim it away and rebuild the bone in its old shape. In the end, even an X-ray may not show where the break was.
stages.bone_zh: 那一團比需要的還結實，也很笨重。接下來的幾個月到幾年，骨細胞把它慢慢修掉，把骨頭重建成原來的形狀。到最後，連 X 光片都可能看不出哪裡斷過。
stages.skin_en: The patch is slowly rebuilt with stronger fibers, for a year or more. A small cut leaves almost no mark. A deep one leaves a scar, which never gets quite as strong as the skin was.
stages.skin_zh: 補丁被比較強韌的纖維慢慢重建，要一年或更久。小割傷幾乎不留痕跡；深的傷口會留下疤，而疤永遠沒辦法和原來的皮膚一樣強韌。

paras: Think about the last time you scraped your knee. It bled, it stung, and a week later the scab fell off and showed new pink skin. Nobody had to tell your knee what to do. A broken toy stays broken, but your body repairs itself, and it follows the same plan every time. The plan has four steps.

Step one: stop the leak. When you are cut, blood vessels are cut too. Within minutes, tiny blood cells called platelets stick to the edges and to one another. Then a net of sticky threads forms and glues everything into a clot. On your skin, the top of the clot dries out and becomes a scab. A scab is your body's own bandage, so try not to pick it.

Step two: clean up. White blood cells, which you met in the lesson about germs, arrive within an hour. They swallow germs, dirt, and dead cells. More blood flows to the area to bring them, and that is why the skin around a cut is red, warm, and a little swollen for a few days. It does not feel good, but it is a sign that the cleanup crew is working.

Step three: build a quick patch. Under the scab, new blood vessels grow, and soft pink tissue fills the gap. Skin cells creep across from the edges until they meet. This patch is made fast, and it is not very strong. Step four: rebuild it properly. For months, even a year or more, your body replaces the patch with stronger fibers. A deep cut leaves a scar, and a scar never gets quite as strong as the skin was before.

Bones follow the same four steps on a slower clock. When a bone breaks, blood pools around the break and forms a clot within a few hours. White blood cells clean up for about a week. Then the body builds a patch: first a soft bridge, like rubber, and then a hard lump of new bone around the break. That takes some weeks, and it is why you wear a cast. The cast does not heal the bone. It only holds the pieces still while the bone heals itself. Finally, over months and years, bone cells trim the lump away until the bone has its old shape again. Young bones do all of this faster than old ones.

A bruise is a repair you can watch in color. A bump breaks tiny blood vessels under the skin, and blood leaks out, but the skin is not broken. At first the bruise is red, blue, or purple. As your body breaks the old blood down and carries it away, the bruise turns green and then yellow or brown. In about two weeks it is gone. You cannot make these steps go faster, but you can help: wash a cut with clean water, keep it covered, eat and sleep well, and let the scab do its job. Now start a healing diary with the tool below the model.
paras_zh: 想想你上一次膝蓋擦傷的時候：它流血、刺痛，一個星期後痂掉了，露出粉紅色的新皮膚。沒有人需要告訴你的膝蓋該怎麼做。壞掉的玩具就是壞了，但你的身體會自己修補自己，而且每次都照同一套計畫。這套計畫有四個步驟。
第一步：止血。你被割傷的時候，血管也被割斷了。幾分鐘之內，叫做血小板的小小血球就會黏在傷口邊緣，也彼此黏在一起；接著，一張由黏黏的絲線織成的網形成了，把所有東西黏成一個血塊。在皮膚上，血塊的表面乾掉，就變成了痂。痂是身體自己做的繃帶，所以盡量不要去摳它。
第二步：清理。你在病菌那一課認識的白血球，一小時內就會趕到。它們吞掉細菌、髒東西和死掉的細胞。為了把它們送過來，更多的血流向這個地方——這就是為什麼傷口周圍的皮膚會紅紅的、熱熱的，還有一點腫，持續好幾天。那種感覺並不舒服，但它表示清潔隊正在工作。
第三步：搭一個臨時的補丁。在痂的底下，新的血管長出來，柔軟的粉紅色組織把缺口填滿；皮膚細胞從邊緣爬過來，直到在中間會合。這個補丁做得很快，但不怎麼結實。第四步：把它重新蓋好。接下來的幾個月，甚至一年以上，身體會用比較強韌的纖維把補丁換掉。很深的傷口會留下疤，而疤永遠沒辦法和原來的皮膚一樣強韌。

骨頭照的是同樣的四個步驟，只是時鐘慢得多。骨頭斷掉時，血積在斷裂處周圍，幾個小時內凝成血塊。白血球清理大約一個星期。然後身體開始搭補丁：先是一座像橡皮一樣柔軟的橋，再來是包在斷裂處周圍、硬硬的一團新骨頭。這要花上好幾個星期，這也是你要打石膏的原因。石膏並不會讓骨頭癒合，它只是把骨頭固定住，讓骨頭自己長好。最後，在接下來的幾個月到幾年裡，骨細胞把那一團慢慢修掉，直到骨頭恢復原來的形狀。年輕的骨頭做這一切，都比年老的骨頭快。
瘀青是一場你可以用顏色觀察的修補。碰撞弄破了皮膚底下的微血管，血流了出來，但皮膚並沒有破。瘀青一開始是紅色、藍色或紫色；當身體把舊的血分解、運走，它就變成綠色，再變成黃色或褐色。大約兩個星期，它就消失了。你沒辦法讓這些步驟變快，但你可以幫忙：用乾淨的水沖洗傷口、把它蓋好、吃好睡好，然後讓痂做它的工作。現在用模型下方的工具，開始寫一份癒合日記吧。
questions: What are the four steps your body follows to repair itself?
What does a cast do for a broken bone?
Why does a bruise change color?
answers: Stop the leak, clean up, build a quick patch, and then rebuild it properly.
It holds the pieces of the bone still while the bone heals itself. The cast does not heal the bone.
Because the body breaks down the old blood under the skin and carries it away, and the colors change as it does.

vocab.ex: The cut will heal in about a week.
vocab.exzh: 這個傷口大約一個星期就會癒合。

vocab.ex: Do not pick the scab on your knee.
vocab.exzh: 不要摳膝蓋上的痂。

vocab.ex: I got a bruise when I bumped the table.
vocab.exzh: 我撞到桌子，瘀青了。

vocab.ex: A clot stopped the bleeding.
vocab.exzh: 血塊把血止住了。

vocab.ex: My ankle is swollen after the fall.
vocab.exzh: 跌倒之後，我的腳踝腫起來了。

vocab.ex: She had a cast on her arm for six weeks.
vocab.exzh: 她手臂上打了六個星期的石膏。

vocab.ex: He has a small scar on his chin.
vocab.exzh: 他的下巴上有一個小疤。

vocab.ex: Your body can repair itself.
vocab.exzh: 你的身體能修補自己。

quiz.q: What is the first step when your body repairs a cut?
options: It stops the leak with a clot

quiz.q: Why is the skin around a new cut red and warm?
options: More blood is bringing white blood cells
The skin is growing too fast

quiz.q: What does a cast do?
options: It holds the bone still while it heals
It kills germs in the bone
It stops the arm from growing

quiz.q: What happens to the hard lump around a healed break?
options: Bone cells slowly trim it away
It falls off after a week

quiz.q: According to the reading, what colors does a bruise usually turn before it disappears?

kinds_head.eyebrow: The Repair Crew · 修補小隊

kinds.where_en: In your blood
kinds.text_en: Tiny pieces of cells that stick together at a wound within minutes.
kinds.text_zh: 很小的細胞碎片，幾分鐘內就會在傷口黏在一起。

kinds.where_en: Over the wound
kinds.text_en: A net of sticky threads traps blood cells. When the top dries, it is a scab: your own bandage.
kinds.text_zh: 一張黏黏的絲網把血球困住；表面乾掉就是痂——你自己做的繃帶。

kinds.where_en: They come out of the blood vessels
kinds.text_en: They swallow germs, dirt, and dead cells. The redness and swelling are signs of their work.
kinds.text_zh: 它們吞掉細菌、髒東西和死掉的細胞；紅和腫就是它們在工作的跡象。

kinds.where_en: In skin, and on the outer skin of a bone
kinds.where_zh: 在皮膚裡，以及骨頭的外膜上
kinds.text_en: They weave fibers in skin and lay down new bone in a break. Fast first, strong later.
kinds.text_zh: 它們在皮膚裡織出纖維，在骨折處鋪上新的骨頭。先求快，再求堅固。

kinds.where_en: On the surface of bone
kinds.text_en: They nibble away the extra bone, a little at a time, for months or years.
kinds.text_zh: 它們一點一點啃掉多餘的骨頭，持續好幾個月到好幾年。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a road crew after a storm: first they close the road, then they clear the mess, then they lay a quick patch so traffic can pass, and months later they come back and pave it properly.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成颱風過後的修路隊：先封路，再清掉雜物，然後鋪一層臨時的路面讓車子能通行，幾個月後再回來把路好好鋪平。

measure.lead_en: Use the diary below the model. You can follow a bruise, day by day, or measure how fast a fingernail grows.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的日記。你可以一天一天追蹤一塊瘀青，或是量一量指甲長得多快。

steps.en: Follow a bruise
steps.zh: 追蹤一塊瘀青
steps.text_en: The next time you get a bruise, look at it once a day. Tap that day's box until the color matches. Most bruises go from red or purple to green to yellow in about two weeks.
steps.text_zh: 下次瘀青的時候，每天看它一次，點當天的格子直到顏色對上。大多數的瘀青會從紅色或紫色變成綠色、再變成黃色，大約兩個星期。

steps.en: Mark a nail
steps.zh: 在指甲上做記號
steps.text_en: No bruise? Ask an adult to help you put a small dot of nail polish at the very base of one fingernail. Measure from the skin to the dot.
steps.text_zh: 沒有瘀青？請大人幫忙，在一片指甲最根部點一小點指甲油，量一量從皮膚到那個點的距離。

steps.en: Measure again
steps.zh: 再量一次
steps.text_en: Two or three weeks later, measure again and enter the numbers. The tool works out your nail's speed and compares it with the usual 3.5 millimeters a month.
steps.text_zh: 兩三個星期後再量一次，把數字輸入進去。工具會算出你的指甲長得多快，並和一般的每個月 3.5 公釐比一比。

myths.myth_en: A cast heals a broken bone.
myths.myth_zh: 石膏會把骨頭治好。
myths.fact_en: The bone heals itself. The cast only keeps the pieces still and lined up while it does.
myths.fact_zh: 骨頭是自己癒合的；石膏只是讓骨頭保持不動、對齊。

myths.myth_en: Picking off a scab helps a cut heal faster.
myths.myth_zh: 把痂摳掉，傷口會好得比較快。
myths.fact_en: The scab protects the new skin growing under it. Pick it off, and the body has to start that part again.
myths.fact_zh: 痂保護著底下正在長的新皮膚。把它摳掉，身體就得把那一段重來一次。

myths.myth_en: Redness and swelling around a new cut mean something has gone wrong.
myths.myth_zh: 新的傷口周圍又紅又腫，表示出問題了。
myths.fact_en: For the first few days, a little redness and swelling is the cleanup crew at work. Tell an adult if it gets worse instead of better.
myths.fact_zh: 頭幾天有一點紅腫，是清潔隊正在工作。如果越來越嚴重、沒有好轉，才要告訴大人。

myths.myth_en: Fingernails keep growing after a person dies.
myths.myth_zh: 人死了以後，指甲還會繼續長。
myths.fact_en: They do not. The skin dries and pulls back, so the nails only look longer.
myths.fact_zh: 不會。那是皮膚變乾、往後縮，指甲才看起來變長了。

tricks.body_en: The same four steps for a scraped knee and for a broken arm.
tricks.body_zh: 擦傷的膝蓋和斷掉的手臂，都是同樣的四個步驟。

tricks.body_en: The patch is quick and weak. The rebuilding is slow and strong.
tricks.body_zh: 補丁做得快，但不結實；重建很慢，卻很堅固。

tricks.body_en: Your body made it. Leave it alone until it falls off.
tricks.body_zh: 那是身體自己做的。在它自己掉下來之前，不要去動它。

tricks.body_en: A bruise changes color as the old blood is cleared away.
tricks.body_zh: 舊的血被清走的過程中，瘀青會一路變色。

materials.en: A banana for each pair, and a table knife for the teacher
materials.zh: 每兩人一根香蕉，以及老師用的餐刀

materials.en: Paper tape, a marker, and a place to leave the bananas for three days
materials.zh: 紙膠帶、一枝麥克筆，以及可以把香蕉放三天的地方

steps.en: The teacher makes two small cuts in the peel of each banana, about three centimeters long.
steps.zh: 老師在每根香蕉的皮上劃兩道小切口，大約三公分長。

steps.en: Close one cut neatly with paper tape, so that the edges touch. Leave the other one open.
steps.zh: 用紙膠帶把其中一道切口整齊地貼合，讓兩邊碰在一起；另一道不要處理。

steps.en: Label the two cuts. Look at them every day for three days, and draw what you see.
steps.zh: 幫兩道切口做記號，連續三天每天觀察，把看到的畫下來。

steps.en: Which cut changed more? Why do doctors close a deep cut?
steps.zh: 哪一道變化比較大？醫生為什麼要把很深的傷口縫起來？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: a banana peel cannot heal, so this is not a model of healing. It is a model of why the edges of a wound are brought together and covered: the open cut dries out, browns, and gapes. Be clear with students about what the model shows and what it does not.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：香蕉皮不會癒合，所以這並不是「癒合」的模型，而是在示範為什麼要把傷口的邊緣拉攏、蓋好：沒有處理的切口會乾掉、變褐、裂得更開。請清楚告訴學生這個模型說明了什麼、沒有說明什麼。

materials.en: A large outline of a body on paper
materials.zh: 一張大大的人體輪廓圖

materials.en: Small stickers in two colors
materials.zh: 兩種顏色的小貼紙

steps.en: Think of one scrape, cut, or bruise you remember. Put a sticker of the first color on that place on the outline.
steps.zh: 想一個你記得的擦傷、割傷或瘀青，在輪廓圖上的那個位置貼一張第一種顏色的貼紙。

steps.en: If you have ever broken a bone, add a sticker of the second color. Use the bone names from Lesson 1.
steps.zh: 如果你骨折過，就再貼一張第二種顏色的貼紙。用第一課學過的骨頭名稱說出是哪一根。

steps.en: Look at the whole map. Where are most of the stickers?
steps.zh: 看看整張地圖：貼紙大多集中在哪裡？

steps.en: Why those places? What could protect them?
steps.zh: 為什麼是那些地方？有什麼東西可以保護它們？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: knees, elbows, and hands usually win, which leads naturally to helmets, knee pads, and looking where you are going. Sharing is optional: some children have injuries they do not want to talk about, so let students place stickers without explaining them.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：膝蓋、手肘和手通常貼得最多，可以很自然地帶到安全帽、護膝，以及走路要看路。分享不是必要的：有些孩子的傷不想被問起，請讓學生貼了貼紙就好，不必說明。

culture.body_en: A Chinese saying goes 傷筋動骨一百天 (shāng jīn dòng gǔ yì bǎi tiān): “hurt a tendon or a bone, and it takes a hundred days.” That is about three months. Long before X-rays, people had noticed how slow bone is: the patching stage alone takes weeks, and the rebuilding takes far longer. In Taiwanese, a bruise is 烏青 (o͘-chheⁿ), “black and green,” which names two of its colors. English says “black and blue.” Both languages noticed that a bruise is a little rainbow of repair.
culture.body_zh: 中文有句俗話：「傷筋動骨一百天。」一百天大約是三個月。早在有 X 光之前，人們就注意到骨頭好得有多慢：光是「搭補丁」就要好幾個星期，重建還要久得多。台語把瘀青叫做「烏青」，正好說出它的兩種顏色；英文則說 black and blue（又黑又藍）。兩種語言都發現了：瘀青是一道小小的、修補中的彩虹。
culture.link_en: More Chinese health words in English
culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Tell an adult about any cut that is deep, will not stop bleeding, or gets more red, swollen, or painful after a couple of days. If you think a bone may be broken, keep it still and see a doctor. Never test how a wound heals on purpose.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果傷口很深、血止不住，或是過了兩三天反而更紅、更腫、更痛，請告訴大人。如果覺得骨頭可能斷了，請保持不動並且去看醫生。絕對不要為了觀察癒合而故意弄傷自己。

lessons.title: What Happens When You Exercise?
lessons.title_zh: 運動的時候，身體發生什麼事？
lessons.blurb_en: When you run, your heart, lungs, and muscles all speed up together. Set the pace for a 3D runner, watch the heartbeat and breathing follow, and then take your own pulse before and after.
lessons.blurb_zh: 跑步的時候，心臟、肺和肌肉一起加速。在 3D 裡幫跑者調速度，看心跳和呼吸怎麼跟上來，再量量自己運動前後的脈搏。
lessons.big_idea_en: Working muscles need more oxygen, so your breathing and your heartbeat speed up to deliver it. With practice, the whole system gets better at the job.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 肌肉工作時需要更多氧氣，所以呼吸和心跳都加快來送貨；常常練習，整套系統就越做越好。

lab.how_en: The runner is a real skeleton with a heart, two lungs, and leg muscles drawn in. Choose a pace: rest, walk, jog, or sprint. The legs change at once, but watch the two numbers in the panel. The heartbeat and the breathing need a little time to catch up, and when the runner stops, they stay high for a while before they settle. The moving line draws that story for you.
lab.how_zh: 這位跑者是一副真實的骨架，加上自繪的心臟、兩片肺和腿部肌肉。選一個速度：休息、走路、慢跑或衝刺。腿的動作馬上就變了，但請看面板上的兩個數字：心跳和呼吸要花一點時間才跟得上；跑者停下來之後，它們還會高一陣子才慢慢降下來。那條會動的線，把這段過程畫給你看。

legend.en: Red: the heart, beating at the rate shown
legend.zh: 紅色：心臟，照顯示的速度跳動

legend.en: Pink: the lungs, breathing at the rate shown
legend.zh: 粉紅色：肺，照顯示的速度呼吸

legend.en: Leg muscles: brighter when they need more oxygen
legend.zh: 腿部肌肉：越亮表示需要越多氧氣

legend.en: Red dots: blood carrying oxygen to the legs
legend.zh: 紅點：把氧氣送到腿部的血液

lab.scale_en: The skeleton is a real one from BodyParts3D; the heart, lungs, muscles, and blood are our own drawing, and the running motion is a simple sketch. The numbers are for one example child of about ten: real heart rates differ a lot from person to person, so this model cannot tell you whether your own pulse is normal. The body really does take time to speed up and to recover; here that time is shortened so that you can watch it.
lab.scale_zh: 骨架是 BodyParts3D 的真實骨架；心臟、肺、肌肉和血液是本站自繪的示意圖，跑步的動作也只是簡單的示意。數字是以一個大約十歲的孩子舉例：每個人的心跳差很多，所以這個模型沒辦法告訴你自己的脈搏正不正常。身體加速和恢復確實都需要時間；這裡把時間縮短了，讓你看得到。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and added joints so that the skeleton can run; the heart, lungs, muscles, and blood are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並加上關節讓骨架能跑，心臟、肺、肌肉與血液為本站自繪示意。

paces.text_en: At rest. The muscles need little oxygen, so the heart and lungs take it easy.
paces.text_zh: 休息中。肌肉需要的氧氣很少，心臟和肺都很輕鬆。

paces.text_en: Walking. The leg muscles ask for more oxygen, and the heartbeat and breathing rise a little. You can still talk easily.
paces.text_zh: 走路。腿部肌肉要更多氧氣，心跳和呼吸稍微上升。你還能輕鬆地說話。

paces.text_en: Jogging. The heart beats faster and harder, breathing is deeper, and the body starts to sweat to stay cool. You can talk, but only in short sentences.
paces.text_zh: 慢跑。心臟跳得更快、更用力，呼吸變深，身體開始流汗來降溫。你還能說話，但只說得出短短的句子。

paces.text_en: Sprinting. The muscles are using oxygen faster than the blood can bring it. Nobody can keep this up for long, and it is very hard to speak.
paces.text_zh: 衝刺。肌肉用掉氧氣的速度，比血液送來的還快。沒有人能維持很久，而且幾乎說不出話。

lab.recover_en: Stopped, but still breathing hard. The body is paying back the oxygen it borrowed. How fast these numbers fall is a sign of fitness.
lab.recover_zh: 停下來了，卻還在喘。身體正在把剛才借用的氧氣補回來。這兩個數字降得多快，是體能好不好的一個指標。

paras: Run across the playground as fast as you can, and then stop. Your heart is pounding, you are breathing hard, and your face is hot. Nothing is wrong. Your body has just done something clever: several of its systems have sped up together to help your muscles.

It starts in the muscles. A working muscle uses energy many times faster than a resting one, and to get that energy it needs oxygen and fuel. Both arrive in the blood. So when your leg muscles start to work hard, they send out a call for more blood.

Your lungs and your heart answer the call. You breathe faster and deeper, so more oxygen enters your blood. Your heart beats faster, and each beat pushes out more blood. At rest, the heart of a child about ten years old beats about 60 to 100 times a minute. In a hard run it can beat much faster than that. At the same time, your blood vessels send more of the blood to the muscles that are working and less to places that can wait, such as your stomach.

All that work makes heat. To keep from getting too hot, your body sends warm blood to the skin, which is why your face turns red, and it makes sweat. As you learned in the lesson about skin, sweat cools you when it dries. That is also why you need to drink water when you exercise.

When you stop, your heartbeat and breathing do not drop at once. For a few minutes your body keeps working to pay back the oxygen it borrowed and to cool down. The better your fitness, the faster you recover. And fitness can be trained. If you are active often, your heart muscle grows stronger and pushes out more blood with every beat, so it does not have to beat as often. Some top long-distance athletes have a resting heart rate below 50.

How much is enough? The World Health Organization says that children and teenagers should be active for an average of at least 60 minutes a day, hard enough to make them breathe faster. It does not have to be a sport: fast walking, dancing, cycling, and playing tag all count. In Taiwan, schools also plan at least 150 minutes of activity a week outside of PE class. Now find out what your own heart does: use the pulse card below the model.
paras_zh: 用最快的速度跑過操場，然後停下來。你的心臟怦怦跳，你喘得很厲害，臉也熱熱的。這不是出了什麼問題——你的身體剛剛做了一件很聰明的事：好幾個系統一起加速，來幫助你的肌肉。
一切從肌肉開始。正在工作的肌肉，使用能量的速度是休息時的好多倍；為了得到這些能量，它需要氧氣和燃料，而這兩樣都是血液送來的。所以當你的腿部肌肉開始用力，它們就會發出訊號：我們需要更多的血！
肺和心臟回應了這個訊號。你呼吸得更快、更深，讓更多氧氣進入血液；你的心臟跳得更快，而且每一下都打出更多的血。休息的時候，大約十歲孩子的心臟每分鐘大約跳 60 到 100 下；用力跑的時候，可以比這快得多。同時，血管把更多的血送到正在工作的肌肉，把比較少的血送到可以等一等的地方，例如你的胃。
這麼多的工作會產生熱。為了不要太熱，身體把溫熱的血送到皮膚——所以你的臉會變紅——並且製造汗水。就像你在皮膚那一課學到的，汗水蒸發的時候會幫你降溫。這也是為什麼運動的時候要喝水。
你停下來的時候，心跳和呼吸並不會馬上降下來。有幾分鐘的時間，身體還在繼續工作，把剛才借用的氧氣補回來，也讓自己涼下來。體能越好，恢復得越快。而體能是可以鍛鍊的：如果你常常活動，心臟的肌肉會變得更強壯，每一下打出更多的血，所以不必跳得那麼頻繁。有些頂尖的長跑選手，休息時的心跳每分鐘不到 50 下。
要動多少才夠？世界衛生組織說，兒童和青少年平均每天至少要活動 60 分鐘，而且要激烈到會讓呼吸變快。不一定要是某種運動：快走、跳舞、騎腳踏車、玩鬼抓人都算。在台灣，學校也會在體育課之外，安排每週至少 150 分鐘的活動時間。現在來看看你自己的心臟會怎麼做：用模型下方的脈搏卡。
questions: Why do your muscles need more blood when you exercise?
What do your lungs and your heart do to help?
What happens to your heart if you are active often?
answers: Because working muscles use energy much faster, and the oxygen and fuel they need arrive in the blood.
You breathe faster and deeper, so more oxygen enters the blood. The heart beats faster, and each beat pushes out more blood.
The heart muscle grows stronger and pushes out more blood with every beat, so it does not have to beat as often.

vocab.ex: Exercise makes your heart stronger.
vocab.exzh: 運動讓你的心臟更強壯。

vocab.ex: I can feel my pulse on my wrist.
vocab.exzh: 我在手腕上摸得到脈搏。

vocab.ex: Breathe in slowly through your nose.
vocab.exzh: 用鼻子慢慢吸氣。

vocab.ex: Sweat was running down my face.
vocab.exzh: 汗水從我臉上流下來。

vocab.ex: My leg muscles are tired after the race.
vocab.exzh: 賽跑之後，我腿上的肌肉很累。

vocab.ex: Your blood carries oxygen to every part of your body.
vocab.exzh: 血液把氧氣送到身體的每一個地方。

vocab.ex: It took me two minutes to recover after the run.
vocab.exzh: 跑完之後，我花了兩分鐘才恢復。

vocab.ex: Try to be active for an hour every day.
vocab.exzh: 試著每天活動一個小時。

quiz.q: What do working muscles need more of?
How does oxygen get to your leg muscles?
options: Through the skin of your legs

quiz.q: Why does your face turn red when you run?
options: Warm blood is sent to the skin to cool you
Your face muscles are working hardest

quiz.q: What happens to your heartbeat right after you stop running?
options: It stays fast for a while and then slows down
It drops to normal at once

quiz.q: According to the reading, how much activity should children get?
options: At least 60 minutes a day on average

kinds_head.eyebrow: The Exercise Team · 運動小隊

kinds.where_en: All over your body, most of all in your legs when you run
kinds.where_zh: 全身都有；跑步時最忙的在腿上
kinds.text_en: They use oxygen and fuel to pull on your bones, and they make heat while they do it.
kinds.text_zh: 它們用氧氣和燃料來拉動骨頭，同時也產生熱。

kinds.where_en: In your chest
kinds.text_en: They breathe faster and deeper, and they also get rid of the extra carbon dioxide your muscles make.
kinds.text_zh: 它們呼吸得更快、更深，也把肌肉製造的多餘二氧化碳排出去。

kinds.where_en: In your chest, between your lungs
kinds.text_en: It beats faster, and each beat pushes out more blood.
kinds.text_zh: 它跳得更快，而且每一下打出更多的血。

kinds.where_en: Everywhere
kinds.control_en: Send blood where it is needed
kinds.text_en: They open wider in working muscles and in the skin, and narrow in places that can wait.
kinds.text_zh: 在工作的肌肉和皮膚裡，它們會張開；在可以等一等的地方，它們會變窄。

kinds.where_en: In your skin
kinds.text_en: Sweat carries heat away when it dries, so you need to drink water to replace it.
kinds.text_zh: 汗水蒸發時把熱帶走，所以你要喝水把它補回來。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a restaurant at lunchtime: when the orders pour in, the kitchen cooks faster, the waiters walk faster, and the fans are turned up. No one part can speed up alone.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成午餐時間的餐廳：訂單一多，廚房煮得更快，服務生走得更快，電風扇也開大。沒有哪一個部分能自己單獨加速。

measure.title_en: Before, after, and two minutes later
measure.title_zh: 運動前、運動後、兩分鐘後
measure.lead_en: Take your pulse three times and use the pulse card below the model. You learned how to find your pulse in the lesson about blood: two fingers on the thumb side of your wrist.
measure.lead_zh: 量三次脈搏，並使用模型下方的脈搏卡。你在血液那一課學過怎麼找脈搏：兩根手指放在手腕靠大拇指的那一側。

steps.en: At rest
steps.zh: 休息時
steps.text_en: Sit quietly for two minutes. Start the 15-second timer, count the beats, and enter the number.
steps.text_zh: 安靜地坐兩分鐘。按下 15 秒計時，數一數脈搏跳了幾下，把數字輸入進去。

steps.en: Right after exercise
steps.zh: 剛運動完
steps.text_en: Do jumping jacks for one minute. As soon as you stop, find your pulse and count for 15 seconds again.
steps.text_zh: 做開合跳一分鐘。一停下來就馬上找到脈搏，再數 15 秒。

steps.en: Two minutes later
steps.zh: 兩分鐘後
steps.text_en: Sit down and rest for two minutes, and then count once more. The card shows how much of the rise is already gone.
steps.text_zh: 坐下來休息兩分鐘，然後再數一次。卡片會算出上升的部分已經降回了多少。

myths.myth_en: Sore muscles the next day are caused by lactic acid.
myths.myth_zh: 隔天肌肉痠痛，是乳酸堆積造成的。
myths.fact_en: Lactic acid is gone within about an hour. The soreness a day or two later comes from tiny damage in the muscle fibers, which the body then repairs.
myths.fact_zh: 乳酸大約一小時內就消失了。隔一兩天才出現的痠痛，是肌肉纖維裡的微小損傷造成的，身體接著會把它修補好。

myths.myth_en: A slow resting heartbeat means a weak heart.
myths.myth_zh: 休息時心跳慢，表示心臟比較弱。
myths.fact_en: A well-trained heart pushes out more blood with each beat, so it can beat less often. Top endurance athletes often have very slow resting heart rates.
myths.fact_zh: 鍛鍊過的心臟每一下打出更多的血，所以可以跳得比較少下。頂尖的耐力型運動員，休息時的心跳常常非常慢。

myths.myth_en: Only sports count as exercise.
myths.myth_zh: 只有正式的運動項目才算運動。
myths.fact_en: Anything that makes you breathe faster counts: fast walking, dancing, cycling, climbing stairs, or playing tag.
myths.fact_zh: 只要會讓你呼吸變快的都算：快走、跳舞、騎腳踏車、爬樓梯，或是玩鬼抓人。

myths.myth_en: You should not drink water while you exercise.
myths.myth_zh: 運動的時候不可以喝水。
myths.fact_en: You lose water as sweat, and your body needs it back. Small sips during and after exercise are a good idea.
myths.fact_zh: 你會隨著汗水流失水分，而身體需要把它補回來。運動中和運動後小口小口地喝水是好習慣。

tricks.title_en: Muscles ask, heart and lungs answer
tricks.body_en: Muscles need oxygen. Lungs bring it in, and the heart delivers it.
tricks.body_zh: 肌肉需要氧氣；肺把它帶進來，心臟把它送過去。

tricks.title_en: Red face, wet skin, cool body
tricks.body_en: Warm blood goes to the skin, and sweat carries the heat away.
tricks.body_zh: 溫熱的血流到皮膚，汗水把熱帶走。

tricks.body_en: A pulse that comes back down quickly is one sign of a fit body.
tricks.body_zh: 脈搏很快降回來，是體能好的一個跡象。

tricks.body_en: At least 60 minutes of activity a day, hard enough to make you breathe faster.
tricks.body_zh: 每天至少活動 60 分鐘，而且要激烈到讓你呼吸變快。

materials.en: A clock or timer that everyone can see
materials.zh: 一個全班都看得到的時鐘或計時器

materials.en: Graph paper, or a large chart on the board
materials.zh: 方格紙，或是黑板上的一大張圖表

steps.en: Everyone counts their resting pulse for 15 seconds and multiplies by 4.
steps.zh: 每個人數休息時的脈搏 15 秒，再乘以 4。

steps.en: Do jumping jacks together for one minute, and count again right away.
steps.zh: 全班一起做開合跳一分鐘，馬上再數一次。

steps.en: Rest for two minutes, and count a third time.
steps.zh: 休息兩分鐘，數第三次。

steps.en: Draw your three numbers as a line graph. What shape does almost everyone's line have?
steps.zh: 把你的三個數字畫成折線圖。幾乎每個人的線，都是什麼形狀？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: do not compare students' numbers. Resting pulses differ a lot among healthy children, and a higher or lower number does not mean better or worse. Compare the shape instead: up fast, down more slowly. Students who should not do jumping jacks can be the timekeepers, and their flat line is a useful comparison.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：請不要比較學生之間的數字。健康孩子休息時的脈搏本來就差很多，數字高一點或低一點並不代表比較好或比較差。要比的是形狀：上去得快，下來得慢。不適合做開合跳的學生可以負責計時，他們那條平平的線正好是很好的對照。

materials.en: A safe place to walk and jog, such as the playground
materials.zh: 一個可以安全走路和慢跑的地方，例如操場

materials.en: A short sentence that everyone knows, such as a line from a song
materials.zh: 一句大家都會的短句子，例如一句歌詞

steps.en: Walk slowly and say the sentence out loud. Was it easy?
steps.zh: 慢慢走，把句子大聲說出來。容易嗎？

steps.en: Walk fast, and say it again.
steps.zh: 快走，再說一次。

steps.en: Jog, and say it again. Then run fast for ten seconds and try once more.
steps.zh: 慢跑，再說一次。然後快跑十秒鐘，再試一次。

steps.en: At which speed did you have to stop for a breath in the middle?
steps.zh: 在哪一種速度，你說到一半就得停下來換氣？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: speaking uses the same air as breathing, so the talk test is a simple way to feel how hard the body is working without any equipment. “Can talk but not sing” is a common everyday description of moderate activity. Link it to the lesson on voice: no air, no voice.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：說話和呼吸用的是同一口氣，所以不需要任何器材，說話測試就能讓學生感覺到身體有多用力。「還能說話，但沒辦法唱歌」是日常生活中常用來形容中等強度活動的說法。可以連回聲音那一課：沒有空氣，就沒有聲音。

culture.body_en: When you have run too hard, Chinese says 上氣不接下氣 (shàng qì bù jiē xià qì): “the breath above cannot catch the breath below.” English says you are “out of breath.” To loosen up, people say 活動筋骨 (huódòng jīngǔ), “get the tendons and bones moving,” which names the same parts you met in the lessons on muscles and hands. Taiwan's schools have their own number for moving: SH150, which stands for Sports and Health, 150 minutes of activity a week outside of PE class. The name is new, but the idea is very old: a body that moves stays strong.
culture.body_zh: 跑得太用力的時候，中文說「上氣不接下氣」；英文則說 out of breath（沒氣了）。想舒展一下身體，我們說「活動筋骨」——筋和骨，正好是肌肉和手那幾課認識的東西。台灣的學校有一個屬於自己的數字：SH150，S 是 Sports（運動）、H 是 Health（健康），意思是體育課之外，每週在校活動 150 分鐘。名字是新的，道理卻很老：常常動的身體才會強壯。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Everyone's heart rate is different, and the numbers in this lesson are only examples. Stop and tell an adult if you feel dizzy, have pain in your chest, or cannot catch your breath. If a doctor has told you to limit exercise, follow the doctor's advice.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。每個人的心跳都不一樣，這一課裡的數字只是舉例。如果覺得頭暈、胸口痛，或是一直喘不過氣，請停下來並且告訴大人。如果醫生說過你要限制運動，請照醫生的話做。
